title: Mustache Madness fundraiser at Mavericks set for Oct. 17
author: Dave
description: Mavericks Beach Club in Pacific Beach is holding the Ninth Annual San Diego Fire Department Mustache Madness fundraiser on Thursday, Oct. 17. This fun event for the follically inclin
content:
Mavericks Beach Club in Pacific Beach is holding the Ninth Annual San Diego Fire Department Mustache Madness fundraiser on Thursday, Oct. 17.
This fun event for the follically inclined, which pays homage to local surf culture while striving to aid firefighters, is being held from 5-11 p.m. at 860 Garnet Ave.
Festivities include a live music performance by Hairforce, a premier hair metal tribute show featuring music from iconic bands Motley Crue, Guns N Roses, Queen, AC/DC, Def Leppard, Journey, Poison, Van Halen, Bon Jovi, and Kiss.
There will also be mustache competitions, raffles, a one-of-a-kind silent auction, drink specials, and more. The cost is $20 for general admission and 100% of ticket proceeds benefit Firefighter Aid. Tickets are available on Mavericks' website, maverickssd.com.
'Firefighter Aid is a San Diego County non-profit that provides charitable assistance to firefighters in crisis and promotes awareness of firefighter health and safety issues,' said Sara Berns, executive director for the San Diego Fire Relief Association and Firefighter Aid. 'Occupational cancer for firefighters is so prevalent that in 2022 the IARC (International Agency for Research for Cancer) listed 'firefighting' as a group 1 carcinogen. Seventy-two percent of Firefighter deaths in 2023 were from occupational cancer.'
Berns noted Mustache Madness proceeds will go to support the Cancer Awareness Prevention Program (CAPP) and other cancer response efforts. She added, 'Firefighter Aid is so grateful to the founders of Mustache Madness and Maverick's Beach Club for supporting our firefighter community.'
Krista Marcheschi, Mavericks' events and marketing director at The Verant Group, talked about what men – and women – can expect from the lighthearted event fundraiser.
'The event started at the Firehouse (722 Grand Ave.) and was created by firefighter Sean Brambir with SDFD Station 21 to raise awareness and money for the Firefighter Aid Foundation to help firefighting men and women with medical bills, hotel stays, etc.,' Marcheschi said adding, 'It's a great cause.'
'When I was a newer firefighter one of my academy mates was diagnosed with cancer,' said Brambir. 'I wanted to show all of our support for him and his battle so I started SD Mustache Madness. This has created awareness for FirefighterAid CAPP. We have raised over $100,000 over the years. It started out going to the UCSD Foundation for cancer research, but now funds go to Firefighter Aid. Unfortunately, cancer is still an issue amongst us firefighters new and old.'
Marcheschi said Mustache Madness, paused during the pandemic, quickly outgrew its original venue, which was when it was moved to more spacious Mavericks, where it has prospered. 'In the last three years, the event has raised over $80,000, last year making about $60,000 from ticket sales, raffle donations, merchandise, and silent auction prizes,' she said adding, in years past, the event has drawn from 400 to nearly 1,800 participants.
Marcheschi noted the event will include live entertainment including roving magicians. There will also be multiple mustache competitions including 'Best In Grow,' 'Best She Stash,' 'Biggest Stash,' 'Most Classy Stash' and the 'Ron Burgundy Award.'
'It comes during a time when wildfires are at an all-time high and you're seeing many people displaced, while firefighters are putting their lives at stake with smoke inhalation, etc.,' noted Marcheschi adding, 'Firefighter Aid is there to help them. And we're (Mavericks) there in turn to help firefighters and their families.'
MUSTACHE MADNESS
When: 5-11 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 17.
Where: Mavericks Beach Club, 860 Garnet Ave.
Info: maverickssd.com. Tags: Mavericks Beach ClubMustache Madness

title: Top 9 Furnace Maintenance Tips from Industry Professionals
author: Grhics Tech
description: Ensuring that a home's heating system works efficiently and safely requires proper maintenance of the furnace, which is crucial for both longevity and energy efficiency. This can lead to reduced…
content:
Ensuring that a home's heating system works efficiently and safely requires proper maintenance of the furnace, which is crucial for both longevity and energy efficiency. This can lead to reduced utility bills in the long run! In this article, we delve into nine expert-recommended tips for maintaining furnaces to help homeowners effectively care for their systems and keep them running smoothly. 1. Regular Filter Replacement
Changing furnace filters regularly is essential. Dirty filters impede airflow, causing the system to work harder and consume more energy. Industry experts recommend replacing filters every one to three months, depending on usage and filter type. Clean filters improve air quality and prevent dust buildup, contributing to more efficient furnace operation and requiring less furnace maintenance in Cincinnati or any other city. 2. Inspect and Clean Ductwork
The duct system is crucial for distributing warmth throughout the house. Over time, it can become clogged with dust and mold, which hampers airflow and heating effectiveness. Experts recommend checking and cleaning ductwork regularly, as well as sealing any leaks to maintain optimal heating performance. 3. Check Thermostat Settings
A well-functioning thermostat optimizes furnace performance. It's essential to check thermostat settings regularly to ensure they are accurate and appropriate for the season. Programmable thermostats can be especially beneficial, allowing homeowners to set temperature schedules that match their daily routines. This not only enhances comfort but also saves energy. 4. Clean Burners and Flame Sensor
Burners and flame sensors play a crucial role in furnace operation. With use, dust and debris can accumulate, obstructing burners and impacting the furnace's heat production efficiency. Likewise, a dirty flame sensor can trigger system shutdowns. Regular home maintenance , including cleaning these components, is key to ensuring the reliable performance of the heating system. 5. Lubricate Moving Parts
The furnace has components that need lubrication to keep them running smoothly and to prevent wear and tear over time. Components such as the blower motor and fan may deteriorate more quickly if not adequately cared for. Regularly lubricating these parts helps reduce friction and prolong the lifespan of the furnace while maintaining functionality. 6. Inspect the Heat Exchanger
The heat exchanger plays a vital role in the furnace by transferring heat to the air safely without leaks that could lead to carbon monoxide issues. Experts recommend regular checks on the heat exchanger for wear and tear to maintain both furnace safety and performance. Timely replacement of a damaged heat exchanger is essential for ensuring the furnace operates safely. 7. Ensure Proper Ventilation
Proper ventilation is crucial for both safety and efficiency in home furnaces. Blocked vents can lead to the accumulation of hazardous gases indoors, so it's important for homeowners to routinely inspect and ensure that all vents and flues are free from blockages. Maintaining proper ventilation not only safeguards occupants from harmful gases but also helps the furnace function more efficiently. 8. Test the Ignition System
A furnace's ignition system is crucial for starting the unit. Issues with the ignition system can prevent the furnace from running altogether. Testing the ignition system periodically ensures it functions correctly. If the furnace uses a pilot light, ensure it remains lit and burns with a steady blue flame. For electronic ignitions, follow the manufacturer's guidelines for testing and maintenance. 9. Schedule Professional Inspections
While homeowners can perform many maintenance tasks, scheduling annual professional inspections is highly recommended. Certified technicians possess the expertise to identify potential issues before they become major problems. A comprehensive inspection includes checking all components, cleaning necessary parts, and ensuring the system operates safely and efficiently. Summary
Incorporating these nine furnace maintenance tips into a regular routine ensures the heating system runs efficiently and safely. Regular filter replacement, ductwork inspection, and checking thermostat settings are simple yet effective tasks. Cleaning burners, lubricating moving parts, and inspecting the heat exchanger require a bit more effort but are equally important. Ensuring proper ventilation, testing the ignition system, and scheduling professional inspections round out a comprehensive maintenance plan. By following these expert tips, homeowners can enjoy a warm, comfortable home while maximizing their furnace's efficiency and longevity.

title: Fall in love with upcoming events in East Village
description: In the blink of an eye, we've already reached the beginni
content:
In the blink of an eye, we've already reached the beginning of fall! There is no shortage of fun-filled activities in the East Village community as the year approaches its end. From Bavarian celebrations to top-notch jazz performances and festive holiday markets, explore all of the happenings this energetic neighborhood has to offer. Oktoberfest
It's time to dust off the lederhosen and dirndl for this year's East Village Oktoberfest! Taking place Oct. 5 from 12 to 6 p.m. within Quartyard and Market Street, between 13th and 14th Street, this 21+ event sets itself apart from the usual Oktoberfest. Shining light on the historic German influence on Mexican culture, it makes it a celebration as distinctive as the East Village itself. In true Bavarian style, communal tables will provide generous space for both new and old friends to gather, savoring the delightful cuisine and vibrant atmosphere. Attendees can explore a vast selection of lagers and pilsners from eight local San Diego craft breweries, enjoy German and Mexican cuisine, and experience a world of entertainment.
Hosted by San Diego favorite, SDHosted, this celebration presents the opportunity to join in on fun games, show off your dance moves to lively performances of Polka melodies with a Latin flair, and check out some cool rides at the classic car show! Get your steins ready and round up your friends for this truly unforgettable Oktoberfest experience. Get groovy at the San Diego Tijuana International Jazz Festival
Prepare for a swinging good time! On Sunday, Oct. 6 from 5 to 9 p.m., Quartyard will host the final day of the inaugural San Diego International Jazz Festival. Celebrating the musical richness of the region, this binational event highlights jazz performers of all kinds in both San Diego and Tijuana. With performances from acclaimed artists like the Binational Youth Ensemble, Surf Fire Soul Ensemble and the Nortec Jazz Experience: Bostich + Fussible and Iván Trujillo Ensamble, this free event is set to bring even more vibrancy to the streets of East Village, honoring the world of jazz musical artistry.
Tribal Streetwear and SDFC Merch collaboration
Exciting news for local SDFC fans! East Village's Tribal Streetwear has teamed up with San Diego FC for an exclusive merch collaboration, blending the essence of Southern California lifestyle with vibrant streetwear. This first-of-its-kind partnership will offer limited edition gear, perfect for showing your pride for San Diego's newest soccer team. Looking Ahead: East Village Tree Lighting and Holiday Market
The East Village Association is excited to kick off the holiday season with the return of the Annual East Village Tree Lighting & Holiday Market on Saturday, Nov. 30, from 4 to 8 p.m. at Quartyard and 13th Street. This festive and family-friendly evening invites the community to enjoy live music, delectable bites and sips, and kid-friendly activities. With a holiday market curated by San Diego Markets, attendees can check off their holiday shopping lists with a delightful array of locally crafted gifts. At 6:45 p.m., join East Village and local officials for the traditional Christmas tree lighting ceremony, and don't forget to snap a picture with Santa as holiday cheer fills the air. Yule be sorry if you miss out on this magical evening!
Whether you're donning your lederhosen for Oktoberfest, soaking in the rich rhythms of the San Diego Tijuana International Jazz Festival, or basking in the holiday spirit at the East Village Tree Lighting and Holiday Market, there's something for everyone to enjoy. These events not only celebrate the diverse cultural tapestry of the East Village but also offer a unique opportunity to connect with friends, neighbors, and new faces. So mark your calendars and get ready to immerse yourself in the festive experiences that this dynamic neighborhood has to offer. Tags: east villageeventsjazz festivalOktoberfest

title: Little Italy's exciting end-of-year events
content:
If you're looking for a spot to have some fun as the year wraps up, Little Italy's got you covered! From the ghoulish celebrations of Halloween and dancing the night away to the sounds of America at the Fleet Week concert, to getting ready for the holiday season, there is no shortage of entertainment in this vibrant urban neighborhood. Trick-or-Treat on India Street: A hauntingly fun night for the family
Calling all families of goblins and monsters, it's time to put on your best costume and get ready for Trick-or-Treat on India Street! Taking place from on Oct. 27 from 3:30 to 7:30 p.m., the event will feature an array of local businesses and neighbors, inviting families of all ages to peruse down India Street and trick-or-treat as the spook-tacular sounds of Halloween music fill the air. The Piazza della Famiglia will be getting a visit from a giant 13-foot Jack Skellington and the Christmas Wreath Monster as it transforms into a Nightmare Before Christmas-themed experience. With pumpkins stacked sky high, fun photo opportunities at the Oogie Boogie backdrop, and locally conjured Halloween treats and goods, this event will highlight the community's small businesses as they show off their spooky spirit! Anchors away: Fleet Week Concert Series sets sail for a night of celebration
Join Little Italy for a special evening of music at the Fleet Week Concert Series! As part of the annual Fleet Week celebrations, this series will honor our military service members with a spectacular lineup of performances. The Navy Band Southwest Rock Band will take the stage on Sunday, Nov. 3 and the Marine Band San Diego Sound Strike on Monday, Nov 4. to perform stirring renditions of classic American tunes, patriotic anthems, and contemporary hits. Nov. 4 also marks Gunnery Sergeant John Basilone's birthday, a United States Marine who received the Medal of Honor for his actions at the Battle of Guadalcanal during World War II. He was the only enlisted Marine in World War II to receive both the Medal of Honor and the Navy Cross. This family-friendly event is a perfect way to show support for our armed forces and honor a remarkable figure while enjoying an unforgettable night of live music. Don't miss out on this tribute to those who serve! Looking ahead: Small business season, unique tours, and holiday celebrations
The holiday shopping season is just around the corner, and what better way to find unique gifts than by exploring the local shops of Little Italy! Small business season is the perfect time to get carefully curated and crafted presents for friends and family. Little Italy is your go-to area to get fresh ingredients for your holiday meals, find thoughtful trinkets to give, shop for new styles for winter, and more. For a quick dive into all of the special local spots this neighborhood has to offer, get an official tour with So Diego Tours! Starting Oct. 1, in partnership with the Little Italy Association, visitors and locals alike can explore all the community has to offer with guided wine, food, and beer tours. Not what you're looking for? There will be customizable tours available for those looking to explore a particular aspect of the neighborhood. To book a tour and learn about all of Little Italy's local gems, visit the Little Italy website.
On Dec. 7 from 4 to 8 p.m., prepare to walk through a winter wonderland at the beloved Little Italy Tree Lighting & Christmas Village! Adorned with twinkling lights, 10-foot-tall nutcrackers, and kinetic tree holiday displays, the streets of the neighborhood will bring holiday cheer for all. The tree lighting will be double the fun with both a permanent 25-foot tree and Joshua Hubert's magical Aurora tree. Patrons can enjoy live music and entertainment, get unique stocking stuffers with a range of seasonal vendors, experience a traditional Italian tree lighting ceremony, and most importantly, meet Santa to make sure all of their holiday wishes come true! title: Who's at your door? A warning about contracting scams that are hitting home!
content:
It starts with a random knock at the door.
The person appears to be a contractor who might say they just repaired a home down the street.
They say they have extra material on their trucks, they offer you a great price.
But, you have to do it now and they only take cash through a payment app.
The pressure is on. What would you do?
They're called 'chasers' and seek out homes damaged by storms or fire.
So far, this has been a bad year for both.
Cal Fire reports as of September, nearly 1 million acres have burned this year across the state.
That's three times the acres burned in 2023 and already ahead of the five year average.
While California requires licenses for people doing contracting work worth more than $500, it's usually unlicensed people appearing at doors after fires or storms.
They can end up causing more damage or just take your money and do nothing.
Last year, the Contractor State License Board (CSLB) warned hiring someone without a license could 'make these vulnerable home and business owners a victim a second time.'
https:/cslb.ca.gov/Media_Room/Disaster_Help_Center/October_17.aspx
Beware of tempting repair deals
While the repair deal is tempting, beware.
Unlicensed people may not have the bonds, insurance or skills required for those who are licensed.
So you could be responsible for any injury on the job as well as shelling out more money to repair their bad work.
If your home suffered fire or storm damage, first check with your insurer.
Homeowner insurance policies cover wind, fire and other damage.
But water damage is usually only covered if the water comes from above, like rain causing roof damage.
You would need a flood policy if the water damage comes from below like from flooding or sewage backups.
Protect yourself when choosing a contractor:
-Check the CSLB website for licensing and complaints.
https:/cslb.ca.gov/
-Check contractor reviews, complaints and for Accredited Businesses with the Better Business Bureau. https:/bbb.org/
-Get three estimates
-Pay with a credit card so you can dispute the charge later.
-In California contractors cannot demand upfront money of more than $1000 or 10% of the total cost, whichever is less.
-and demand a signed contract with payment on progress and final payment when completed
Not all door knocks are scams.
But instead of hiring on the spot, take the information, check them out and only then, make your decision.
Report unlicensed contractors to the CSLB
https:/cslb.ca.gov/
See all the ways to protect yourself against scams and bad business practices at joeknowsbetter.com
https:/joeknowsbetter.com/
Report and check the latest scams through BBB Scam Tracker
https:/bbb.org/scamtracker/lookupscam.

title: Common Injuries After Motorcycle Accident in Fort Lauderdale, Florida
author: Grhics Tech
description: Understanding the medical and legal ramifications of motorcycle accident injuries in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, is crucial for those affected. For comprehensive legal support and to learn more about your rights, consulting with experienced Fort Lauderdale motorcycle accident attorneys https://schillingsilvers.com is advisable. In Florida, the rise in motorcycle-related incidents is a…
content:
Understanding the medical and legal ramifications of motorcycle accident injuries in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, is crucial for those affected. For comprehensive legal support and to learn more about your rights, consulting with experienced Fort Lauderdale motorcycle accident attorneys https://schillingsilvers.com is advisable.
In Florida, the rise in motorcycle-related incidents is a growing concern, with 9,448 motorcycle crashes reported in 2023, resulting in 592 fatalities. These accidents often lead to severe and sometimes life-altering injuries due to the exposed nature of motorcycles. Common injuries include road rash, fractures, traumatic brain injuries, and spinal cord injuries, each carrying potential long-term consequences.
This blog delves into the common injuries suffered by victims after motorcycle accidents, underscoring the significance of safety precautions. Head Injuries
Head injuries continue to be an issue in motorcycle crashes despite the use of helmets for protection. Some common types of injuries are concussions from sudden impacts causing headaches and confusion, skull fractures that can cause brain bleeding and swelling with severe consequences, and traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) that may result in lasting cognitive and emotional challenges. Spinal Cord Damage
Motorcycle accidents can be particularly harmful to the spinal cord, leading to repercussions such as partial or full paralysis. This may occur when the back or neck undergoes sudden and forceful movements, resulting in symptoms like numbness, tingling sensations, or even total loss of mobility. Seeking medical attention is crucial for reducing lasting harm and enhancing the chances of recovery. Broken Bones
Fractures are common in motorcycle accidents due to the collision force and limited protective measures. The affected bones are the arms, legs, and ribs. Riders frequently use their arms to cushion their falls, resulting in wrist and forearm fractures. Leg fractures often happen when pinned beneath the motorcycle, while rib fractures can occur from hits or pressure. It's crucial to seek attention for broken bones to support adequate recovery and avoid further issues. Road Rash
When you slide across the pavement and get road rash , it hurts a lot because your skin gets scraped off. Mild injuries may need a doctor's help to heal properly and prevent infections. Internal Injuries
Injuries inside the body after motorcycle crashes can be dangerous despite being harder to see, like bruises or cuts on the skin surface. When organs like the liver or spleen get hurt in an accident, internal bleeding may occur, causing symptoms like belly pain, feeling lightheaded, and passing out. Getting attention is vital because if these internal injuries are left untreated, they could turn life-threatening. Facial Injuries
Riders often suffer injuries after being ejected from their motorcycles. Jaw fractures and broken cheekbones and noses are common occurrences, along with dental damage like chipped or lost teeth as well. While wearing a full-face helmet can lower the chances of injuries occurring to some extent, it cannot eradicate the risk completely. Timely medical attention and dental treatment play a role in ensuring recovery and reducing any potential long-term harm. Soft Tissue Injuries
Soft tissue injuries impact muscles, ligaments, and tendons. Strains, sprains, and tears can occur from impacts or awkward landings. These injuries may not be immediately noticeable but can lead to discomfort and restricted movement. Initial treatment involves rest, ice, compression, and elevation, known as RICE, followed by therapy for the chance of recovery. Psychological Impact
The emotional toll of being in a motorcycle crash should never be downplayed. Those who make it through often struggle with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), feelings of anxiousness, and sadness. Recurring memories and dreams of the incident and overwhelming worry can disrupt daily activities. It's vital to seek assistance from health professionals to address these issues and enhance one's state of mind. Preventive Measures
The effective way to prevent injuries in motorcycle accidents is through measures like wearing the right protective gear, such as helmets and gloves, and following traffic laws to ensure rider safety is prioritized. End Note
Motorcycle crashes frequently lead to a range of injuries, including head injuries and fractures, as well as emotional impacts such as trauma and stress disorders. Recognizing these injuries underscores the significance of safety precautions and prompt medical attention. By focusing on measures and seeking treatment, bikers can savor their journeys while lessening the chances of severe damage.

title: October updates in Uptown
author: Uptown Downtown News
description: Max Benjamin Partners (MBP), a boutique real estate advisory firm that provides innovative capital solut
content:
Max Benjamin Partners (MBP), a boutique real estate advisory firm that provides innovative capital solutions to developers and investors, announced it secured a $16.5 million loan for the construction of 10th and Robinson, a 70-unit multifamily community located in Hillcrest. 10th and Robinson is nestled in a quiet residential area just minutes from retail and dining. Combined with its sister building, it will have abundant amenities including a pool, co-working space, gym, and high-end finishes. Museums, exhibits and Balboa Park Kids get in free at museums this month
The San Diego Museum Council has announced the return of the popular Kids Free San Diego program, now in its 13th year . From Oct. 1 to 31, children ages 12 and under can enjoy free admission to more than 50 museums, aquariums/zoos, gardens, state parks, historic sites and other family-friendly attractions throughout San Diego County. Sites include some of San Diego's most popular sites, including the USS Midway Museum, Fleet Science Center, Birch Aquarium and San Diego Air & Space Museum, as well as many hidden gems waiting to be discovered. Some locations are free for the entire family or offer pay-what-you-wish admission year-round. A full list of participating museums can be found on the San Diego Museum Council website . (Left to right) Interim ED Desha Crownover, board president Bill Schneiderwind, former ED Jimmy Saba (Photo by Josie Gonzales) Jimmy Saba exits Junior Theatre
After 11 years of service, James 'Jimmy' Saba departed as Executive Director from San Diego Junior Theatre. A committee of the Board of Trustees is enlisting former JT Artistic Director, Desha Crownover, as Interim Executive Director.
SDJT's 77th season gets underway this month with 'The Addams Family' (Oct. 25 – Nov. 10) followed by the world premiere production of 'Churlish Chiding of Winter Winds: A Shakespeariment' (Jan. 10-19, 2025), which will be devised by JT's students under the direction of David Goodwin. Tickets for these productions and the rest of the exciting season are on sale now at juniortheatre.com . South Park's Gold Leaf now at The Nat
In The Nat's atrium, visitors can now shop at South P a rk-based retailer Gold Leaf. They offer a curated selection of home goods, unique gifts, natural beauty products, nature-centric art, and sustainable products and toys for kids. Given their proximity to the Park, this new, second location inside The Nat felt like 'the right next step' to the owners. In addition, The Nat announced a new cafe partnership with The Craft Taco, based in Sorrento Valley. These local, independently owned and operated businesses align with The Nat's regional focus—to study and conserve nature in Southern California and the Baja California Peninsula—and its goals to feature artisan brands and sustainable products. 19th century sculpture exhibition at Timken
San Diego's Timken Museum of Art will present Modeling for the Masses: Sculptural Ideals in Nineteenth-Century America Oct. 23, 2024 through March 16, 2025. This new exhibition highlights the small-scale, three-dimensional works of acclaimed sculptors including celebrated works by Hiram Powers, Thomas Ball, Chauncey B. Ives and John Rogers.
Modeling for the Masses draws upon examples from the Timken's permanent collection as well as significant loans from prominent public and private collections. Period photographs will show how works were often broadly disseminated, and both stereoviews and 'cartes de visite' images represent another dimension of the exhibition. SDMA welcomes Foster + Partners exhibit Foster+Partners Great Court at British Museum Model
Showcasing groundbreaking architectural designs by Lord Norman Foster and his internationally renowned studio Foster + Partners, a new exhibition titled ' Foster + Partners: Architecture of Light and Space ' opens at The San Diego Museum of Art (SDMA) this fall. On view Oct. 19, 2024, through April 27, 2025, the exhibition invites visitors to explore the innovative architectural vision of Foster + Partners, one of the world's leading architectural firms, renowned for their pioneering approach to design and sustainability, through models, drawings, and an early concept design of the museum's west wing renovation.
Announced in 2023, SDMA has chosen Foster + Partners to renovate its west wing, with the goal of expanding exhibition space, including free galleries; enhancing public engagement; achieving greater efficiency and sustainability; supporting the Museum's permanent collection; and improving accessibility while honoring the Museum's and Balboa Park's architectural heritage. The renovation aims to include a new education pavilion and sculpture garden, as well as a free community gathering space with exhibitions, pop up concerts, and a café. In addition, the renovation will accommodate new storage vaults for the collection and enhanced sustainability technologies. A public survey is open now through Oct. 14, inviting the community to share about their current and desired SDMA experiences and renovation updates. For more details on the renovation project and to take the survey, visit sdmart.org/west-wing-building-renovation/ . ' The Myth of Superheroes' at Comic-Con Museum
At the crossroads between ancient cultures and modern-day superheroes stands Comic-Con Museum 's world-premiere exhibition, 'The Myth of Superheroes: From Antiquity to Contemporary Art,' exploring the connection between Greco-Roman mythology and today's superheroes. The exhibit showcases an extensive collection of more than 400 objects including original comic books from all over the world, hand drawings, modern statues, movie posters, action figures, album covers, and other vintage memorabilia. It is open now on the main floor, replacing Popnology.
Visitors will have the opportunity to journey through the ages and discover the evolution of some of today's fan favorite heroes: from Hercules to Superman, the Amazons to Wonder Woman, Neptune to Aquaman, and Mercury to Flash. Dear Bruce: A Story Told in Letters exhibit
This intimate exhibit at The Studio Door will showcase deeply personal correspondence, tracing the profound relationships between San Diego art historian Bruce Kamerling and two men, Robert Miles Parker and Paul Cadmus . On loan from Lambda Archives of San Diego, the letters, drawings, and newspaper clippings shared in this exhibit offer a rare glimpse into the emotional and artistic connections that flourished between Bruce Kamerling and the two men spanning over more than 15 years. The exhibit will also feature artworks on loan from the San Diego History Center as a supplement to the letters. The exhibit will be on view through Nov. 2. North Park photographer documents San Diego River 'Flooded Villages' by Louis Russell
The San Diego River Artists' Alliance (SDRAA) will exhibit work celebrating the San Diego River and its ecosystem in a show titled 'Ebb and Flow: Art Along the River' at the Point Loma Public Library from Oct. 3 through Dec. 30. with an opening reception Saturday, Oct. 5 from 2-4 p.m. A portion of the sales will be donated to the San Diego River Park Foundation (SDRPF).
North Park resident, Louis Russell, will display photographs of the river. The images are captured with an 8' x 10' pinhole camera on black and white film, processed in her darkroom, then scanned and edited in Photoshop. They are printed in two ways: on Hahnemuhle Fine Art Paper and on Kozo Niyodo 25 gram paper with white gold leaf hand applied.
The San Diego River Artists' Alliance is a collective of visual and 3D artists from around San Diego County who hike and spend time along the San Diego River from its source in mountains near Julian to the ocean. The artists create artwork about the San Diego River and its ecosystem to celebrate its history, beauty and promise and to encourage the public to connect with the variety of experiences available along the river. The work includes acrylic, photography, mixed media, glass, watercolor, oil, color pencil, fiber arts, paper, ceramic, and polymer clay. Make the world a better place Mama's Pies bake sale returns
Fall is upon us–which means it's time for Mama's Pies Thanksgiving Bake Sale ! San Diego's largest annual bake sale is back for its 20 th year, raising critical funds for Mama's Kitchen, the Food is Medicine Coalition-accredited medically tailored meal provider serving San Diegans facing malnutrition due to critical illnesses like HIV, cancer, congestive heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease.
Over the last two decades, the annual bake sale has become a San Diego staple, with more than 88,000 pies being sold to raise more than $2.2 million. Last year alone, Mama's Pies raised over $114,000 thanks to the sale of over 2,600 pies and nearly 1,200 direct donations. Mama's Kitchen hopes to raise $145,000 during this year's month-long pie sale, which can fund up to 54,500 meals for the organization's clients. All proceeds from Mama's Pies Thanksgiving Bake Sale, both from pie sales and direct donations, directly fund Mama's Kitchen's medically tailored meal delivery services.
Pies go on sale Monday, Oct. 21 and close Friday, Nov. 22. To learn more, visit mamaspies.org. 244 San Diegans kept from homelessness through Diversion program
From January to July 2024, 244 San Diegans were kept from becoming chronically homeless through the Regional Task Force on Homelessness' Diversion practice, thanks to added funding from the County of San Diego.
When the $1 million Supervisor Terra Lawson-Remer and philanthropic partners raised started being spent, 209 unduplicated households were provided support and financial assistance. On average, it costs just $2,863 per household to return people to housing.
Diversion helps steer people who recently became homeless (usually within the first month) from a shelter or living on the street because providers who are specially trained on Diversion engagement know how to ask the right questions about if a person needs family reunification, diverting temporarily as new housing is sustained, and/or relocating permanently to a safe place out of town. They also can connect them with short-term financial assistance – utility deposit, car repair, application fee, security deposit – to get them quickly rehoused. Wightman Street's major cleanup
In an extensive cleanup effort during September focused on Wightman Street Neighborhood Park in the Chollas Creek neighborhood of City Heights, City of San Diego crews cleared more than 8,000 pounds of trash – including large appliances, mattresses, boxes and clothing – caused by illegal dumping and encampments.
The City had received complaints about conditions along the Auburn Creek corridor, which is connected to the stormwater channel just behind Wightman Street Park, with large amounts of debris and hazardous items left behind. More than 60 Get It Done encampment reports had been submitted for this location. Something to celebrate City awarded for website improvements
In recognition of its efficient and user-friendly digital experience, the City of San Diego has received a first place award in The Center for Digital Government's 2024 Government Experience Awards . These awards recognize the achievements of states, cities and counties that have raised the bar on the experience of government services to create a better-engaged constituency and a more responsive government.
According to The Center for Digital Government, the city was awarded first place in the 'city' category for its website's topic-based organization, readable content, user-centric design, increase in online forms and greater transparency and accountability. The city was also recognized for the continued revamping of its customer engagement strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic to foster ease of access to City programs and services for residents and businesses via Sandiego.gov . Handbag company celebrating 12 years with BOGO sale
Sash Bag, the San Diego-based company that's redefined the handbag game with its patented hands-free design, is celebrating its 12-year anniversary in style. For one day only on Oct. 11, Sash Bag will be offering a Buy One, Get One Free sale across all styles and sizes with no limits—a 24-hour celebration of customer love, thriving community spirit, and hands-free freedom!
Following the smashing success of last year's first-ever BOGO Free sale, which broke all single-day sales records, this year's event is set to be even bigger. 'Last year, we dipped our toes in with just 12 hours of BOGO Free, and it was a total blowout!' says Nichole MacDonald, founder of Sash Bag. 'Our customers went wild for it, so we're turning up the fun this year—24 hours of BOGO madness, sitewide! Whether you're treating yourself or stocking up on holiday gifts, now's the perfect time to shop with Sash Bag.'
For more information, visit thesashbag.com . Indie film 'To Fall in Love' announces distribution
A locally-produced indie film will be released on North American cable and streaming platforms on Oct. 22. After a successful film festival run including the world-renowned San Diego International Film Festival, ' To Fall In Love ' was courted by Gravitas Ventures, an Anthem Sports & Entertainment Company, for distribution.
Four filmmakers who first met in San Diego collaborated on 'To Fall In Love,' about an estranged couple navigating a last-ditch effort to save their marriage. Written by Jennifer Lane and directed by San Diego native Michael Foster, actors Beth Gallagher and Eric Casalini take viewers on a painstaking and emotion-inducing journey through psychologist Arthur Aron's famous relationship tool '36 Questions To Fall in Love.'
' To Fall in Love' will be available to rent or own on Oct. 22 and is currently live for pre-orders on iTunes: apple.co/4d3nJrw . To read about how the movie was made, visit sdnews.com/san-diego-intl-film-fest-includes-local-micro-budget-indie-film-to-fall-in-love. It's the economy, stupid! 2024 record year for funding
According to Crunchbase data, fundraising by San Diego County companies has already hit a record $23.6 billion in 2024 for all funding types. The funding amounts have shown a steady increase for a third consecutive year, mostly driven by Post-IPO Debt and Equity funding rounds. Several factors could contribute to this surge, including a robust investment environment, increased interest from venture capital firms and Post-IPO follow-on offering raises from the public markets. These factors indicate a positive trend in funding, potentially driving further growth and innovation in the future. $100 million plus rounds for all funding types have already outpaced the year prior by 23%, totaling 42.
In addition, the correlation between funding and tenant demand has been more pronounced in the life sciences sector for all types of funding, from Venture capital to Post-IPO capital. For example, Mirador raising a Series A $400 million and Avidity Biosciences' Post-IPO capital of $1.2 billion have both resulted in lease transactions in 2024. SD Foundation's State of Latinos report
A new report commissioned by San Diego Foundation (SDF) and developed in partnership with the San Diego Regional Policy & Innovation Center found that most San Diego Latinos have individual incomes of $39,000 or less. The income gap between Latinos and non-Latinos in San Diego is substantial: Latino San Diegans make around $28,000 less per year than white, non-Latino San Diegans. More highlights: While San Diego's Latino population has a high bachelor's degree attainment, 24%, compared to Los Angeles (16%), San Bernardino (13%) and Riverside (12%) counties, they trail other groups in San Diego County with the lowest bachelor's degree attainment.
San Diego's Latino population is young, with a mean age of 33, compared to 42 for San Diego's non-Latino residents.
The majority of San Diego's Latinos were born in the U.S. (70%), and most immigrants are U.S. citizens (53%).
Latinos represent 35% of San Diego County's population. Yet, compared to non-Latino San Diegans, this community faces significant economic challenges due to systemic barriers, socio-economic disparities and unique community needs. SD Community College District adopts $1.05 billion budget
The San Diego Community College District governing board has adopted a balanced operating budget of more than $1.05 billion for the 2024-25 fiscal year, a budget that includes a 2.5% increase from the previous year during a time of continued enrollment growth.
Serving approximately 90,000 students annually at four colleges with campuses throughout the city, the SDCCD is the largest provider of higher education and workforce training in the region and has become a powerhouse in expanding career pathways and preparing students for a fast-evolving economy. A 2023 study found that for every $1 million in tax dollars spent educating SDCCD students, taxpayers receive an average of $1.4 million in return over the course of the students' working lives.
The SDCCD Board of Trustees approved the spending plan on a unanimous vote at its Sept. 12 meeting. The budget includes nearly $643 million in General Fund spending and $402 million from other revenue. Funding sources are varied, and include local property taxes, enrollment fees, federal financial aid and other revenue streams. Tags: Balboa Parkjunior theatremuseums

Handbag company celebrating 12 years with BOGO sale
Sash Bag, the San Diego-based company that's redefined the handbag game with its patented hands-free design, is celebrating its 12-year anniversary in style. For one day only on Oct. 11, Sash Bag will be offering a Buy One, Get One Free sale across all styles and sizes with no limits—a 24-hour celebration of customer love, thriving community spirit, and hands-free freedom!
Following the smashing success of last year's first-ever BOGO Free sale, which broke all single-day sales records, this year's event is set to be even bigger. 'Last year, we dipped our toes in with just 12 hours of BOGO Free, and it was a total blowout!' says Nichole MacDonald, founder of Sash Bag. 'Our customers went wild for it, so we're turning up the fun this year—24 hours of BOGO madness, sitewide! Whether you're treating yourself or stocking up on holiday gifts, now's the perfect time to shop with Sash Bag.'
For more information, visit thesashbag.com . Indie film 'To Fall in Love' announces distribution
A locally-produced indie film will be released on North American cable and streaming platforms on Oct. 22. After a successful film festival run including the world-renowned San Diego International Film Festival, ' To Fall In Love ' was courted by Gravitas Ventures, an Anthem Sports & Entertainment Company, for distribution.
Four filmmakers who first met in San Diego collaborated on 'To Fall In Love,' about an estranged couple navigating a last-ditch effort to save their marriage. Written by Jennifer Lane and directed by San Diego native Michael Foster, actors Beth Gallagher and Eric Casalini take viewers on a painstaking and emotion-inducing journey through psychologist Arthur Aron's famous relationship tool '36 Questions To Fall in Love.'
' To Fall in Love' will be available to rent or own on Oct. 22 and is currently live for pre-orders on iTunes: apple.co/4d3nJrw . To read about how the movie was made, visit sdnews.com/san-diego-intl-film-fest-includes-local-micro-budget-indie-film-to-fall-in-love. It's the economy, stupid! 2024 record year for funding
According to Crunchbase data, fundraising by San Diego County companies has already hit a record $23.6 billion in 2024 for all funding types. The funding amounts have shown a steady increase for a third consecutive year, mostly driven by Post-IPO Debt and Equity funding rounds. Several factors could contribute to this surge, including a robust investment environment, increased interest from venture capital firms and Post-IPO follow-on offering raises from the public markets. These factors indicate a positive trend in funding, potentially driving further growth and innovation in the future. $100 million plus rounds for all funding types have already outpaced the year prior by 23%, totaling 42.
In addition, the correlation between funding and tenant demand has been more pronounced in the life sciences sector for all types of funding, from Venture capital to Post-IPO capital. For example, Mirador raising a Series A $400 million and Avidity Biosciences' Post-IPO capital of $1.2 billion have both resulted in lease transactions in 2024. SD Foundation's State of Latinos report
A new report commissioned by San Diego Foundation (SDF) and developed in partnership with the San Diego Regional Policy & Innovation Center found that most San Diego Latinos have individual incomes of $39,000 or less. The income gap between Latinos and non-Latinos in San Diego is substantial: Latino San Diegans make around $28,000 less per year than white, non-Latino San Diegans. More highlights: While San Diego's Latino population has a high bachelor's degree attainment, 24%, compared to Los Angeles (16%), San Bernardino (13%) and Riverside (12%) counties, they trail other groups in San Diego County with the lowest bachelor's degree attainment.
San Diego's Latino population is young, with a mean age of 33, compared to 42 for San Diego's non-Latino residents.
The majority of San Diego's Latinos were born in the U.S. (70%), and most immigrants are U.S. citizens (53%).
Latinos represent 35% of San Diego County's population. Yet, compared to non-Latino San Diegans, this community faces significant economic challenges due to systemic barriers, socio-economic disparities and unique community needs. SD Community College District adopts $1.05 billion budget
The San Diego Community College District governing board has adopted a balanced operating budget of more than $1.05 billion for the 2024-25 fiscal year, a budget that includes a 2.5% increase from the previous year during a time of continued enrollment growth.
Serving approximately 90,000 students annually at four colleges with campuses throughout the city, the SDCCD is the largest provider of higher education and workforce training in the region and has become a powerhouse in expanding career pathways and preparing students for a fast-evolving economy. A 2023 study found that for every $1 million in tax dollars spent educating SDCCD students, taxpayers receive an average of $1.4 million in return over the course of the students' working lives.
The SDCCD Board of Trustees approved the spending plan on a unanimous vote at its Sept. 12 meeting. The budget includes nearly $643 million in General Fund spending and $402 million from other revenue. Funding sources are varied, and include local property taxes, enrollment fees, federal financial aid and other revenue streams. Tags: Balboa Parkjunior theatremuseums

title: Wave playoff hopes dwindle after loss to NC
description: The San Diego Wave's chances to make the playoffs for a third straight season took another, potentially defining, hit on Saturday after a 2-1 road defeat to the North Carolina Courage. With San Diego behind 2-0 at halftime, interim head coach Landon Donovan's adjustments paid dividends. The visitors played better…
content:
The San Diego Wave's chances to make the playoffs for a third straight season took another, potentially defining, hit on Saturday after a 2-1 road defeat to the North Carolina Courage.
With San Diego behind 2-0 at halftime, interim head coach Landon Donovan's adjustments paid dividends. The visitors played better during the second half in terms of possession and scoring opportunities.
The pressure paid off in the 84th minute when defender Hanna Lundkvist scored on a header, which came off a corner kick beating goalkeeper Casey Murphy. The final seconds saw a fierce attack from the San Diego Wave that almost ended up tying the game and included a check by the upstairs VAR referee for a potential handball inside the box. The check was to no avail as North Carolina ended up with the win to extend its home undefeated streak to 20 games.
The loss puts SD Wave in a precarious position where another loss in either of its final three regular-season matches would guarantee it can finish with no more than 28 points overall. That is the same amount that both Portland and Bay FC have as those two teams hold the seventh and eighth spots respectively. If all three finish tied in points, it would come down to goal differential as the tiebreaker with the Thorns holding a solid advantage over both Bay FC and San Diego in that regard but with the Wave slightly better than Bay FC.
Racing Louisville is also chasing the final playoff spot holding a three-point advantage over the Wave as the two sides will face each other in the regular season finale at Snapdragon Stadium on Nov. 3 with Angel City also lurking and tied in points with San Diego but slightly behind in goal differential.
San Diego next plays against the Houston Dash on Sunday, Oct. 13 at Snapdragon Stadium followed by a Concacaf W Champions Cup match versus Club América on Wednesday, Oct. 16.

title: The Impact of Micro-Learning on Student Success
author: Grhics Tech
description: In today's fast-paced world, traditional learning methods often strug
content:
In today's fast-paced world, traditional learning methods often struggle to keep up with the rapidly evolving demands of students and professionals alike. This is where micro-learning comes into play, offering a modern approach to education that breaks down complex information into easily digestible chunks. With the rise of digital technology and online learning, micro-learning has gained popularity as a tool to enhance student success and skill development. But what exactly is micro-learning, and how does it shape the learning experience for both traditional and online students? Let's explore how this innovative method is revolutionizing education and boosting student outcomes.
What is Micro-Learning?
Micro-learning is an educational strategy that delivers information in small, focused bursts, usually lasting from a few minutes to about 15 minutes. It's designed to target specific learning objectives, making it easier for students to absorb and retain knowledge. This approach often incorporates multimedia elements like videos, infographics, quizzes, and interactive modules to keep learners engaged.
Unlike traditional learning, which might involve lengthy lectures or extensive reading sessions, micro-learning is all about efficiency and relevance. Imagine learning a new skill in bite-sized pieces, like savoring individual chocolates from a box rather than devouring the entire box in one sitting. This method aligns perfectly with today's learners who are used to consuming information on-the-go and prefer learning in short, engaging segments.
For students looking to manage their workload more effectively, especially when facing tight deadlines, micro-learning can be a game-changer. However, when the pressure mounts and you need extra support, it's helpful to know that there is reliable service https://samedaypapers.com/pay-someone-to-do-my-homework/ where you can get assistance with assignments, essays, and other academic tasks. This allows you to focus on mastering new skills through micro-learning without the added stress of juggling too many responsibilities at once.
This combination of self-paced study and professional support can greatly enhance your learning experience, helping you stay ahead in both your coursework and skills development.
How Micro-Learning Enhances Student Success in Traditional Education
Micro-learning has found its way into classrooms, transforming how students engage with the material. In traditional educational settings, it offers several benefits that directly contribute to student success: Improved Focus and Retention: Students often find it challenging to concentrate during long lectures. Micro-learning addresses this by delivering content in shorter bursts, which helps maintain attention and improves information retention. This approach is similar to how our brains naturally process information — in small chunks rather than large amounts. Customization and Personalization: Teachers can tailor micro-learning modules to fit individual learning styles and needs, ensuring that each student gets the most out of the material. For example, visual learners might benefit from infographic-based lessons, while auditory learners could engage more with short podcasts. Increased Engagement: Micro-learning incorporates various multimedia elements that make the learning process interactive and fun. This engagement boosts students' interest in the subject matter, leading to better performance and deeper understanding. Flexibility in Learning Pace: Since micro-learning allows students to absorb content at their own pace, it reduces the pressure and anxiety often associated with traditional learning. This flexibility is especially helpful for students who might struggle with the faster pace of regular classroom settings.
The Role of Micro-Learning in Online Learning Platforms
As online education continues to expand, micro-learning has become a vital component of digital learning platforms. Its adaptable nature fits perfectly with the needs of online learners, offering numerous advantages: Convenience and Accessibility: Online learners often juggle multiple responsibilities, such as work, family, and education. Micro-learning's short modules are easy to fit into a busy schedule, making learning more convenient and accessible to a broader audience. Interactive Learning Experience: Many online courses now use micro-learning to create a more engaging experience through interactive videos, quizzes, and real-time feedback. This helps to keep learners motivated and encourages active participation, which is often lacking in traditional online classes. Real-Time Progress Tracking: Digital platforms that use micro-learning provide tools to track a student's progress in real-time. This immediate feedback loop allows learners to identify their strengths and areas for improvement, making their educational journey more targeted and effective. Scalable Learning: Micro-learning modules can be easily updated and scaled across different platforms. This adaptability ensures that learners always have access to the most current information and skills, keeping them ahead in their academic and professional lives.
Micro-Learning and Skills Development
Beyond academic success, micro-learning plays a significant role in developing essential skills that are crucial in today's world. It equips students with both soft and hard skills that are valuable in personal and professional growth.
Developing Soft Skills through Micro-Learning
Soft skills, such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability, are becoming increasingly important in the modern workforce. Micro-learning modules often focus on these skills by simulating real-life scenarios and encouraging learners to practice them in a controlled environment. For instance, a module might present a case study that requires critical thinking or role-playing exercises to enhance communication skills.
This method not only builds these essential skills but also instills a mindset of continuous learning, where students are motivated to keep improving through small, consistent efforts.
Building Technical and Hard Skills
When it comes to technical or hard skills, micro-learning is a game-changer. Whether it's coding, data analysis, or learning a new language, breaking down complex tasks into manageable lessons helps students grasp these skills more effectively. Interactive tutorials, step-by-step guides, and hands-on exercises allow learners to practice at their own pace, ensuring they thoroughly understand each concept before moving on to the next.
By focusing on skill-specific content, micro-learning accelerates the learning curve, making it easier for students to master technical abilities in less time compared to traditional methods.
Challenges and Considerations
While micro-learning offers many benefits, it's not without its challenges. One of the main issues is the risk of oversimplification. Breaking information into small pieces might lead to a loss of context or a shallow understanding of more complex topics. Additionally, not all subjects are suited for micro-learning. For instance, subjects that require deep, analytical thinking and long-term study might not fit well into this framework.
To overcome these challenges, it's crucial to balance micro-learning with other instructional methods. Educators should integrate micro-learning as part of a broader learning strategy, combining it with in-depth lessons and discussions to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the subject matter.
Conclusion
Micro-learning has proven to be a powerful tool in modern education, significantly enhancing student success both in traditional classrooms and online learning environments. Its ability to boost engagement, improve focus, and develop critical skills makes it an invaluable approach for today's learners. By combining the flexibility of digital learning with targeted, skill-specific content, micro-learning helps students not only succeed academically but also grow into well-rounded individuals ready for the challenges of the modern world. As educational technologies continue to evolve, the impact of micro-learning on student success will only grow stronger, paving the way for a more efficient and adaptable learning experience.

title: La Mesa-El Cajon AAUW features Dr. Connie Mariano on Nov. 9
description: Dr. Connie Mariano is used to breaking barriers, used to shattering the glass ceiling. Dr. Mariano is the featured speaker
content:
Dr. Connie Mariano is used to breaking barriers, used to shattering the glass ceiling.
Dr. Mariano is the featured speaker at the Nov. 9 meeting of the La Mesa-El Cajon AAUW Branch. In addition to the speaker, the branch's scholarship recipients will be present to introduce themselves and share their educational journey. Carol Perkins and Cindy Rittershofer are co-chairs of the scholarship committee.
The meetings are open to the public and are held in King Hall at Foothills United Methodist Church, 4031 Avocado Blvd. in La Mesa. Check the branch website for further details. AAUW La Mesa-El Cajon (CA) Branch.
Born to a Navy steward and his dentist wife in the Philippines, Dr. Mariano lived the life of a family in the American armed forces. Her life has been filled with many achievements: high school valedictorian, graduate with honors at the University of California at San Diego, medical degree from the Uniformed Services University School of Medicine, and a distinguished 24-year career in the U. S. Navy.
Dr. Mariano has also been the first in the following achievements:
ï The first military woman to become the White House Physician to the President
ï The first woman Director of the White House Medical Unit
ï The first Filipino American in U.S. history to become a Navy Rear Admiral
After leaving the White House in 2001 following nine years and service to three sitting American presidents, Dr. Mariano became a consultant in the Executive Health Program at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale from July 2001 to October 2005.
In November 2005, Dr. Mariano founded the Center for Executive Medicine, a medical concierge practice which provides presidential quality medical care to CEOs and their families.
An expert in presidential health care including the 25th Amendment to the Constitution, Dr. Mariano is a frequent guest speaker on television and print media on the topics of care to VIPs, presidential disability, travel medicine, and optimizing quality of care. Dr. Mariano is also a former external advisory board member to the committee advising the Secretary of Veterans Affairs on the overhaul of the VA system.
She is the author of the book, The White House Doctor: My Patients were Presidents, A Memoir, published in 2010 by St. Martin's Press. Dr. Mariano also hosts two talk shows on the VoiceAmerica network, 'House Calls with Dr Connie,' now in its ninth season, and the 'The Widow's Walk' dedicated to the widow's journey.
La Mesa-El Cajon Branch of American Association of University Women (AAUW) has been engaged in 'equity for all' efforts since the 1950's and is one of the largest branches in the state. AAUW empowers women and girls by advocating for more women in leadership positions, closing the gender pay gap and preventing sexual harassment and discrimination. We support girls entering STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) careers. We use research, education, and advocacy at the national, state, and branch levels to accomplish these goals.
For more information about this organization go to lamesaelcajon-ca.aauw.net .
New members are always welcome and do not need to be invited to attend a meeting. Tags: AAUW La Mesa-El Cajon Branch

title: How to Prepare for a Medical Assistant Career in New York
author: Grhics Tech
description: The healthcare industry is one of the fastest-growing sectors in the U.S.
content:
The healthcare industry is one of the fastest-growing sectors in the U.S., and medical assistants are essential players in this field. Whether you are interested in working in a bustling urban hospital or a quiet suburban clinic, a career as a medical assistant offers diverse opportunities and a rewarding professional path. In New York, the demand for medical assistants continues to rise, making it an excellent location to start your healthcare journey. This article will guide you through how to prepare for a medical assistant career in New York, focusing on education, certification, and job prospects.
1. Understanding the Role of a Medical Assistant
Before embarking on this career, it's essential to understand the duties of a medical assistant. Medical assistants handle both administrative and clinical tasks, making them vital to the smooth operation of healthcare facilities. Their responsibilities range from managing patient records, scheduling appointments, and billing to taking vital signs, drawing blood, and assisting physicians with patient exams.
Because of the variety of tasks involved, medical assistants must be versatile, detail-oriented, and skilled at multitasking. In New York, medical assistants work in hospitals, outpatient care centers, clinics, and physicians' offices, providing essential support in diverse medical settings.
2. Enroll in a Medical Assistant Program in New York
The first step to becoming a medical assistant is to complete an accredited training program. A medical assistant program in New York will provide you with the foundational knowledge and practical skills you need to succeed in this role. Most programs cover topics such as Medical terminology
Anatomy and physiology
Pharmacology
Clinical procedures
Office Administration
Patient interaction
Medical assistant programs can be completed in as little as 9-12 months for a certificate or diploma, while associate degree programs may take around two years. New York offers a variety of programs, from community colleges to technical schools, all designed to prepare you for a career in this dynamic field.
While certification is not a legal requirement to work as a medical assistant in New York, it is highly recommended. Many employers prefer or even require medical assistants to be certified, as it shows a higher level of competence and professionalism.
There are several certifications available for medical assistants, with the most common being: Certified Medical Assistant (CMA)
Registered Medical Assistant (RMA)
Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA)
To qualify for these certifications, you typically need to graduate from an accredited medical assistant program and pass a comprehensive exam. Preparing for the certification exam involves reviewing course materials, practicing clinical skills, and taking mock exams.
4. Gain Hands-On Experience
Experience is crucial in the medical assisting field. Most training programs include externships or clinical rotations where you can apply what you've learned in real healthcare settings. These hands-on experiences allow you to work alongside healthcare professionals, interact with patients, and gain a better understanding of your role as a medical assistant.
In New York, you'll find many opportunities to complete your internship at hospitals, clinics, and outpatient centers. Some medical assistant programs in New York have established partnerships with local healthcare providers to facilitate externships, so be sure to ask about these opportunities when selecting a program.
5. Prepare for Job Interviews
Once you've completed your training and earned your certification, the next step is to apply for jobs. Medical assistant positions in New York are available in various healthcare environments, including private practices, urgent care centers, and specialized clinics.
When preparing for interviews, focus on highlighting both your technical skills and soft skills. Employers will want to see that you are competent in medical procedures, but they will also look for qualities such as strong communication skills, empathy, and the ability to handle high-pressure situations.
Research potential employers and tailor your resume and cover letter to the specific job listing. Emphasize any experience gained during externships or part-time healthcare jobs, as this will make you a more competitive candidate.
6. Understand the Job Market in New York
The demand for medical assistants in New York is strong, especially in urban areas like New York City, Buffalo, and Albany. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), employment for medical assistants is expected to grow by 16% from 2021 to 2031, much faster than the average for all occupations.
Pursuing a career as a medical assistant in New York offers many opportunities for growth and fulfillment. By enrolling in a medical assistant program, getting certification, gaining practical experience, and preparing for the job market, you can build a solid foundation for your future in healthcare. With the right preparation, you'll be well on your way to making a meaningful impact in the lives of patients and contributing to the healthcare system.

title: Judge sets bail for OB murder suspect at $2 million
description: An attorney for an Ocean Beach murder suspect was successful in getting a judge to set bail for his client on Oct. 14, but the judge rejected a bid for $100,000 bail and instead set it at $2 million.…
content:
An attorney for an Ocean Beach murder suspect was successful in getting a judge to set bail for his client on Oct. 14, but the judge rejected a bid for $100,000 bail and instead set it at $2 million.
Attorney Brandon Roesler, who represents Andrew Phillip Restrepo, 33, asked San Diego Superior Court Judge John Pro to set aside the no bail figure for Restrepo. He said his family would help him with an 'electronic monitoring' system with authorities on $100,000 bail.
Restrepo has pleaded not guilty to killing Sean Ellis Glenn, 34, in a May 10, 2023, incident in the 5000 block of Newport Avenue for which Restrepo was arrested in August of 2024.
Roesler said the victim had traumatic injuries to the back of his head when he was punched and his head hit the ground. Glenn was in a coma for three months in a hospital without waking up and died on Aug. 5, 2023.
Roesler said the correct charge is manslaughter but not murder because Restrepo had no malice or intent to kill. 'It is a routine bar fight that occurred outside,' he added.
Roesler said Restrepo's mother and sister were in the audience and added they would help him. He said Restrepo would continue working in a communications company if granted $100,000 bail. A $2 million bail figure is considered too high for Restrepo's family.
Deputy District Attorney Jessica Sutterley said Restrepo 'does have training' in martial arts. 'He knocked two people unconscious,' she said.
Restrepo is also charged with injuring another man on a city bus in the Midway area just weeks earlier and that victim was also knocked unconscious, said the prosecutor.
'The defendant appears to like fist fighting,' said Sutterley, adding that one witness claimed to see him laughing after Glenn hit the ground and walked away. 'His targets are random,' she said.
Sutterley said Restrepo has an incident in a Florida bar in which he punched someone in the face, and the San Diego incidents show 'callousness.' She urged bail be set at $2 million.
His attorney told the judge Restrepo 'was an amateur' in fighting.
Pro told the attorneys he was setting $2 million bail for 'protection of the public,' considering one person was killed in one fight.
A preliminary hearing was set for Jan. 27, 2025. Restrepo remains in the South Bay Detention Facility.

title: Crusaders Soccer getting a kick out of fall activities
description: Crusaders Soccer staff continues to provide pertinent information to help our soccer
content:
Crusaders Soccer staff continues to provide pertinent information to help our soccer players stay healthy, considering trying out for their high school team and/or playing soccer at the college level.
On Oct. 1, Kate Maietta, the college director and a competitive coach with the Crusaders Soccer Club, teamed up with Kamryn Correll, a Crusaders Soccer competitive level coach and held a classroom session attended by 40 girls playing on Crusaders Soccer competitive teams born in 2012 through 2008 emphasizing physical fitness.
Correll is a collegiate Division III athlete who received CCCAA (junior college association league honors. She is also a 3X Junior Olympics participant in Track and Field. Kamyrn has experience in college scouting, coaching at Francis Parker and has four years of coaching private training sessions. Correll is a CPT (certified personal trainer) and currently playing in the WPSL for the San Diego Strikers.
Correll's program is free for the players and consists of two parts. She stated, 'The first was a one-hour classroom session to provide middle and high school aged girls important information on injury prevention exercises, pre, and post-game/practice recovery exercises and basic nutrition information.'
The second portion of this program will be six one-hour sessions held on the turf field at Pershing Middle School.
At the end of the first session, each girl received a packet with three workouts a week. Following each of the three workouts, the girls will meet with Correll at Pershing Middle School for a one-hour conditioning workout session with a complete warm-up and cooldown session with an emphasis on injury prevention. Upon completion of the six-week workshop, players will be able to utilize their packet independently.
On Tuesday, Oct. 8, Seth Tunick, an assistant director of Coaching for the Crusaders Soccer Club and the varsity soccer coach for Patrick Henry High School, conducted a program for all 9th grade boys and girls, and their parents, interested in trying out for their high school soccer team.
The presentation focused on everything involving high school soccer including requirements to participate, the different levels, the tryout process, club vs high school differences, and Seth answered questions from players and parents.
Victor Melendez, the director of coaching for Crusaders Soccer, announced the dates and time of the annual three Thanksgiving soccer camps. The Competitive and Recreational camps will be held Nov. 25-27, and the Goalkeepers camp will be Nov. 29-30. For more information and to register, go to crusaderssoccer.org.
As part of his commitment to the Crusaders recreational program, all goalkeepers on teams playing 7 V 7, were invited to a special one-hour goalkeeper clinic as part of the on-going Friday Clinics.
Melendez, who is also the goalkeeper coach for the San Diego Sockers, conducted the goalkeeper clinic giving basic instructions to the goalkeepers to help them defend their goal in a safe manner.
For more information on the Crusaders Soccer Club and its program, visit crusaderssoccer.org.
