title: Why Studying Law is More Challenging Than You Think (and How to Overcome It)
author: Grhics Tech
description: People often think of studying law as mentally challenging a
content:
People often think of studying law as mentally challenging and prestigious, but a lot of students don't realize how hard it can be. There are a lot of things that you have to do to become an expert in the law, from understanding complicated legal ideas to going through long reading lists. If you are in law school or are thinking about going, you need to know what the difficulties will be. More importantly, it's important to have plans for how to deal with these problems head-on. 1. Managе Written Assignments and Papers
Writing legal essays and papers is another formidable challenge. To do these tasks well, you need to know a lot about the law and be able to explain your ideas in a way that persuades others. It can also be very stressful for students because their teachers expect them to make original, well-researched arguments.
How to handle it: When writing a legal essay, it's crucial to begin by outlining your key points, which will help you stay organized and ensure your arguments flow logically. Be sure to support your claims with relevant case law and statutes. However, it can be challenging to write under time constraints. If you're struggling to complete all your assignments or feel uncertain about the quality of your work, consider seeking help. Many students choose to buy custom essay at CustomWriting , where professional writers can assist in crafting well-structured and coherent papers, giving you more time to focus on other important tasks. This method helps you meet deadlines and makes sure that your papers meet the high academic standards needed in law school. In the end, it lowers your stress and makes you better at everything you do. 2. Recognize Terminology and Complex Legal Theories
One of the hardest things for law students is getting to grips with complicated legal ideas and terms. In some areas, ideas may be easier to understand, but in the legal world, things often have their own rules and language. It's not always easy to understand case law, laws, and legal concepts. It takes a lot of time and patience to fully grasp them.
How to handle it: The key to getting through this problem is to break up tough information into smaller pieces that are easier to understand. Talk to your teachers or classmates about something you don't understand. Don't be afraid to ask for help. You can find more information online, like law blogs or educational videos, that can help you understand things that are hard to understand in your reads. Making mind maps is another useful way to see how different legal ideas connect with each other. This might help you remember things better on tests. 3. Managе the heaviest workload
The sheer volume of reading in law school can leave students feeling overwhelmed. Casebooks are often filled with hundreds of pages of dense legal texts, and keeping up with your assignments can seem impossible at times. On top of that, you're expected to engage with the material critically and not just memorize it.
How to handle it: Time management is your best friend here. Use a planner or a digital tool to map out your deadlines, reading schedules, and study times. Break down your reading assignments into daily or weekly goals to avoid the last-minute rush. Additionally, speed reading techniques can help you process material more quickly without sacrificing comprehension. If you find yourself falling behind, it may be beneficial to form a study group where you can divide reading tasks and share notes. 4. Critical Thinking and Analytical Skills
Legal education isn't just taking in facts; it's also about questioning them, studying them, and using what you've learned in real life. Law students need to be able to carefully look at arguments, spot flaws in legal reasoning, and make their own points in response. Because of this focus on critical thinking, law school may be more mentally difficult than other fields.
How to handle it: One way to sharpen your critical thinking is to actively engage with every case or reading. Don't just passively read the material—ask yourself why certain decisions were made, and think about how you would approach the issue differently. Participate in class discussions and debate with your classmates to hone your analytical skills. Over time, you'll find that thinking critically becomes second nature. 5. Handlе Severe Pressure and Competition
Law school is known for its competitive environment, with students vying for top grades, internships, and job offers. The pressure to succeed can become overwhelming, leading to stress, burnout, and self-doubt. This mental strain is one of the less talked-about challenges of law school, but it's a significant one.
How to handle it: First, remember that it's okay to ask for help when things become too much. Talk to a counselor if you're feeling overwhelmed or stressed out. Developing a support network, whether through family, friends, or fellow students, can also make a big difference. Remember that taking care of your mental health is crucial for academic success.
In addition, learning how to manage competition positively is essential. Focus on your personal growth rather than comparing yourself to others. Celebrate small victories and understand that setbacks are part of the learning process. 6. Memorization and Application
Law exams are notoriously difficult. They typically require not just rote memorization of laws and cases but the application of legal principles to hypothetical scenarios. Many students struggle with this dual challenge—remembering vast amounts of information while thinking on their feet during exams.
How to handle it: Active recall techniques can be a game changer when it comes to memorizing laws and cases. Create flashcards , quiz yourself, or use spaced repetition apps to ensure you retain information over time. Additionally, practice applying the material by working through past exam papers. The more you expose yourself to hypothetical scenarios, the better you'll become at applying the law under time pressure. Don't wait until the last minute—start preparing for exams well in advance to reduce stress. Conclusion
Studying law is undoubtedly a challenging endeavor, but with the right strategies, it's a challenge you can overcome. Being ready, organizing your time well, and being willing to ask for help when you need it are the keys to success, whether you're dealing with a lot of reading or a tough competition. Don't forget that becoming a great lawyer isn't about getting things done quickly. It's about learning how to stick with things until you get better.
With these tips, you'll not only survive law school but thrive in it!

title: Point Loma finds some new life in 27-16 win over Steele Canyon
description: A struggling Point Loma Pointer offense found some new life last week in a 27-16 win over Steele Canyon High to spoil the host's Homecoming night.
content:
A struggling Point Loma Pointer offense found some new life last week in a 27-16 win over Steele Canyon High to spoil the host's Homecoming night.
This was a night when new quarterback Henry Heuser threw four touchdown passes to four different teammates and five different defenders intercepted five Cougar passes.
The win improved the Pointers' season record to 3-2 and marked the team's first winning streak of the season after shutting out Eastlake 16-0 two weeks ago as they begin Western League play tonight when they visit Madison. Romeo Carter (front) and Leo Sahd (rear) move in to tackle a Steele Canyon runner during last week's 27-16 Pointer win at Steele Canyon.
The Pointers started early against the Cougars when, on the first series of the game, Leo Sahd grabbed the first of those five interceptions and several plays later grabbed another pass, this time from Heuser in the right corner of the end zone for a 7-0 lead with just 5:10 expired in the game.
After neither team moved the ball well, Heuser threw an interception that gave the Cougars the ball at the Pointer 22, but after several attempts to tie the score, Pointer Jack Leitz intercepted a Steele Canyon pass that led to the next Pointer score. From their own 10, the Pointers found themselves backed up to their own four-yard line as halftime neared.
Surprisingly, they covered that 96-yard distance in just two plays, with Heuser hitting Ben Kamen on a 51-yard pass play, and Kamen again to cover the remianing 44 yards for the touchdown and 14-0 lead just 3:49 before the break.
Steele Canyon continued to pass and found the end zone 50 seconds before halftime to get within six at 14-8.
A third quarter interception and shifty return by Matteo Correia left some observers wondering whether Correia could jump-start a Pointer running game averaging just 2.8 yards per carry through the first half of the season.
Correia's pick did lead to the third Pointer score, this time a 19-yard strike to Romeo Carter who did a nice job getting his feet down before stepping out of bounds. Ryan Cleator's third PAT upped the Pointer lead to 21-8 in the final minute of the third quarter.
But before the quarter ended, Cleator intercepted a pass on the first play of the Cougars' drive, his long return being called back by an illegal block penalty. But his interception also led to another Pointer score.
Heuser's 12-yard pass to Caden Williams ended Pointer scoring when the PAT attempt was moved back on a penalty and then blocked by the Cougars with 7:11 remaining in the game. Heuser finished 10 of 18 for 196 yards Pointer defenders Carson Allen (90) and Julius Moya (75) pursue the Steele Canyon quarterback during last week's 27-16 Point Loma win.
The Cougars threatened at the Pointer 10-yard line again but Ian Metayer intercepted a desperate fourth-down pass, the fifth by Pointer defenders on the night.
With 21 seconds left on the scoreboard, the Cougars finally scored against Pointer reserves, the two-point conversion making the 27-16 score a final.
Metayer, a third-year varsity player who stands at 6 ft. 2 in. and weighs 210 pounds, is a team captain and defensive force. He is talking to several colleges but has not made a selection.
'Our defense came out strong tonight,' Metayer said, 'And five interceptions to end the game is a great thing to look at. We have a strong schedule coming up and there's always improvements to be made but today was a good showing for our defense.' Speaking to his teammates, Metayer said, 'Hell of a job boys! We did great out there!'
Head coach Ryan Price saw growth in his team's effort.
'Five interceptions, the defense played well again and our offense finally got some big chunk plays in our passing game and the running game got going in the second half. We learned from our previous instances where we're up in the first half how to close out a game. It's a great indication of growth and that's what I'm really happy about.'
The Pointers now embark on their Western League schedule which includes No. 1 ranked Lincoln and No. 3 ranked Cathedral Catholic and a non-league game against longtime rival No. 10 La Jolla.
Tonight's foe is a Madison team undergoing an uncharacteristic difficult season. A longtime Pointer nemesis, the Warhawks are currently 1-4 and ranked 27th in the San Diego CIF Section after playing tough opponents. They also defeated Steele Canyon 35-21 on Aug. 30.
EXTRA POINTS
The Pointer JV is 4-1 after wins over Eastlake (49-0) and Steele Canyon (14-6). The freshman team is also 4-1 after defeating Eastlake (27-8) and Steele Canyon (14-7).
The Pointers are currently ranked No. 23 in the CIF San Diego Section and have scored 88 points while giving up 83..
Community members are reminded no unsupervised elementary and middle school students will be admitted to remaining Pointer home games Oct. 18 and Nov. 1. They must remain seated with a parent or adult chaperone except when using the restroom or purchasing from the Chick-fil-A concession.
Top photo: Running back Braden Lane (23) picks up part of the 65 yards he gained in the Pointers' 27-16 win at Steele Canyon last week. Photos by Scott Hopkins Tags: footballPoint Loma High School

title: ALBION San Diego standouts making an impact In Irvine
description: With ALBION San Diego taking a break from the National Independent Soccer Association (NISA) for the 2024 season, that has not stopped many of its standout players from making an impact in other…
content:
With ALBION San Diego taking a break from the National Independent Soccer Association (NISA) for the 2024 season, that has not stopped many of its standout players from making an impact in other teams.
Among them are the three who currently play with Irvine Zeta FC in the NISA west division and who are now one step away from making it the final. Defender Andrew Kleszewski, Shinya Kadono and defender Harold Hanson have continued to put their skills from their time with ALBION to good use as Irvine Zeta gets ready to face the Michigan Stars on Saturday, Oct. 12 at Championship Soccer Stadium.
The 'three amigos', as they've been affectionately nicknamed by the fans, helped lead ALBION San Diego to the semifinals in 2023 before falling 3-2 at the hands of the Stars which came a season after the team made the championship match.
Kleszewski, Kadono and Hanson have also strengthened their chemistry on the pitch which has helped lead Irvine to a chance at lifting the trophy in its rookie NISA season. The added advantage is that they still have Tyler Silva and Khadim Seye as part of the coaching staff just as it was when they played their home games at Canyon Crest Academy last year with ALBION San Diego.
The task to reach the final will not be an easy one as they face a familiar foe in Michigan who won the 2022 NISA title and was also a 2023 finalist. The Stars have always had a core of seasoned and talented players who can impose themselves through their physicality and technical abilities from the opening whistle. ALBION San Diego has yet to officially announce its return for the 2025 season where it could play the role of San Diego FC's local professional rival now that San Diego Loyal is no longer around.
Who wouldn't want to see a US Open Cup game between ALBION San Diego and San Diego FC?
Based on how much fan attention there was the two times that ALBION and San Diego Loyal faced each other, it would be a must see game that no true soccer fan would want to miss.
Photo credit: Oscar Yu Tags: Albion San Diegosoccer

title: Renowned pro boxer to speak at Outreach event on Oct. 19 in Spring Valley
description: Local professional boxer Adrian Vargas will be a special guest at the upcoming Casa de Oro Bible Church Community Outreach event which will feature a car show and live music for those attending. The…
content:
Local professional boxer Adrian Vargas will be a special guest at the upcoming Casa de Oro Bible Church Community Outreach event which will feature a car show and live music for those attending.
The address for those interested in attending the event on Oct. 19 at Casa de Oro Bible Church is 10195 Madrid Way in Spring Valley. The event runs from noon to 4 p.m.
Vargas competes in the welterweight class and is currently undefeated in his first 15 fights with 14 wins and one draw which includes nine knockouts.
'I pray that the holy spirit moves throughout all the speakers, Lord willing, and everyone enjoys the good food, Christian music and all the fellowships because it's going to be a great environment with wonderful people,' Vargas stated.
Besides the accolades that he's received as a boxer, Vargas has also served for over a year as the vice president of Restoring San Diego which is a Christ-centered outreach that focuses and targets the street population. Its mission is to reach people who have been affected by choices that have resulted in homelessness, a life of drug addiction, gangs, prostitution, and crime while prioritizing the men, women, and youth who have been victims of the struggles within urban communities by reaching them with the love of Jesus Christ.
The event where Vargas will be present and speaking is open to the public and also has a goal of empowering those present by providing information on housing, transitional living, addiction services, career and educational resources, spiritual counseling, discipleship and youth outreach.
'The message is to always fight the good fight of faith and be ready in season and out of season to preach the word of God,' he added.
Vargas trains at the House of Boxing Training Center in Paradise Hills.
Courtesy photo Tags: Adrian VargasCasa de Oro Bible Church

title: The latest in Downtown this October
author: Uptown Downtown News
description: A coalition of Downtown residents and businesses announced an
content:
A coalition of Downtown residents and businesses announced an action plan to reduce crime, improve public safety, and enhance cleanliness in San Diego's urban core. Led by the Downtown San Diego Partnership, the group's five-point safety plan was endorsed by Mayor Todd Gloria during a morning rally on C Street and Third Avenue.
The five-point safety plan calls for a variety of actions, including: A 24/7 no tent encampment policy on all Downtown streets and sidewalks
Increased police presence in Downtown
Deploying a dedicated team to address psychiatric crises throughout Downtown, including MTS trolley and bus stops
Funding for fentanyl task force operated by SDPD
Helping people in need get off the streets by speeding up implementation of California's conservatorship program
Backing a ballot measure mandating stronger sentences for certain drug and theft crimes, and implementing new California laws cracking down on 'smash and grabs'
Actions to reduce trash, clean sidewalks, and improve street lighting
The full plan can be read at downtownsandiego.org/safety-plan. Explore Downtown Gaslamp Quarter updates its transportation guide
The Gaslamp Quarter has revamped its website's transportation guide to make getting to-and-from the popular nightlife destination easier. A standout feature of the new website is the interactive map function, which includes unique layers for all types of mobility. T he enhanced website provides clear, concise details on public transit, rideshare services, parking facilities, bike routes, and more. Visitors are encouraged to explore the new transportation page at gaslamp.org/transportation/ and watch the 'Gaslamp: It All Starts With How You Get Here' video. New tours of Little Italy
So Diego debuted a new tour through the history, culture and culinary delights of Little Italy. For locals or tourists, the tour is a way to explore the iconic neighborhood and enjoy tastings at multiple restaurants. Book through littleitalysd.com. State of pay 2024 record year for funding
According to Crunchbase data, fundraising by San Diego County companies has already hit a record $23.6 billion in 2024 for all funding types. The funding amounts have shown a steady increase for a third consecutive year, mostly driven by Post-IPO Debt and Equity funding rounds. Several factors could contribute to this surge, including a robust investment environment, increased interest from venture capital firms and Post-IPO follow-on offering raises from the public markets. These factors indicate a positive trend in funding, potentially driving further growth and innovation in the future. $100 million plus rounds for all funding types have already outpaced the year prior by 23%, totaling 42.
In addition, the correlation between funding and tenant demand has been more pronounced in the life sciences sector for all types of funding, from Venture capital to Post-IPO capital. For example, Mirador raising a Series A $400 million and Avidity Biosciences' Post-IPO capital of $1.2 billion have both resulted in lease transactions in 2024. SD Foundation's State of Latinos report
A new report commissioned by San Diego Foundation (SDF) and developed in partnership with the San Diego Regional Policy & Innovation Center found that most San Diego Latinos have individual incomes of $39,000 or less. The income gap between Latinos and non-Latinos in San Diego is substantial: Latino San Diegans make around $28,000 less per year than white, non-Latino San Diegans. More highlights: While San Diego's Latino population has a high bachelor's degree attainment, 24%, compared to Los Angeles (16%), San Bernardino (13%) and Riverside (12%) counties, they trail other groups in San Diego County with the lowest bachelor's degree attainment.
San Diego's Latino population is young, with a mean age of 33, compared to 42 for San Diego's non-Latino residents.
The majority of San Diego's Latinos were born in the U.S. (70%), and most immigrants are U.S. citizens (53%).
Latinos represent 35% of San Diego County's population. Yet, compared to non-Latino San Diegans, this community faces significant economic challenges due to systemic barriers, socio-economic disparities and unique community needs. Data: Offices leaving Downtown
Since the onset of the pandemic, there has been a notable increase in office tenants choosing to relocate to a different submarket, surpassing the number of tenants staying within their current submarket by 23%, according to JLL. Among the submarkets in San Diego, Downtown and UTC have witnessed the largest exodus of tenants relocating to new regions outside their previous submarket. Many of these tenants have opted to move where they can find more cost-effective options and be in closer proximity to their employees. Mission Valley and Kearny Mesa have experienced a significant influx of tenants relocating from other submarkets within San Diego. These submarkets have attracted tenants due to their central locations, competitive rental rates, amenities and free parking. SD Community College District adopts $1.05 billion budget
The San Diego Community College District governing board has adopted a balanced operating budget of more than $1.05 billion for the 2024-25 fiscal year, a budget that includes a 2.5% increase from the previous year during a time of continued enrollment growth.
Serving approximately 90,000 students annually at four colleges with campuses throughout the city, the SDCCD is the largest provider of higher education and workforce training in the region and has become a powerhouse in expanding career pathways and preparing students for a fast-evolving economy. A 2023 study found that for every $1 million in tax dollars spent educating SDCCD students, taxpayers receive an average of $1.4 million in return over the course of the students' working lives.
The SDCCD Board of Trustees approved the spending plan on a unanimous vote at its Sept. 12 meeting. The budget includes nearly $643 million in General Fund spending and $402 million from other revenue. Funding sources are varied, and include local property taxes, enrollment fees, federal financial aid and other revenue streams. Airport secures $26.3 million grant from FAA
The San Diego International Airport's Terminal 1 project has accrued a total of $192.1 million in federal funding following a recent $26.3 million grant from FAA. The revamped Terminal 1 will feature 30 gates, a 5,200-space parking garage , a new baggage handling system with a 2,000-bag-per-hour capacity, and a three-lane access road to reduce congestion on Harbor Drive. Good works 244 San Diegans kept from homelessness through Diversion program
From January to July 2024, 244 San Diegans were kept from becoming chronically homeless through the Regional Task Force on Homelessness' Diversion practice, thanks to added funding from the County of San Diego.
When the $1 million Supervisor Terra Lawson-Remer and philanthropic partners raised started being spent, 209 unduplicated households were provided support and financial assistance. On average, it costs just $2,863 per household to return people to housing.
Diversion helps steer people who recently became homeless (usually within the first month) from a shelter or living on the street because providers who are specially trained on Diversion engagement know how to ask the right questions about if a person needs family reunification, diverting temporarily as new housing is sustained, and/or relocating permanently to a safe place out of town. They also can connect them with short-term financial assistance – utility deposit, car repair, application fee, security deposit – to get them quickly rehoused. New clients headed to Day Center during heat waves
The Neil Good Day Center, operated by Father Joe's Villages, saw a dramatic uptick in the number of people accessing services during extreme heat conditions in late August.
In August, the organization served more than 3,000 individuals with key services like showers, laundry, and more. There were also 412 new enrollments at the Day Center, more than double the number seen in July and the highest number so far in 2024.
The Neil Good Day Center is the only drop-in services center for people experiencing homelessness in San Diego. It provides a safe break from extreme weather conditions, as well as crucial services like a mailing address, phone charging, and free haircuts.
During August, Father Joe's Villages served 3,821 people experiencing homelessness, including through 23,249 shelter bed nights. The Village Health Center provided medical, dental, psychiatric and behavioral health care to 1,069 unduplicated clients. Mama's Pies bake sale returns
Fall is upon us–which means it's time for Mama's Pies Thanksgiving Bake Sale ! San Diego's largest annual bake sale is back for its 20 th year, raising critical funds for Mama's Kitchen, the Food is Medicine Coalition-accredited medically tailored meal provider serving San Diegans facing malnutrition due to critical illnesses like HIV, cancer, congestive heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease.
Over the last two decades, the annual bake sale has become a San Diego staple, with more than 88,000 pies being sold to raise more than $2.2 million. Last year alone, Mama's Pies raised over $114,000 thanks to the sale of over 2,600 pies and nearly 1,200 direct donations. Mama's Kitchen hopes to raise $145,000 during this year's month-long pie sale, which can fund up to 54,500 meals for the organization's clients. All proceeds from Mama's Pies Thanksgiving Bake Sale, both from pie sales and direct donations, directly fund Mama's Kitchen's medically tailored meal delivery services.
Pies go on sale Monday, Oct. 21 and close Friday, Nov. 22. To learn more, visit mamaspies.org. Let's celebrate! City awarded for website improvements
In recognition of its efficient and user-friendly digital experience, the City of San Diego has received a first place award in The Center for Digital Government's 2024 Government Experience Awards . These awards recognize the achievements of states, cities and counties that have raised the bar on the experience of government services to create a better-engaged constituency and a more responsive government.
According to The Center for Digital Government, the city was awarded first place in the 'city' category for its website's topic-based organization, readable content, user-centric design, increase in online forms and greater transparency and accountability. The city was also recognized for the continued revamping of its customer engagement strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic to foster ease of access to City programs and services for residents and businesses via Sandiego.gov . Phyllis Barber named president of Downtown Lions Club
The Downtown San Diego Lions Club announced Phyllis Barber is the new president of the club. A Navy veteran, Barber, will be taking over from Jonathan Moiser whose emphasis was on, 'Show Up, Do Something.' She was officially sworn in at the Lions annual Installation Dinner on the deck of the Downtown Lions Manor.
Barber will continue to focus on moving the Downtown San Diego Lions Club forward in 2024 and 2025 with an emphasis on growing the membership so they can help even more organizations, individuals and causes in the San Diego area. Indie film 'To Fall in Love' announces distribution
A locally-produced indie film will be released on North American cable and streaming platforms on Oct. 22. After a successful film festival run including the world-renowned San Diego International Film Festival, ' To Fall In Love ' was courted by Gravitas Ventures, an Anthem Sports & Entertainment Company, for distribution.
Four filmmakers who first met in San Diego collaborated on 'To Fall In Love,' about an estranged couple navigating a last-ditch effort to save their marriage. Written by Jennifer Lane and directed by San Diego native Michael Foster, actors Beth Gallagher and Eric Casalini take viewers on a painstaking and emotion-inducing journey through psychologist Arthur Aron's famous relationship tool '36 Questions To Fall in Love.'
' To Fall in Love' will be available to rent or own on Oct. 22 and is currently live for pre-orders on iTunes: apple.co/4d3nJrw . To read about how the movie was made, visit sdnews.com/san-diego-intl-film-fest-includes-local-micro-budget-indie-film-to-fall-in-love. Handbag company celebrating 12 years with BOGO sale
Sash Bag, the San Diego-based company that's redefined the handbag game with its patented hands-free design, is celebrating its 12-year anniversary in style. For one day only on Oct. 11, Sash Bag will be offering a Buy One, Get One Free sale across all styles and sizes with no limits—a 24-hour celebration of customer love, thriving community spirit, and hands-free freedom!
Following the smashing success of last year's first-ever BOGO Free sale, which broke all single-day sales records, this year's event is set to be even bigger. 'Last year, we dipped our toes in with just 12 hours of BOGO Free, and it was a total blowout!' says Nichole MacDonald, founder of Sash Bag. 'Our customers went wild for it, so we're turning up the fun this year—24 hours of BOGO madness, sitewide! Whether you're treating yourself or stocking up on holiday gifts, now's the perfect time to shop with Sash Bag.'
For more information, visit thesashbag.com. Museums and exhibits Kids get in free at museums this month
The San Diego Museum Council has announced the return of the popular Kids Free San Diego program, now in its 13th year . From Oct. 1 to 31, children ages 12 and under can enjoy free admission to more than 50 museums, aquariums/zoos, gardens, state parks, historic sites and other family-friendly attractions throughout San Diego County. Sites include some of San Diego's most popular sites, including the USS Midway Museum, Fleet Science Center, Birch Aquarium and San Diego Air & Space Museum, as well as many hidden gems waiting to be discovered. Some locations are free for the entire family or offer pay-what-you-wish admission year-round. A full list of participating museums can be found on the San Diego Museum Council website . Chicano history at City Hall
The City Clerk Archives , in proud collaboration with the Chicano Park Museum and Cultural Center (CPMCC), is holding a groundbreaking exhibit honoring both American Archives Month and Hispanic/Latino Heritage Month. Titled 'Telling Our Stories and Preserving Our Histories: The Chicano Movement in San Diego,' the exhibit runs through Oct. 18. at the City Administration Building (202 C Street lobby).
This exhibit is part of the city clerk's inaugural 'Telling Our Stories and Preserving Our Histories' series, which seeks to document and celebrate the rich and diverse history of San Diego's communities. By engaging with community storytellers and exploring new preservation techniques, the exhibit aims to offer a comprehensive view of 'The Chicano Movement in San Diego' and its lasting impact. New Navy Seal Museum Downtown receives giant artifact through second-story window
The upcoming Navy SEAL Museum San Diego (NSMSD), located at 1001 Kettner Blvd., received a SEAL Delivery Vehicle (SDV) that was crane-lifted into the museum's second floor in a highly visible installation on Sept. 26.
The SDV is 21-ft. long and weighs over 1,600 lbs. It shipped cross country from Navy SEAL Museum, Fort Pierce via flatbed truck. Once inside, the SDV will eventually be suspended from the ceiling 15 ft. overhead. Visitors will be able to witness the collection piece's size and scale personally when the Museum opens in Summer/Fall 2025.
Naval Special Warfare has been using SDVs since the 1970s in various configurations. SDVs are used to recon enemy harbors, conduct anti-ship operations, and covertly insert and extract U.S. Navy SEALs. They can be deployed from submarines and other craft.

title: Fall DIY: Pumpkin Succulent Arrangements and Gardening Tool Care Workshops
description: If you're passionate about gardening, sustainability, or simply looking for ways to get involved with your community, becoming a member of the San Carlos Community Garden (SCCG) might be just what you…
content:
If you're passionate about gardening, sustainability, or simply looking for ways to get involved with your community, becoming a member of the San Carlos Community Garden (SCCG) might be just w hat you need.
For an annual fee of just $35, you'll not only help support the ongoing growth and maintenance of our all-volunteer run nonprofit, but you'll also enjoy free access to monthly educational workshops and other seasonal programs. These workshops are a great opportunity to enhance your gardening skills, meet like-minded people, and participate in hands-on projects that are as fun as they are informative.
With workshops covering a wide range of topics—from crafting beautiful fall decor to learning how to compost at home, to growing tomatoes all year long and other essential gardening techniques—SCCG's membership program is a great way to grow your knowledge and contribute to the local gardening community.
Upcoming Workshops: Creativity and Skills for Every Gardener
DIY Pumpkin Succulent Arrangement – Saturday, Oct. 19 9 – 10:30 a.m.
As the season shifts into fall, what better way to celebrate than by creating your own festive decor? The DIY Pumpkin Succulent Arrangement Workshop offers you the chance to make a stunning autumn centerpiece.
Led by SCCG's local Master Gardener, April Lowe, this 'make-and-take' seminar is designed for all skill levels. Participants will be guided through the steps of assembling a beautiful pumpkin succulent arrangement that will brighten up any space. Succulents and decorative materials will be provided, but attendees are encouraged to bring their own pumpkin (while some supplies will be on hand, they are limited, so it's best to come prepared).
Succulent arrangements are a fantastic way to blend the beauty of nature with fall's signature decor element—the pumpkin. Plus, these arrangements last much longer than traditional fall flowers, and the succulents can be replanted after the pumpkin starts to break down. This workshop is a perfect opportunity to let your creativity shine while making something sustainable and beautiful for your home.
Gardening Tool Care & Sharpening Workshop – Saturday, Nov. 16
After you've crafted your pumpkin centerpiece, it's time to focus on something every gardener needs to know: proper tool care. Join Master Gardener Jake Jacobs for the Gardening Tool Care & Sharpening Workshop, where you'll learn the ins and outs of maintaining your garden hand tools.
From cleaning and sharpening to honing and oiling, this hands-on workshop will cover everything you need to keep your tools in tip-top shape. Regular maintenance ensures that your tools last longer and work more efficiently, saving you time and effort in the garden. You'll even get the chance to practice on your own set of hand pruners, so bring them along!
Cost to attend these workshops are $10 per person or become a SCCG garden member and attend for free.
Why Become a San Carlos Community Garden Member?
The San Carlos Community Garden is a nonprofit organization run entirely by volunteers, and your membership fee directly supports the upkeep of the garden, ensuring it remains a thriving, sustainable resource for everyone in the community. At just $35 per year, becoming a member is an affordable and impactful way to deepen your connection to nature, build community, and give back to a space that is dedicated to environmental education and sustainability. Your support is how SCCG's vibrant volunteer-driven garden continues to carry out its mission of Growing Community.
How to Sign Up
Becoming a member of the San Carlos Community Garden is easy. And, if you're eager to start planting, you can also lease a garden plot for just $125 a year. Simply visit sancarloscommunitygarden.com where you can sign up for an annual membership, garden plots and more. SCCG is open every Saturday and on the first and third Sunday each month from 9-11 a.m. and is located at 6460 Boulder Lake Ave., San Diego. Tags: San Carlos Community Garden

title: Best Project Management Tools
author: Grhics Tech
description: Every successful project starts with a solid foundation, and that foundation often lies in the right project management tools. With countless options flooding the market, it's vital to identify the tools that not only meet your needs but also enhance your team's collaboration and efficiency. Join us as we delve…
content:
Every successful project starts with a solid foundation, and that foundation often lies in the right project management tools. With countless options flooding the market, it's vital to identify the tools that not only meet your needs but also enhance your team's collaboration and efficiency. Join us as we delve into a curated list of the best project management tools with their standout features and find the one that will revolutionize your project workflow.
GanttPRO
GanttPRO stands out as a powerful and intuitive Gantt chart maker, particularly excelling in visual project planning. Its cornerstone feature is the Gantt chart, which provides a clear timeline view of tasks, dependencies, and project progress. This makes it especially useful for teams that need to visualize project timelines and track milestones.
Central features of GanttPRO are: User-friendly interface with drag-and-drop functionality
Resource management and workload tracking
Time and cost estimation tools
Collaboration features like task comments and file sharing
Integration with popular tools such as Slack, Google Drive, and Jira
GanttPRO is suitable for small to medium-sized teams across various industries. Most commonly users come from construction, software development, and marketing industries.
ProofHub
ProofHub positions itself as an all-in-one project management and team collaboration software. It aims to eliminate the need for multiple tools by providing a centralized platform for task management, file sharing, and team communication.
Standout features of ProofHub are: Kanban boards and Gantt charts for visual project management
Custom workflows and task dependencies
Time tracking and timesheets
Proofing tools for visual feedback on designs and documents
Discussion threads and chat for team communication
White-labeling options for client-facing projects
ProofHub's flexibility makes it a great match for creative agencies, marketing teams, and organizations aiming to simplify their project management workflows.
Redmine
Redmine is an open-source project management web application that offers a robust set of possibilities for issue tracking and project collaboration. Its flexibility and customization options make it a favorite among technical teams and organizations with specific workflow requirements.
Notable features of Redmine are: Multiple project support
Flexible role-based access control
Issue tracking system with custom fields
Time tracking and Gantt charts
Wiki and forum for each project
Repository integration (SVN, Git, Mercurial)
Although Redmine's interface may lack the sleek polish of some commercial alternatives, its real strength lies in its versatility. As an open-source platform, Redmine offers extensive customization through plugins, so it may be particularly appealing to organizations looking for a tailored PM solution without the hefty price tag.
Celoxis
Celoxis is a comprehensive project management and work collaboration platform that caters to businesses of all sizes. By offering a wide range of features that cover project planning, tracking, and reporting, it adapts very well to complex project environments.
Key strengths of Celoxis are: Advanced scheduling and resource management
Custom workflows and approval processes
Financial management tools including budgeting and expense tracking
including budgeting and expense tracking Business intelligence and interactive dashboards
Client portal for external stakeholder collaboration
Extensive integration capabilities with popular business tools
Celoxis stands out as an ideal solution for organizations juggling multiple projects at once, especially those with a strong focus on detailed financial tracking and reporting.
Linear
Linear is a modern project management tool designed with software development teams in mind. It focuses on providing a fast, intuitive interface for managing issues and workflows in an agile environment.
Essential characteristics of Linear are: Sleek, minimalist interface with keyboard shortcuts for efficiency
Customizable workflows and issue tracking
Roadmapping and cycle planning tools
Git integration for linking issues to code changes
Powerful search and filtering capabilities
API and webhooks for custom integrations
Linear's lightning-fast performance and developer-focused design make it an especially attractive option for software engineering teams and startups seeking a streamlined, no-nonsense project management solution.
Jira
Jira, developed by Atlassian, is one of the most widely used project management tools, especially in the software development industry. It offers robust features for agile project management, issue tracking, and workflow customization.
Notable aspects of Jira are: Flexible project views (Scrum and Kanban boards, roadmaps, timelines)
Customizable workflows and issue types
Powerful reporting and dashboards
Extensive integration ecosystem
Advanced search and JQL (Jira Query Language) for complex filtering
On-premise and cloud deployment options
While Jira's learning curve can be steep, its scalability and depth of features make it suitable for organizations of all sizes. However, those with complex project management needs will benefit the most.
Trello
Trello is known for its simplicity and visual approach to project management. Based on the Kanban methodology, it uses boards, lists, and cards to help teams organize and prioritize projects in a flexible, visual manner.
Principal features of Trello are: Intuitive drag-and-drop interface
Customizable boards and card templates
Checklists, due dates, and file attachments
Power-Ups for added functionality (calendars, voting, etc.)
Automation capabilities with Butler
Mobile apps for on-the-go project management
Trello's intuitive design and visual layout make it a perfect choice for small to medium-sized teams, personal projects, and collaborative efforts that thrive on a straightforward, board-based system.
Toggl Plan
Toggl Plan, formerly known as Teamweek, is a project planning tool that emphasizes simplicity and visual scheduling. It's designed to help teams plan projects, manage resources, and track progress with minimal complexity.
Toggl Plan's standout features are: Color-coded timelines for easy project visualization
Team workload management and capacity planning
Shareable project roadmaps
Task boards for detailed task management
Integrations with popular tools like Slack and Google Calendar
Time tracking capabilities (when used with Toggl Track)
Toggl Plan is an ideal fit for small to medium-sized teams seeking a simple, visually-driven project planning tool. It offers a clear, streamlined approach without the overwhelming complexity of more feature-packed alternatives.
Paymo
Paymo is an end-to-end project management solution that combines task management, time tracking, and invoicing in a single platform. This integration makes it especially useful for freelancers and small to medium-sized agencies that need to manage projects from start to finish, including billing.
Paymo's top characteristics are: Task lists and Kanban boards for task management
Gantt charts for project planning
for project planning Time tracking with desktop and mobile apps
Resource scheduling and workload management
Invoicing and expense tracking
Client portal for improved client collaboration
Paymo offers a holistic solution to project management by combining task organization with integrated financial tracking. That is why it can be fairly considered as an ideal choice for businesses aiming to manage every phase of their projects under one roof.
Agantty
Agantty is a free project management tool designed with simplicity in mind. This is what makes it an ideal choice for small teams and individuals who are just beginning their journey into the world of project management software.
Notable aspects of Agantty are: Gantt chart-based project planning
Task management with dependencies and milestones
Team collaboration features
Resource management and workload view
Time tracking capabilities
Completely free to use, with no limitations on users or projects
Agantty stands out thanks to simplicity and affordability. With that in mind, many startups, small businesses, and individuals choose it while seeking a no-frills project management solution.
nTask
nTask is a comprehensive project management tool that aims to cater to various project management methodologies and team sizes. It offers a wide range of features to help teams plan, collaborate, and execute projects efficiently.
Pivotal features of nTask are: Task management with custom fields and dependencies
Kanban boards and Gantt charts for visual project planning
Meeting management tools for agenda setting and minutes
Risk management and issue tracking
Time tracking and timesheet management
Team collaboration features including file sharing and comments
nTask's versatility makes it suitable for a wide range of industries and project types, from simple task management to complex project planning and execution.
How to make a choice?
The project management tool landscape is diverse with loads of solutions tailored to different team sizes, industries, and project complexities. When choosing a project management tool, consider factors such as your team's size, project complexity, required features, integration needs, and budget.
GanttPRO excels in visual project planning, while Redmine offers extensive customization for technical teams. Celoxis provides comprehensive features for complex project environments, and ProofHub aims to be an all-in-one solution for team collaboration. Linear caters specifically to software development teams with its sleek interface and developer-centric features.
Jira remains a powerhouse for large-scale and complex projects, particularly in software development. Trello offers simplicity and flexibility for various team sizes and project types. Toggl Plan focuses on visual scheduling and resource management, while Paymo integrates project management with time tracking and invoicing.
Agantty provides a free option for those just starting with project management tools, and nTask offers a comprehensive set of features suitable for various methodologies and team sizes.
Ultimately, the best project management tool for your team will depend on your specific needs, workflows, and preferences. Many of these tools offer free trials. It makes sense to experiment with a few options to find the one that best fits your organization's requirements.

title: Happenings in Hillcrest during Halloween month
description: What I love about Hillcrest is that there is always so much going on. This is a neighborhood full of active and passionate people— there is never a dull moment. Here's a glimpse of what is going on this month in Hillcrest. Uptown Community Planning Group The new Uptown Community…
content:
What I love about Hillcrest is that there is always so much going on. This is a neighborhood full of active and passionate people— there is never a dull moment. Here's a glimpse of what is going on this month in Hillcrest. Uptown Community Planning Group
The new Uptown Community Planning Group, which replaces the Uptown Planners as the area's advisory body to the City of San Diego on issues such as land use, development, and discretionary projects within the six Uptown neighborhoods, was finalizing its elections at the time I was writing my column for last month's edition. On Tuesday, Sept. 3, the results of the election were announced, which included Alberto Guaradado for the Hillcrest property owner seat and Isaac Warner for the Hillcrest renter seat. Benjamin Nicholls and Margit Whitlock were elected to Hillcrest business seats, and Anar Salayev was elected to the Hillcrest nonprofit seat, representing BikeSD.
For transparency, I was also elected to the board of the Uptown Community Planning Group, but my residential address is in University Heights, so I will proudly be serving in the renter seat dedicated to that neighborhood.
Community members had 24 hours to submit challenges to the election results, and several were filed, including challenges to the Hillcrest renter seat election, the Hillcrest nonprofit seat election, and the Hillcrest business seat that went to Benjamin Nicholls. At the time of this writing, I am unsure what will happen with these challenges as they will be handled at the board's first meeting, scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 1. I look forward to sharing more about how community members can engage with the board once these challenges are worked through.
You can learn more about the Uptown Community Planning Group at uptowncommunityplanning.org. Hillcrest Community Volunteer Patrol
Since this past summer, a small group of community members has held a couple of meetings to discuss the formation of a volunteer-led Hillcrest community patrol, in light of the dissolution of the Stonewall Citizens Patrol. The patrol's goal would be to bring an extra set of eyes and ears to the neighborhood and also to educate community members on how to report crime and other issues they need help with.
This volunteer patrol will not intervene in any situation and is not a force of 'mini-cops.' The goal is to be hands-off but create a presence that could possibly deter potential crime while making community members feel safer. With reports of increased hate incidents and crimes in the neighborhood, many community members have asked for something like this, and the group hopes to have something organized by early next year.
Plans are in the works for a 'Take Back the Night' type rally to officially launch the new patrol, with continued work to build the infrastructure and recruit volunteers. To be successful, the patrol will need a lot of volunteer support. If you are interested in learning more, please send me an email at [email protected] and I'll make sure you get out the email list to learn about the next meeting date and other activities. Nightmare on Normal Street
October is here and I couldn't be more excited! I absolutely love Halloween and spooky season. I can't wait for all the fun events that are in store. One of the largest Halloween parties in town happens right here in Hillcrest: Nightmare on Normal Street.
The Hillcrest Business Association (HBA) is thrilled to bring back Hillcrest's haunted Halloween dance party and costume competition on Saturday, Oct. 26, from 5-11 p.m. at Pride Plaza (located at Normal Street and University Ave). The event includes a night of live entertainment, a costume competition (for both furry friends and humans), monstrous bars, a haunted speakeasy, spooktacular vendors, non-stop dancing, and top-notch people-watching. HBA goes all out to produce Nightmare on Normal Street so it's one not to miss! Visit fabuloushillcrest.com for tickets. For families, the free Boo Bash by TransFamily Support Services will be held in the same space, on the same day, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. with tickets on Eventbrite. Hillcrest Community Ofrenda
In honor of Dia de los Muertos, Rick Cervantes and @HillcrestSanDiego will present the third annual Hillcrest Community Ofrenda from Tuesday, Oct. 29 to Thursday, Oct. 31, also around the Hillcrest Pride Flag. Rick started this annual tribute at his home to honor his brother, who was murdered in 2016, and in 2022, he decided to merge his Latino and LGBT cultures by creating an ofrenda that everyone could contribute to. The ofrenda will be open 24 hours a day during the three days it is up, with a team of volunteers keeping it secure at all hours. All community members are welcome to come place photos or items at the ofrenda at any time, or just come and visit. Pan dulce will be served as well. Visit @HillcrestSanDiego on Instagram for more information. Hillcrest's Most Famous Murderess
Longtime San Diegans could never forget the name Betty Broderick, the divorcee who murdered her ex-husband and his new wife at their Hillcrest home on Cypress Street in 1989. Broderick, who remains imprisoned to this day at the California Institution for Women in Chino, Calif., has been the subject of numerous documentaries, films, and made-for-TV movies, some of higher quality than others.
San Diego's fabulous Jazmyn Glam is hosting a fun show at Urban Mo's on Friday, Oct. 11, called 'Murder On The Dancefloor – A Night of True Crime & Killer Cocktails: The Betty Broderick Story.' Jazmyn is a true crime buff and is putting a lot of work into making this an intriguing but really fun show. You don't want to miss it! Visit urbanmos.com for tickets. title: 5 Essay Writing Strategies for Humanities Students
author: Grhics Tech
description: Essay writing is a fundamental skill for humanities students. Whether you're studying literature, history, philosophy, or any other humanities discipline, the ability to communicate your ideas clearly…
content:
Essay writing is a fundamental skill for humanities students. Whether you're studying literature, history, philosophy, or any other humanities discipline, the ability to communicate your ideas clearly and persuasively in writing is essential. For students struggling with these demands, seeking essay help can be invaluable.
Professional essay help services provide guidance in developing coherent arguments, structuring essays, and refining analytical skills. Unlike subjects that rely heavily on quantitative analysis or experimentation, humanities disciplines focus on argumentation, critical thinking, and interpretation. This requires students to craft well-structured essays that not only present information but also analyze, interpret, and engage with complex ideas. Essay help can support students in mastering these tasks, allowing them to better express their thoughts and ideas.
Here are five essential essay writing strategies for humanities students to help you improve your writing, develop persuasive arguments, and excel in your coursework.
Formulate an Effective Thesis Statement
A practical humanities essay relies on having a clearly stated thesis statement. Your thesis must state your main argument or interpretation for your entire essay and, in particular, in relation to texts, historical events, philosophical concepts, or cultural phenomena analyzed within its body – thus, your thesis must present specific viewpoints or arguments that speak back directly to its prompt.
Before writing your essay, take time to brainstorm and consider your prompt carefully. After creating a potential thesis statement, test it by asking whether it is specific, arguable, and supported by evidence from the text/subject matter you're studying – for instance, instead of saying: 'Shakespeare's Hamlet is an intricate play,' try writing instead: 'In Hamlet by Shakespeare uses madness as a symbol for political instability that illuminates Elizabethan court politics.'
Provide Evidence to Support Your Argument
Humanities essays require supporting your argument with textual evidence, examples, and quotations that back it up. When writing about literature, historical events, or philosophical theory – be they novels, historical events, or theories – concrete evidence should demonstrate your point and back it up with quotes and quotations to prove it.
Make sure that the evidence selected directly supports your thesis statement. Avoid simply summarizing or providing too much description without analysis – interpret evidence and show its connection to supporting arguments; for instance, if writing about isolation as seen in *Frankenstein* don't just describe Victor Frankenstein's loneliness–instead, show how this contributes to his demise while reflecting larger Romantic ideals of individualism and alienation.
Create a Clear and Logical Structure
An effective essay structure ensures your ideas flow logically and that your argument can quickly be followed. Humanities essays often cover complex subjects with subtle arguments; therefore it's vitally important that they're organized so they build from point to point in an intuitive fashion.
Follow a standard essay structure of introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion. Your introduction should introduce your thesis and provide an overview of your argument; each body paragraph should focus on one idea that supports it with clear topic sentences stating its main point; the conclusion should round off this sequence by summarizing key points and restating the significance of the argument.
Analyze, Don't Just Describe
One of the greatest mistakes humanities students make in essay writing is succumbing to summarization or description without genuinely engaging the subject matter. While context should always be provided, essays written for humanities students should go beyond simply summarizing material by providing deeper analyses that interpret its significance and meaning.
Ask critical questions about any text or topic you're discussing, from historical events to novels; instead of simply detailing their events and actions, analyze their causes, consequences, and significance from different angles; seek different perspectives; query assumptions; investigate contradictions or tensions within material if applicable; rather than simply outlining actions taken by characters within fiction novels merely describe motivations relationships themes represented while always connecting your analysis back to your thesis statement.
Revision and Proofread
No essay can be complete on its initial draft; revising and proofreading are vital steps in crafting an attractive, coherent final paper. A first draft serves to capture thoughts; revision allows you to refine arguments, increase clarity, and eliminate errors from your essay.
Revision will ensure your essay is logically organized, well-argued, and free from inconsistencies or unclear ideas. Proofreading removes grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors that might compromise its professionalism or affect its grade.
Once you've completed a first draft, take some time off before revising it to gain fresh perspective and spot areas which need improvement more readily. When revising, keep this big picture in mind: does your argument make sense, are your ideas presented clearly, does each paragraph support your thesis statement etc.
Once satisfied with the structure and content, move on to proofreading. Look out for grammar/punctuation errors, awkward sentences, and typos; reading your essay aloud may help detect mistakes you would miss when reading silently.
Writing essays in the humanities involves more than simply placing words onto paper; it demands critical thought, analysis, and an in-depth engagement with its subject matter. By formulating an engaging thesis statement and using evidence persuasively, maintaining an uncluttered structure, prioritizing analysis over revision, and revising in-depth, you can produce compelling essays that demonstrate your ability to think critically while convincingly arguing your case – strategies that not only will help you thrive in humanities classes but will also hone and enhance overall writing abilities – invaluable both academically and professional settings alike!

title: Boys to Men Mentoring celebrates Crystal Anniversary of 100 Wave Challenge, raising $270,000
description: Spring Valley-based Boys to Men Mentoring (B2M) celebrated its 15th Annual 100 Wave Challenge in late September at Mission Beach.
content:
Spring Valley-based Boys to Men Mentoring (B2M) celebrated its 15th Annual 100 Wave Challenge in late September at Mission Beach.
This year marked the Crystal Anniversary of the surf-a-thon, an event that began in 2009, challenging surfers of all skill levels to catch 100 waves in a single day while raising funds to support B2M's in-school mentoring programs throughout San Diego County.
This year, the event raised an astounding $270,000, moving B2M closer to its vision of providing mentorship in every middle and high school in San Diego.
'The 100 Wave Challenge works so well because we offer surfers a chance to integrate their passion for surfing with a purpose that is transforming the lives of young men struggling to become the good men they want to be,' said Co-founder Joe Sigurdson. 'Matching passion with purpose makes it easy to say yes to the Challenge and inspire those around us to say yes to supporting us.'
Executive Director Rose Courtney echoed Sigurdson's sentiments, adding: 'Our Crystal Anniversary not only represents 15 years of surfing for a great cause — but also our clarity and commitment to expanding our programs into more schools. We're incredibly grateful to our generous sponsors, surfers, volunteers, and the community for helping us reach this milestone.'
Sponsors like Kaiser Permanente, Dr. Bronner's, and Molly's Angels Foundation played a role in the event's success. Local surf legends Bird Huffman of Bird's Surf Shed and Joe Roper also lent their support, paying heartfelt tributes and emphasizing the importance of B2M's mission.
A special highlight of the event was the presentation of the One Drop Award to local real estate broker Dane Soderberg for his dedication to Boys to Men Mentoring. Soderberg, who has supported B2M for nearly a decade, recently hosted a BBQ to introduce the mission to his family and friends, inspiring others to get involved.
More than just a physical challenge, the 100 Wave Challenge embodies the spirit of community, purpose, and support for the next generation.
While the event has concluded, the opportunity to make waves of impact continues. Fundraising remains open until Oct. 31, giving the community more time to contribute and help Boys to Men Mentoring reach even more boys across San Diego.
To make a donation or learn more about Boys to Men Mentoring and the 100 Wave Challenge, visit boystomen.org .

title: Bathing Bliss: How to Create a Spa-Like Experience at Home
author: Grhics Tech
description: Imagine sinking into warm, fragrant baths, surrounded by soft candlelight and the soothing sounds of nature. Sounds like a luxurious spa experience, right? But what if you could recreate this blissful atmosphere in the comfort of your own home? With a few simple tweaks and thoughtful design choices, you can…
content:
Imagine sinking into warm, fragrant baths , surrounded by soft candlelight and the soothing sounds of nature. Sounds like a luxurious spa experience, right? But what if you could recreate this blissful atmosphere in the comfort of your own home? With a few simple tweaks and thoughtful design choices, you can transform your bathroom into a serene retreat that will leave you feeling pampered and relaxed. Start with Soothing Colors
When it comes to creating a spa-like ambiance , color plays a crucial role. Soft, calming hues can instantly transport you to a state of relaxation. Consider painting your bathroom walls a gentle shade of blue, green, or neutral beige. These colors have a proven track record of promoting relaxation and reducing stress. If you're not ready to commit to a full paint job, add some calming accents like a blue-tiled backsplash or a greenery-filled planter. Lighting: The Key to Ambiance
Lighting can make or break the ambiance of your bathroom. Harsh overhead lights can be jarring and uninviting, while soft, warm lighting can create a cozy and intimate atmosphere. Consider installing dimmer switches or using table lamps to create pools of warm light. Candles are also a great option – just be sure to place them safely out of reach of water. Indulge in Luxurious Textiles
There's nothing quite like wrapping yourself in a plush towel after a warm bath. Invest in some luxurious textiles like Egyptian cotton towels, a soft bath mat, and a cozy robe. These small indulgences can make a big difference in your bathing experience. Bring in Nature
Nature has a way of calming the mind and soothing the soul. Bring the outdoors in by adding some natural elements to your bathroom. A vase of fresh flowers, a potted plant, or even a bowl of river rocks can create a sense of serenity. If you're feeling adventurous, consider installing a living wall or a vertical garden. Sensory Delights
Our senses play a huge role in our relaxation experience. Consider adding some sensory delights like essential oils, scented candles, or a sound machine to create a multi-sensory experience. Lavender and vanilla are popular choices for promoting relaxation, while the sound of rain or ocean waves can be incredibly calming. Invest in a Comforting Bathtub
Let's face it – the bathtub is the star of the show when it comes to creating a spa-like experience. Invest in a comfortable, ergonomic tub that invites you to linger. Consider adding some indulgent accessories like a bath pillow, a set of scented bath salts, or a good book. Make it Tech-Friendly
In today's fast-paced world, it's easy to get caught up in our devices. But when it comes to creating a spa-like experience, it's all about disconnecting. Consider installing a waterproof Bluetooth speaker or a tablet holder to stream your favorite relaxing tunes or nature sounds. Add Some Visual Interest
A spa-like bathroom should be visually appealing, too. Consider adding some decorative elements like a statement piece of art, a colorful rug, or a beautiful vase. These small touches can add a lot of personality to your space. Create a Calming Routine
Finally, it's all about creating a calming routine that signals to your brain that it's time to relax. Consider setting aside some time each day to unwind in your bathroom oasis. Whether it's reading a book, taking a warm bath, or simply enjoying some quiet time, make it a ritual that you look forward to.
In conclusion, creating a spa-like experience at home is all about attention to detail and a willingness to indulge in some luxurious treats. By incorporating soothing colors, soft lighting, and natural elements, you can transform your bathroom into a serene retreat that will leave you feeling pampered and relaxed. So go ahead, take a deep breath, and let the bathing bliss begin!

title: Choosing the Right Framework for Risk Management Success

content:
In business, understanding and managing uncertainties is a critical skill that every organization must master. However, choosing the right framework for effective management can be overwhelming. With a multitude of options available, each designed to handle different types of challenges and organizational needs, it's essential to select one that aligns with your strategic objectives and operational realities.
Selecting the right frameworks for risk management involves understanding your organization's unique needs, evaluating various options, and aligning the chosen approach with your overall business strategy. This article lays down the major variables to consider when adopting a management framework, analyzes the differences between strategic and operational issues, and underlines the necessity of aligning your management efforts with your overall company goals.
Understanding Risk Management Frameworks
It is more than just a set of guidelines—it's a comprehensive approach that helps organizations identify, assess, and mitigate challenges. While some businesses focus solely on strategic uncertainties, such as market trends and competitive dynamics, others may prioritize operational considerations, which include internal processes, employee actions, and day-to-day functions. Choosing the right one means evaluating your organization's profile, industry landscape, and specific objectives. An effective framework not only identifies and mitigates potential pitfalls but also boosts overall business performance.
Strategic Risk And Operational Risk
One of the most fundamental distinctions in management is between strategic and operational issues. Understanding these two categories is essential in the process of selection: Strategic Challenges : These are serious hazards that might make it more difficult for a business to meet its long-term objectives. These often stem from external factors such as economic shifts, regulatory changes, or evolving market conditions. Managing them requires a forward-looking approach that aligns efforts with strategic planning.

Operational Challenges: These are connected to an organization's daily activities and internal procedures. They might involve everything from supply chain interruptions and compliance problems to human error, equipment malfunctions, or system failures. Operational hazards can directly affect an organization's capacity to perform its duties and are more urgent.
Choosing the right framework depends on whether your organization is more concerned with strategic or operational challenges, or both. Some frameworks are designed specifically to address high-level strategic concerns, while others are better suited for managing the complexities of operational issues.
Key Considerations When Choosing a Framework for Risk Management Organizational Objectives and Strategy : The first step is to understand your organization's strategic objectives. A scalable and flexible framework will allow you to adjust your strategy as your organization grows or as new challenges emerge.

Aligning Risk Management with Organizational Strategy
A management framework should be integrated into the overall business strategy, not operate in isolation. This alignment ensures that management goes beyond compliance to enable the organization to seize opportunities and achieve strategic goals. When fully integrated, it fosters a proactive culture where potential issues are anticipated and prioritized, leading to better decision-making across the organization.
Leveraging Technology to Support Risk Management
Technology plays a crucial role in supporting management frameworks. Modern technologies may offer real-time insights, increase detection of potential issues, and strengthen overall response capabilities. These capabilities range from automation and data analytics to artificial intelligence.
Many organizations are turning to management software solutions to streamline their processes. These tools can help automate assessments, monitor key indicators, and provide a centralized platform for managing across the organization. By utilizing technology, organizations may guarantee the effectiveness and efficiency of their framework.
The Role of Advisory Services in Framework Selection
Selecting an appropriate management framework may be difficult, particularly for businesses that are new to structured management or are involved in highly regulated sectors of the economy. Advisory services can provide valuable guidance in selecting and implementing a framework that aligns with your organization's unique needs. Organizations may learn about market trends, acquire insights into best practices, and successfully negotiate the challenges of adopting a framework by collaborating with seasoned experts. By working together, it is ensured that the structure selected will fulfill present requirements while also being flexible enough to accommodate future expansion.
Selecting the best frameworks for risk management success necessitates a thorough comprehension of the operational and strategic objectives of your company. It's not a one-size-fits-all approach; rather, it involves evaluating different frameworks and selecting one that aligns with your business strategy, industry standards, and appetite for challenges. Whether you opt for COSO or another framework, the key is to ensure that your chosen framework supports proactive management and drives business success.

title: Grossmont High math teacher earns California's top teaching honor
description: State Superintendent of Instruction Tony Thurmond announced recently that Grossmont High School Math teacher Kristen LoPrell has been named one of five California Teachers of the Year.
content:
State Superintendent of Instruction Tony Thurmond announced recently that Grossmont High School math teacher Kristen LoPrell has been named one of five California Teachers of the Year.
LoPrell has served as a Grossmont High School (GHS) m ath teacher since 2015 and currently serves as Math Department Chair. She has served as an academic league coach, freshman orientation leader, and math coach. She has also updated course pathways to provide access to all levels of honors math for all students.
As an adjunct professor at Point Loma Nazarene University, where she earned both her Bachelor of Science in Math and Master of Teaching degrees, she taught courses in research methods and best practices for statistical analysis and also guided new teachers in math practices, classroom management, and instruction.
'Over Kristen LoPrell's remarkable career, she has helped countless Grossmont High School students discover the beauty of mathematics,' said GUHSD Superintendent Mike Fowler. 'She is an outstanding educator whose dedication to ensuring every student has a path to success is demonstrated by her fierce commitment to improving instructional practices and the many students who have testified to the influence she has had on their lives,' he added.
'This is the honor of my career,' LoPrell said. 'Teaching mathematics is pure joy for me. My students make my days brighter and helping them realize they can do math is my favorite,' she added.
According to the California Department of Education (CDE), the California Teachers of the Year Program, which is supported by the California Teachers of the Year Foundation, began in 1972 to honor outstanding teachers and encourage and inspire new teachers to enter the profession.
County offices of education nominate California Teachers of the Year applicants through their county-level competitions.
The CDE selection committees review applications, evaluate teachers' rapport with students, classroom environments, presentation skills, and teaching techniques, and interview the teachers. The State Superintendent of Public Instruction then selects the five California Teachers of the Year and the National Teacher of the Year nominee.

title: Cheers to 80 years: Everybody knows your name at Hob Nob Hill
description: Located at 2271 First Avenue, the Hob Nob Hill Restaurant has been serving San Diego since 1944 thanks to a loyal fanbase. Many frequent diners say 'The Hob' reminds them of 1980s sitcom 'Cheers.' 'This place is like 'Cheers' because they always know my name,' says 76-year old Kathy Kinkade.…
content:
Located at 2271 First Avenue, the Hob Nob Hill Restaurant has been serving San Diego since 1944 thanks to a loyal fanbase. Many frequent diners say 'The Hob' reminds them of 1980s sitcom 'Cheers.' Kathy Kinkade recommends the coffee cake for those new to Hob Nob Hill. (Photos by Terry L. Wilson)
' This place is like 'Cheers' because they always know my name,' says 76-year old Kathy Kinkade. 'I guess my husband and I have been coming here, mostly for breakfast, for 18 years. We really like the coffee cake; when my husband travels overseas, he will order an entire Blackberry Coffee cake to take with him, and he will eat the whole thing himself!'
' The Hob' has its own cast of characters — each with their own reason for coming back, again and again. For Ed Hearn, President of Vista City High School, a trip to Hob Nob Hill is about keeping the memory of an old friend alive. A standing customer, Ed Hearn, outlived the friend who originally brought him to Hob Nob Hill every Friday for lunch. He still visits to remember his friend over a scrumptious meal.
' I've been coming here for 18 years,' said Hearn. 'Every Friday I had lunch with my dear friend, Julius Zolezzi, and we would sit at the same table, facing each other and talk about life. I learned about the history of San Diego, and the history of the Hob Nob, sitting right here with my friend. Julius was in his 90s when he died. Every time I walk into the Hob Knob I think about him. So yes, the Hob Knob is a very special place for me.' Wayne Jenkins celebrated his 82nd birthday at The Hob.
Another main cast member, Wayne Jenkins, has a backstory fit for Hollywood – and a t 6'4', the frame to match. Jenkins was a pilot and SWAT team member, plus he ran around with the Rat Pack.
' I owned a Rolls Royce repair shop in Palm Springs, that's how I met Sinatra,' said Jenkins. 'He was a nice guy; he sent his plane to fly me and my wife to his concerts. And me and Steve McQueen used to race motorcycles in Baja. I always let him win.'
Jenkins recently celebrated his 82nd birthday at his favorite hangout. ' I love this place,' said Jenkins. 'I think the staff is great, they really make me feel welcome and I wouldn't celebrate my birthday anywhere else.'
For those familiar with San Diego's demographics, it should come as no surprise that many service members eat at Hob Nob Hill . However, what may be surprising is their service record. There is no telling who might be sitting in the next booth. Pull up a chair with 97-year-old Bob Allan to hear about his service in World War II.
' I served in the Navy in World War II and Korea in the '50s,' said 97-year old Bob Allan. 'I've been in San Diego for about 60 or so years now. I come to the Hob Nob all the time; it's a great place to watch people. Have you ever seen that show, 'Cheers'? The Hob Nob is a lot like that.'
Serving up classic American comfort food, its the clientele and staff as much as the food that makes Hob Nob Hill a keystone for many nostalgic San Diegans shaping their community. Tags: bankers hillfood and drinkhob nob hill
