title: San Diego man pleads guilty in federal case that killed pair of North Park residents
description: A San Diego man has pleaded guilty to distributing fentanyl in a federal case in which two No
content:
A San Diego man has pleaded guilty to distributing fentanyl in a federal case in which two North Park residents were found dead on the floor in which the defendant also overdosed but was revived.
San Diego Police officers responded to a 911 call to a North Park residence at 6 a.m. on Nov. 10, 2022 and they found four people lying on the floor of a bedroom.
Police and investigators from the Drug Enforcement Administration were able to revive Scott Anthony Sargent, 63, and another person with Narcan, and they were transported to a hospital, where they recovered.
Sargent appeared Jan. 14 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Allison Goddard and pleaded guilty to 'knowingly and intentionally' distributing fentanyl. Charges that he caused the deaths of the two men, who were only identified in court records as Z.W. and M.L., will be dismissed at the sentencing.
Sentencing was set for April 4 before U.S. District Court Judge Robert Huie. Sargent remains detained without bail in the Metropolitan Correctional Center.
Sargent faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison and a $1 million fine, according to court records. He may be subject to restitution of $15,926 to the family of M.L., and $3,597 to the family of Z.W., records say.
A search of Sargent's backpack and duffel bag at the scene showed the mixture of fentanyl and para-fluorfentanyl. Investigators also searched Sargent's storage unit and discovered additional baggies containing the same type of mixture, according to the U.S. Attorney's office.
'Fentanyl kills indiscriminately,' said U.S. Attorney Tara McGrath in a news release at the time of his arrest in April, 2024. 'Investigators will leave no stone unturned in the effort to identify and charge distributors of this poison.'
Also to be dismissed is a conspiracy charge that alleges Sargent distributed the drug with others. Sargent is the only person charged.
It was Goddard who signed a detention order remanding Sargent without bail on the grounds that he was a danger to the public and was a flight risk, according to court records.
Sargent was in possession of a firearm at the scene of the deaths and had five prior felony convictions since 2006, the magistrate noted.
Photo credit: Pixabay.com Tags: fentanylNorth ParkScott Anthony Sargent

title: Bail set for Point Loma man charged with attempted murder of cop
description: A judge on Jan. 27 set bail at $1 million for a Point Loma man who is charged with attempted murder of a San Diego police officer whose leg was broken when he was struck by the man's car. Officer…
content:
A judge on Jan. 27 set bail at $1 million for a Point Loma man who is charged with attempted murder of a San Diego police officer whose leg was broken when he was struck by the man's car.
Officer Matthew Salisbury was walking up the driveway of the man's house on Jan. 23 on Inez Street in response to the 911 call by the man's wife who told police her husband had just cut her fingers with a knife and beat her.
Deputy District Attorney Spencer Sharpe asked for the $1 million bail, saying William Woodward Stephens, 65, 'targeted the officer' and drove his Jeep Wrangler in reverse from the garage, hitting him.
Sharpe said the officer had surgery Monday and will have another surgery later as he has 'several broken bones.' He was still in the hospital on Monday.
Sharpe told San Diego Superior Court Judge Euketa L. Oliver that Stephens discovered he had lost a good job offer recently and began to drink alcohol. He became violent, punched his wife's head, and cut her fingers with a knife, he said.
A Feb. 7 preliminary hearing was set, but it probably will be delayed.
Stephens pleaded not guilty to all charges, which include attempted murder of a peace officer and inflicting great bodily injury in the process. He is also charged with assault with a deadly weapon(which is the Jeep Wrangler), and resisting arrest.
Additionally, Stephens is accused of inflicting corporal injury to Sally Stephens, his wife, felony assault, and attempting to dissuade a witness from reporting a crime.
Sharpe filed a criminal protective order against Stephens that bars him from contacting his wife, her sister, and the officer by telephone, social media, mail, or in person, should he be able to post bail.
Sharpe said the attempted murder charge on an officer carries a life sentence in prison if he is convicted. He remains in the central jail.

title: Chucky Lozano scores first goal for SDFC
description: After much anticipation from local soccer fans, Irving Chucky Lozano made his first appearance on the pitch with his new San Diego FC teammates during the inaugural pre-season preparation match…
content:
After much anticipation from local soccer fans, Irving Chucky Lozano made his first appearance on the pitch with his new San Diego FC teammates during the inaugural pre-season preparation match against USL Championship side Phoenix Rising on Saturday.
The closed-door meeting saw SDFC come out victorious 2-0 with the other goal coming from forward Marcus Ingvartsen. The Rising set foot in San Diego for the first time since defeating SD Loyal 4-3 in the USL Championship quarterfinals at Torero Stadium.
Lozano officially arrived in San Diego on June 10 to the cheers and applause of the waiting fans having signed with the club on June 6 to a four-year contract through 2028 making him the first Designated Player in the history of the club. He started his professional career with Liga MX side Pachuca and most recently with Eredivisie club PSV Eindhoven.
He made 70 appearances with the senior Mexican national team including his most famous appearance on June 17, 2018, in the opening round of the World Cup when El Tri defeated then defending champion Germany. The goal, which came in the 35th minute, caused the ground to shake and set off seismic sensors in Mexico City due to the celebration that ensued, according to experts.
Besides winning championships with PSV Eindhoven, Lozano has also lifted the league title with Napoli in Italy and with Pachuca of Liga MX. Among his many accolades are being named CONCACAF Men's Player of the Year in 2018 and the best eleven in 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2021.
SDFC will be playing in the upcoming Coachella Valley Invitational versus NYC FC on Feb. 8, followed by the Portland Timbers on Feb. 12 and N.Y. Red Bulls on Feb. 15 as part of its preseason preparations.

title: Crush Your Social Media Goals: Top Ways to Expand Your Accounts in 2025
author: Graphics Tech
description: Social media is no longer just a tool for connecting with friends and family; it's a crit
content:
Social media is no longer just a tool for connecting with friends and family; it's a critical asset for personal and professional growth. As we enter 2025, social media continues to evolve, with new trends, features, and platforms emerging. To succeed in this dynamic landscape, you must not only keep up with these changes but also strategically grow your accounts. This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to expand your social media presence in 2025, offering actionable strategies to help you crush your goals. Understanding Your Social Media Goals
Before diving into specific strategies, it's essential to understand the importance of setting clear, measurable social media goals. Simply wanting to 'grow your followers' or 'gain more engagement' isn't enough. You need to define what success looks like for you. Setting SMART goals—specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound—is key to maintaining focus and tracking progress. For instance, your goal might be to increase Instagram engagement by 20% over the next three months by posting high-quality content and engaging more with your followers.
Your goals should also align with your larger personal or business objectives. Whether you're an influencer looking to build your brand, a small business aiming to increase sales, or an individual hoping to connect with like-minded people, your social media strategy must serve your broader goals. Understanding why you're on social media in the first place will help you refine your strategies and prioritize the efforts that will lead to the most significant impact.
While growing an organic following is the ultimate goal, some people choose to buy TikTok followers to give their accounts an initial boost. However, it's important to approach this tactic carefully, as it can be a double-edged sword. While a higher follower count might help with credibility, sustainable growth is achieved through genuine engagement and consistent content creation. Harnessing the Power of Emerging Platforms
The social media landscape is constantly changing, and platforms rise and fall in popularity. As we head into 2025, it's crucial to stay ahead of the curve and identify the next big social media trends. While giants like Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter still dominate, new platforms and features are continuously capturing attention. TikTok, for example, revolutionized short-form video content and continues to grow in popularity. Similarly, platforms like BeReal or newer niche networks are offering unique ways to engage with users.
By exploring these emerging platforms, you can tap into new audiences before they become oversaturated. Being an early adopter allows you to build a dedicated following and establish yourself or your brand as a leader in a specific niche. For instance, BeReal focuses on authenticity, and leveraging this platform might allow you to connect with younger audiences who value transparency and genuine interaction over polished content.
In addition to exploring new platforms, it's important to pay attention to changes and updates in existing platforms. Instagram's shift toward more video-based content, for example, means that users should focus on producing engaging video content to stay relevant. Keeping an eye on trends will help you stay adaptable and position your account for success in 2025. Mastering Content Creation
Content remains king in the world of social media. Without high-quality, engaging content, growing your following will be an uphill battle. In 2025, creating visual content that captures attention is more important than ever. Whether you're posting on Instagram, TikTok, or even LinkedIn, the images, videos, and infographics you share must be visually appealing and shareable.
Video content, in particular, continues to dominate social media. Platforms like Instagram Reels and TikTok are built for short, entertaining videos, and users expect to see content that grabs their attention quickly. But visuals alone aren't enough. Storytelling is a crucial aspect of engaging your audience. People connect with stories on a deeper level, and sharing your brand's or personal story can foster a stronger emotional connection with your followers. Optimizing Your Social Media Profiles
When it comes to social media, first impressions matter. Your profile is often the first thing potential followers will see, and it should convey who you are, what you stand for, and what followers can expect from your content. A well-crafted bio and a professional profile picture are essential. Your bio should be concise yet informative, giving visitors a reason to follow you. Use keywords relevant to your niche and include a call-to-action (CTA), whether it's visiting your website, checking out your latest post, or signing up for your newsletter.
The profile picture is another critical element. Whether it's a personal photo or a company logo, it should be clear and represent your brand accurately. It's the visual cue that will help people recognize you across different platforms. Conclusion
Expanding your social media presence in 2025 requires a combination of strategy, creativity, and consistency. By setting clear goals, embracing emerging platforms, mastering content creation, and engaging with your audience, you'll be well on your way to growing your accounts. Remember, success on social media doesn't happen overnight. It takes time, effort, and adaptation to the ever-changing landscape. Stay authentic, stay consistent, and most importantly, stay engaged with your followers. The rewards will follow as you continue to crush your social media goals.

title: What to Do After Long-Term Exposure to Workplace Hazards
author: Graphics Tech
description: Prolonged exposure to hazards at work can cause severe and lasting harm to your health, even when symptoms take years to develop. Toxic chemicals, repetitive strain, and hazardous environments all create chronic diseases that could affect your daily life and work performance. The earlier the identification of risks, the better…
content:
Prolonged exposure to hazards at work can cause severe and lasting harm to your health, even when symptoms take years to develop. Toxic chemicals, repetitive strain, and hazardous environments all create chronic diseases that could affect your daily life and work performance. The earlier the identification of risks, the better the medical interventions and financial securities one gets.
By being proactive in terms of medical care and cognizance of your legal rights, you will be protected and get the help you need. Here are critical steps to take when exposed to a workplace hazard over a long term.
Get a Comprehensive Medical Examination
Chronic exposure to hazards at work can result in illnesses whose symptoms do not manifest immediately, making regular checkups vital. A thorough examination may uncover the early stages of diseases resulting from toxic chemicals, repetition strain, and bad conditions in the workplace.
Lung function tests, blood screenings, and even imaging tests are all part of the diagnoses physicians will go through to find the damage done to the body over time. Keeping good medical records links your health to your workplace conditions. If your condition worsens, early symptoms and medical checkups will help back up your claims for compensation and treatment.
Seek Legal Advice
If your illness results from prolonged exposure to hazardous workplace conditions, legal action may be necessary to secure compensation beyond what workers' compensation provides. Certain cases, such as exposure to asbestos, may involve lawsuits against negligent employers or third-party manufacturers of hazardous materials.
Individuals diagnosed with mesothelioma due to asbestos exposure in states like California need to approach law firms dealing with occupational illness cases. A competent California mesothelioma lawyer will be helpful in complicated litigation, evidence collection, and the fight for due compensation to cover the cost of treatment and long-term care.
Notify Your Employer and Document Everything
Many companies have procedures to respond to workplace health concerns, and your report can trigger workplace safety reviews or regulatory inspections. Failure to report promptly may affect your right to claim workers' compensation or other benefits.
Maintain a record of your work conditions with photographs, coworker testimony, and communication regarding safety concerns to supervisors. Keeping detailed records of your symptoms, visits to doctors, and incidents at work may be the most important part of building any case for seeking compensation later.
Explore Workers' Compensation and Benefits
Many states permit the benefit of workers' compensation if a worker has contracted diseases because of working in certain workplaces. The benefits shall compensate for medical expenses, wages lost during the sickness or injury period, and expenses related to re-establishing employment.
The procedure for compensation filling is tedious as some employers and insurance companies also try to dismiss or decrease the substantial amounts in the payout. It is important that you understand your rights under workers' compensation laws. Seeking the help of a professional may become necessary to file your claim properly and claim the entitled benefits.
Advocating Improvement in Workplace Safety
Taking action against long-term exposure to hazards saves you and can help protect others. Reports on safety violations to organizations such as the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) ensure that workplaces are inspected and measures taken to avert employee harm.
If you are part of a labor union or employee advocacy group, inform them about the workplace hazards that can trigger your employer's implementation of safety policies. Workers have a right to safety in the workplace, and voicing concern about safety helps further create a healthy and safe workforce.
Endnote
Workplace hazards have the potential to lead to serious complications with exposure over long periods, so taking action early is very important. Seeking medical care, reporting your concerns, and being knowledgeable about your rights will help you take care of your health and protect your financial future. Consult professionals, such as a specialist attorney, to get all the compensation and benefits you deserve.

title: Councilmember Elo-Rivera selected as chair of the San Diego Workforce Partnership Policy Board
description: Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera has been selected to serve as chair of the Policy Board of the San Diego Workforce Partnership, the region's leading organization dedicated to workforce development,…
content:
Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera has been selected to serve as chair of the Policy Board of the San Diego Workforce Partnership, the region's leading organization dedicated to workforce development, economic mobility, and equal opportunity.
As Chair, Elo-Rivera will bring a commitment to economic justice to the forefront of efforts to ensure every San Diegan—regardless of background, zip code, or income—has access to good jobs, fair wages, and a pathway to fulfill their potential.
'San Diego's economy is only as strong as the working people who keep it moving,' said Elo-Rivera, District 9. 'For too long, economic opportunity has been reserved for too few, while too many are forced to work multiple jobs just to survive. That's unacceptable. As Chair of the Policy Board, I will fight for a fairer, more inclusive economy—one where workers are respected, wages reflect the true cost of living, and everyone has a real shot at success.'
Elo-Rivera's leadership comes at a time when San Diego is facing an affordability crisis, growing income inequality, and uncertainty about how Federal actions may impact our binational economy.
Under his guidance, the San Diego Workforce Partnership will expand efforts to:
· Strengthen workforce training programs that connect workers—especially those from historically marginalized communities—to good-paying, high-quality jobs and careers.
· Ensure public investments in job training and education prioritize those who need it the most, including young people, immigrants, and those reentering the workforce.
· Partner with local businesses and labor unions to create stronger career pathways that lead to stable employment and long-term financial security.
· Fight for policies that put working people first, ensuring that every worker is paid fairly, treated with dignity, and given a fair shot at success.
Elo-Rivera is succeeding County Supervisor Monica Montgomery-Steppe as Chair and expressed appreciation for the Supervisor's leadership. 'Supervisor Montgomery-Steppe skillfully guided the Workforce Partnership through multiple challenges without ever losing sight of the mission,' Elo-Rivera said. 'I am incredibly appreciative of her leadership in positioning the Workforce Partnership for its most impactful chapter. I am grateful for her vote of confidence and the confidence of my colleagues in selecting me as Chair.'
Elo-Rivera represents San Diego's Ninth Council District including communities of City Heights, College Area, El Cerrito, Kensington, Mission Valley East, Mountain View, Mt. Hope, Normal Heights, Rolando Village, Rolando Park, Stockton and Talmadge. He is the chair of the Environment Committee and the Select Committee on Addressing Cost of Living.

title: What Are the Steps to Take If the Insurance Company Offers a Low Settlement?
author: Graphics Tech
description: When filing a personal injury claim, you expect a fair settlement covering your damages. However, many insurance compani
content:
When filing a personal injury claim, you expect a fair settlement covering your damages. However, many insurance companies initiate with a low offer, hoping you'll accept less than deserved. If this occurs, don't feel pressured to settle immediately. Instead, take steps to negotiate a better offer and safeguard your rights.
This may involve counteroffers, evidence submission, and potentially seeking professional legal guidance to ensure you receive just compensation. Why Do Insurance Companies Offer Low Settlements?
Insurance companies often start with a low settlement offer to see if they can close the case quickly and save money. This initial offer might cover some of your medical expenses, but it typically won't account for all current and future damages, such as lost wages, ongoing medical treatment, pain and suffering, and other related costs.
It's important to assess the offer critically. Accepting a low settlement means you may not have the chance to claim more compensation later. Therefore, knowing your rights and understanding the negotiation process is important. Step 1: Review the Settlement Offer
When you receive a low settlement offer, the first step is to read it carefully, considering several key factors. Look for coverage of your medical bills, lost wages, and other expenses related to your injury, as well as the timing of the offer, as a quick response may indicate the insurer's desire to settle before you've fully assessed your situation.
Ensure you understand what the offer includes, seek clarification from the insurer if necessary, and take your time with this review, as rushing to accept an offer can lead to future financial struggles. Step 2: Gather Supporting Documentation
If you believe the settlement offer is too low, start gathering evidence that supports your claim. This documentation may include: Medical records and bills
Police reports (if applicable)
Photos of the accident scene and injuries
Proof of lost wages
Witness statements
Having strong documentation can help counter the insurer's claim that your injuries or damages are less severe than stated. Step 3: Get a Professional Evaluation
If you're unsure about a settlement offer, consider consulting an experienced NJ injury attorney , like from Rosengard Law Group, located at 496 Kings Highway North Suite 220B Cherry Hill, NJ 08034 , who can provide valuable insights and offer free consultations. They can help you assess your claim, calculate both economic and non-economic damages, and understand your rights, ensuring you don't settle for less than you deserve.
Approximately 91% of individuals with an experienced personal injury attorney receive a settlement payout, compared to only about 51% of those without legal representation. An injury attorney can advocate on your behalf, negotiate with the insurance company, and take legal action if necessary. Get a Professional Evaluation Step 4: Respond to the Offer
Once you've reviewed the offer and gathered documentation, it's time to respond by drafting a written counteroffer that includes the amount you believe fairly compensates you for your injuries, referencing the evidence you've collected to justify your request. When communicating, remain calm and professional, expressing gratitude for their offer while explaining why you believe it's insufficient.
Use clear, straightforward language to ensure the adjuster understands your position, setting the stage for negotiation and demonstrating your commitment to receiving fair compensation. Step 6: Consider Legal Action
If negotiations with the insurance company stall, consider legal action to protect your rights and secure compensation. Filing a lawsuit can serve as leverage, prompting the insurer to reconsider. Consult an experienced attorney to guide you through the process. According to a study by the Insurance Research Council , injury victims who hired attorneys received settlements 3.5 times larger than those who settled on their own.
Be aware of your state's statute of limitations, as waiting too long can jeopardize your case. Taking legal action is a serious step, but may be necessary to ensure justice. Step 5: Engage in Negotiation
Negotiation is an essential part of dealing with insurance companies, requiring a strategic approach to achieve a fair outcome. To navigate this process effectively, be prepared to compromise, understanding that negotiation often involves both parties giving a little, while still holding firm on what you believe is fair.
Additionally, stay patient, as the negotiation process may take time, and avoid rushing into an agreement, as patience can pay off in the long run. Maintaining open lines of communication with the insurance adjuster is also important, so don't hesitate to ask questions or request more time when needed. Step 7: Don't Accept the First Offer
Never accept the first settlement offer without careful consideration. Insurance companies often rely on desperation or lack of information to secure minimal payouts. Advocate for yourself to ensure adequate compensation. Be cautious of quick settlement agreements, as they often can't be renegotiated later. Have an attorney review any agreement before signing it to ensure it covers all damages.
In a notable New Jersey case, a shopper from Mount Laurel , Winifred Freeman, filed a l awsuit against Walmart after being struck by a heavily loaded restocking cart, resulting in significant injuries. This legal action highlights the importance of not accepting initial settlement offers without thorough consideration and legal consultation. Conclusion
Receiving a low settlement offer from an insurance company can be frustrating, but it's not the end of the road. By following these steps, you can negotiate a better settlement and fight for the compensation you deserve. Remember to stay calm, gather evidence, and consider hiring a personal injury attorney to help you deal with the process. Don't be afraid to stand up for your rights and seek the justice you deserve.

title: The Stronghold jiu-jitsu moves to Liberty Station
author: Dave
description: Family-owned and operated since 2007, The Stronghold jiu-jitsu has found a new home in Liberty Station.
content:
Family-owned and operated since 2007, The Stronghold jiu-jitsu has found a new home in Liberty Station.
Previously at 2176 Chatsworth Blvd., The Stronghold now offers martial arts training for both genders ages 2 and up at 2751 Roosevelt Road, Suite 200, above G3 Kids in Liberty Station.
'We strive to offer high-quality jiu itsu in a family-friendly environment and have recently moved our academy to our beautiful and historical new neighborhood,' said the martial arts training center on its website, thestronghold.com. 'We consider all of our students Stronghold family for life. We're not just an academy; we're a community dedicated to fostering personal growth through martial arts.'
On its website, The Stronghold states its mission is to provide a supportive and empowering environment where individuals of all ages and skill levels can train, learn, and grow both on and off the mats. 'Founded by a team of experienced and dedicated practitioners, Stronghold is committed to excellence in both technique and character development. Whether you're a complete beginner or a seasoned competitor, our world-class instructors are here to help you achieve your goals and unleash your full potential.'
'Everyone has their niche,' noted The Stronghold's co-founder Raquel Regno Cusi, adding 'We've been part of this community (Peninsula) for 18 years now.'
Is one jiu-jitsu center much different from another? 'Always. So much,' answered Regno Cusi. 'Some schools train hard. We're more of a family-friendly, train-for-life type of gym. This is a lifelong martial art.'
Regno Cusi discussed the 'coolest' thing about The Stronghold. 'We've graduated two generations now,' she said. 'So a lot of those kids that started with us when they were ages 3 to 5, now come back and coach for us.'
Stronghold's co-founder noted their business co-leases space from G3 Kids downstairs in their barracks building. G3 is a children's active learning academy offering parties, gymnastics classes, after-school programs, and more. 'Everyone knows G3,' noted Regno Cusi pointing out, 'I feel every family should swim, do gymnastics or wrestling or jiu-jitsu, self-defense; that's what every kid should do.'
For Regno Cusi and her family, jiu-jitsu is more than just a business: It's a generational lifestyle. 'We start at age 2 now,' she said adding, 'I've had several students who've now brought their children to me.'
About Liberty Station, Regno Cusi said: 'It's such an untapped thing for Point Loma families – everything is here. It feels like this is perfect for us, all the history. The trade-offs have been good.'
The Stronghold offers a free group class or private lesson for prospective members. For more information, call 858-722-0942.
THE STRONGHOLD
Where: 2751 Roosevelt Road, Suite 200
Info: thestrongholdsd.com, 858-722-0942
Hours: Mondays-Fridays 10 a.m.-6 p.m. Saturday 10 a.m. to noon.
Jiu-jitsu is a family of Japanese martial arts and a system of close combat that can be used defensively or offensively against one or more weaponless or armed and armored opponents. Certain styles of jiu-jitsu were used to develop many modern martial arts and combat sports such as judo, aikido, sambo, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and mixed martial arts.
Because striking against armored opponents proved ineffective, practitioners learned that the most efficient methods for neutralizing an enemy took the form of pins, joint locks, and throws. These techniques were developed around the principle of using an attacker's energy against them, rather than directly opposing it.
There are many variations of the art leading to a diversity of approaches. Jiu-jitsu schools may utilize all forms of grappling techniques – throwing, takedowns, leg sweeps, trapping, pins, joint locks, holds, choke holds, striking, etc. – to some degree. Jiu-jitsu, like karate, has colored belts distinguishing achievement levels as practitioners advance. Today, jiu-jitsu is practiced in both traditional self-defense-oriented and modern sports forms. title: What to Know About Asbestos Trust Funds Before Filing a Claim
author: Graphics Tech
description: Asbestos trust funds have become the best solution for those tested with asb
content:
Asbestos trust funds have become the best solution for those tested with asbestos-related conditions. Bankrupt companies established these accounts to compensate people exposed to asbestos-containing products. However, before filing a claim, victims must understand how the funds work and how much to expect. Below is a comprehensive guide to help victims navigate the process.
Who is Eligible for the Funds
These accounts were created mainly to support those exposed to asbestos or suffering from any illness. However, victims must meet specific requirements to qualify for payment. For instance, they must have a confirmed mesothelioma case or any other related disease, like lung cancer. The medical report must also come from a qualified doctor to be valid.
Providing exposure history and proper documentation can solidify the case and hold the company responsible. Victims must provide sufficient evidence that the exposure was linked to a company listed under the fund. They should also provide work history documents, union records, or affidavits to prove exposure to hazardous products . Each fund has its timeframe, meaning victims must file a claim within a specific period to qualify. Testing and filing a case as soon as possible is crucial to ensure qualification.
What is the Average Payout
The maximum payout varies depending on various factors. These include the severity of the illness and the percentage set by the fund's trustees. For instance, victims diagnosed with mesothelioma typically receive higher compensation than other related conditions. On average, victims can get over $400,000 in total payouts for a mesothelioma claim, although it is lower than a lawsuit that can give an average of $1.4 million in settlement.
Most trust funds do not pay full claim amounts to victims. Instead, they pay a certain percentage of the value to preserve money for future claims. Victims can maximize their payout percentages by working with experienced Mesothelioma Lawyer Nevada , who will negotiate for them based on other factors such as exposure duration and medical expenses. Filing claims with multiple trust funds and asbestos lawsuits can also help victims maximize their settlements.
How to File a Claim
Filing a trust fund claim involves five key steps, each playing a vital role in influencing the outcome. Understanding these steps before preparing a claim is essential in increasing the payout percentage and expediting the process. The process starts with gathering the necessary documents and evidence. These include medical records, employment history, witness statements, and any other records proving exposure to asbestos. The victim then identifies eligible asbestos trust funds and researches if the company is among the bankrupt asbestos companies.
Once the victim has adequate evidence and a responsible company, they can submit their claim. They can do this through expedited or individual review. An expedited review leads to a faster payout, although the victim has to accept the standardized amount. On the other hand, individual review takes longer but may result in higher compensation. After submitting the claim, victims can wait for the administrators to review and verify their eligibility. If the claim is denied or ends in a lower offer, the claimant can appeal the decision with additional evidence.
Endnote
Trust funds offer critical financial support to patients suffering from asbestos-related illnesses or their families. However, qualifying and getting the payout requires claimants to verify their claims with sufficient evidence. Consulting an experienced attorney is vital to ensure victims gather the necessary records and increase their chances of a successful claim.

SCCG was selected by Epic Gardening as a demonstration garden for its Birdie Beds and high-quality seeds from Botanical Interests, which the company acquired in 2023.
Kris Moriarty, d irector of Customer Experience & Special Projects for Epic Gardening, was instrumental in creating this partnership with SCCG. 'We're happy to announce our partnership with the San Carlos Community Garden,' said Moriarty. 'Together we're cultivating a greener, healthier community by providing resources, education, and support to inspire gardeners of all levels. At Epic Gardening, we exist to help you grow, and this collaboration allows us to extend that vision locally.'
' We are always looking for ways to give back to our gardeners and the community,' said Gayle Mills, co-chair of SCCG Board of Directors. 'Our partnership with Epic Gardening is more than we could have ever imagined and will be a great resource to our current and future gardeners.'
Chia-Ming Ro, owner of coastalhomestead.com and one of Epic Gardening's content curators, has helped create a gardening plan for Epic Gardening's plot at SCCG.
' You might not realize it, but it's still winter and that means it's still a great time to plant and grow winter veggies,' said Ro. 'In the weeks ahead, we'll be planting (from seed), plants that are also good for transitioning into spring. So, lot's of veggies like radishes, carrots, leafy greens and Asian greens like Swiss chard, Bok Choy, and Fennel. We'll also plant flowers to attract pollinators and help with pest control; and since it's bare-root season, we'll add some blueberries too.' Scott Sherman.
' It's hard to beat the knowledge we'll gain by having such great access to Epic Gardening and their team, but we're also fortunate to have experienced gardeners, like Scott Sherman, who has been with us for many growing seasons and has built quite the reputation for his peppers, turnips, and cauliflower,' said Mills. 'And, I hear he makes a mean cauliflower mac and cheese.'
Sherman, a resident of Allied Gardens, has been a member of SCCG since leasing his plot in 2013.
' I've seen SCCG grow from its humble beginnings into the jewel it has become,' said Sherman. 'I really like the life lessons gardening teaches to children. It teaches them about planting seeds, caring for seedlings, nurturing and growing the seedlings into mature plants and how and when to harvest the results. But it really teaches them that with hard work and patience and perseverance you can literally enjoy the fruits of your labors.'
Eliana and Bryce Newall, of East Lake, joined the garden in December 2024.
' We live in a home with no yard and have been growing what we can from pots on our small patio, which can be challenging, especially for growing larger produce. We've always wanted to join a community garden and discovered SCCG by my sister who lives close by. We attended SCCG's Produce Swap a few times and were really impressed with all the friendly people involved, and all the neat programs that they offer, said Eliana. Eliana & Bryce Newell's plot. (Courtesy photos)
In just a few months, Eliana and Bryce have produced a beautiful bounty of organic veggies including c abbage, c auliflower, and b roccoli. 'Now I'm ready to lease a second plot and start growing carrots,' said Eliana. 'And, I can't wait to attend yoga in the garden.'
' Not only is it a fantastic place to grow organic, healthy, fresh produce; it's also a great spot to meet and engage with your neighbors,' added Sherman. 'I highly recommend people come and visit SCCG and become part of our community. You'll be glad you did.'
Learn more about the SCCG at: sancarloscommunitygarden.com.
Top photo: The Epic Gardening team at the site of their soon to be SCCG demonstration garden (Left to right): Paul Ruiz, Chia Ming Ro, Ian Ware Tags: San Carlos Community Garden

title: 5 Benefits of Using a Full-Mouth Toothbrush
author: Graphics Tech
description: A full-mouth toothbrush, also known as a mouthpiece toothbrush, represents a significant evolution in dental care technology. Designed to clean all teeth simultaneously, this device encloses the…
content:
A full-mouth toothbrush, also known as a mouthpiece toothbrush, represents a significant evolution in dental care technology. Designed to clean all teeth simultaneously, this device encloses the entire dental arch within its structure, providing a comprehensive clean with each use. Unlike traditional toothbrushes, which require manual manipulation to reach different areas of the mouth, the full-mouth toothbrush offers a uniform application of pressure and cleaning capability, ensuring no tooth is left behind. Time-Saving Efficiency Simultaneous Cleaning of All Teeth
The time-saving toothbrush fundamentally changes the game by cleaning all teeth at once, eliminating the need to individually scrub each tooth. This is particularly advantageous for those who find morning routines to be hectic. It ensures that every surface of the tooth gets attention within seconds, significantly reducing overall brushing time compared to conventional methods. Ideal for Busy Lifestyles
For individuals with demanding schedules, the best U shaped toothbrush for adults offers a practical solution to maintain oral health without compromising on thoroughness. This toothbrush caters to those who value efficiency, allowing more time for breakfast, family, or squeezing in an extra few minutes of sleep. Comparison with Traditional Brushing Time
Typically, dental professionals recommend brushing for at least two minutes with traditional toothbrushes, a duration that many find difficult to consistently fulfill. In contrast, a full-mouth toothbrush can deliver cleaning in about 30 seconds. Such efficiency doesn't sacrifice quality; it maintains high cleaning standards by ensuring that every part of the mouth receives equal treatment during the brushing process. Consistent and Thorough Cleaning Even Bristle Distribution Across Teeth
Engineered to distribute its bristles evenly across each tooth's surface, this design feature ensures that the pressures and cleaning agents are uniformly applied, promoting optimal plaque removal and reducing the likelihood of developing cavities. Uniform bristle distribution is critical for achieving a consistent clean, which traditional brushes may not provide due to uneven manual strokes. Reducing the Risk of Missed Spots
One of the main challenges with standard toothbrushing techniques is ensuring that all areas of the mouth receive adequate attention, particularly the hard-to-reach back teeth and interdental spaces. The whole mouth toothbrush excels in this aspect by covering the entirety of both the upper and lower teeth rows simultaneously. Impact on Overall Oral Hygiene
Providing a thorough cleaning every time helps prevent the buildup of plaque and tartar, which are the primary causes of gum disease and tooth decay. The comprehensive brushing action ensures that all surfaces are well-cared for, promoting healthier gums and cleaner teeth, which can reduce the frequency of dental problems over time. Improved Oral Hygiene with Smart Technology Real-Time Adjustments
The most immediate benefit of using a toothbrush with apps is the ability to make real-time adjustments while brushing. The companion app monitors how the brush is being used—tracking movements, pressure, and duration. If the user applies too much pressure or misses certain areas, the app alerts them instantly. This feedback helps protect against gum damage from over-brushing and ensures that every part of the mouth receives adequate attention. It's an interactive way to learn and apply the best brushing techniques, effectively reducing the risk of dental issues caused by improper brushing. Progress Tracking
A connected toothbrush not only helps in improving daily brushing habits but also offers comprehensive progress tracking. The app records each session and provides visual feedback that shows changes and trends over time. Users can see how their brushing technique has evolved from day to day or over longer periods, like weeks and months. This can be particularly motivating, as tangible improvements in oral health hygiene, such as reduced plaque levels and healthier gums, are highlighted. Tailored Brushing Plans
Smart toothbrush apps optimize dental care by crafting personalized brushing plans based on individual brushing habits and problem areas. These plans focus on: Custom Targets: These apps meticulously analyze your brushing patterns to pinpoint zones within your mouth that are particularly vulnerable to dental issues like plaque buildup or early signs of gingivitis. By identifying these specific areas, the app can guide you to concentrate your brushing efforts on these trouble spots, ensuring they receive adequate attention during each brushing session. A targeted approach not only helps in maintaining optimal oral hygiene but also in preventing the progression of potential dental problems that could lead to more serious conditions if left unattended.
Adaptive Strategies: As your brushing technique improves and your oral health needs evolve, the app adjusts your personalized brushing plan accordingly. This dynamic adjustment is crucial as it ensures that the brushing strategy remains effective over time, catering to any new dental issues that may arise or changes in your oral health status. For instance, if the initial focus was on mitigating gingivitis but your condition improves, the app might shift focus to maintaining gum health and preventing plaque redevelopment.
Improved Dental Health: By addressing the specific dental concerns of each user, they play a pivotal role in enhancing overall dental health. This is achieved through a combination of targeted cleaning that prevents common dental issues and adaptive strategies that evolve with the user's changing needs. Regular use of such apps leads to better plaque control, reduced incidence of gum disease, and an overall improvement in oral hygiene.
These features make smart toothbrush apps a transformative tool in the realm of dental hygiene, providing users with a sophisticated method to boost their oral health based on scientific analysis and tailored feedback. Enhanced Accessibility and Ease of Use Simplified Brushing for Those With Limited Dexterity
This is particularly beneficial for individuals with limited hand dexterity, such as those suffering from arthritis or other conditions that impair movement. Its design minimizes the need for gripping and precise movements required by traditional toothbrushes. Instead, users can easily place the device in their mouth and activate it, allowing for effective cleaning without the strain or discomfort typically associated with manual brushing. Ergonomic Design
Ergonomics plays a crucial role in the full-mouth toothbrush advantages. The device is shaped to fit comfortably in the mouth, reducing jaw fatigue and the discomfort that can come from holding a brush in an awkward position for extended periods. The design consideration ensures that brushing is a comfortable experience for all users, particularly enhancing usability for children, the elderly, and those with physical disabilities. Portability and Convenience Travel-Friendly Design Features
When preparing for travel, choosing accessories that simplify the journey without compromising functionality is essential. A well-designed travel toothbrush can make all the difference in maintaining daily routines while away from home. Here are two key features: Compact Size : The ingenious design of this toothbrush prioritizes convenience without sacrificing usability. Its compact dimensions allow it to slip effortlessly into any nook of a suitcase, backpack, or handbag. The strategic design ensures it consumes minimal space, making it as unobtrusive as possible in your travel setup. Lightweight : This toothbrush is not only small in size but also exceptionally light, crafted from materials that reduce its weight to almost negligible. The lightweight nature is crucial for travelers who are sensitive to the overall weight of their luggage, especially when airline restrictions come into play. By minimizing its weight, the toothbrush allows for more flexibility in packing other essentials or souvenirs without worrying about exceeding weight limits. It's an ideal attribute that enhances the overall travel experience, ensuring that essentials can be carried without burden.
The travel-friendly full-mouth toothbrush integrates seamlessly into the lifestyle of a modern traveler. By focusing on compactness, lightness, and efficiency, it addresses common travel concerns such as space, weight, and the ability to maintain personal care standards. Models for Easy Storage
Many models are designed to be disassembled or come with protective cases that keep the brush sanitary when not in use. This functionality is particularly useful for those living in tight spaces or looking to minimize clutter in their personal care items.
Investing in full-mouth toothbrush benefits is not just about upgrading your dental care tool; it's about enhancing your overall quality of life. This advanced toothbrush simplifies the brushing process, guarantees a comprehensive cleaning, and adapts to your personal oral health needs through innovative features. Whether you are looking to save time, improve your dental health, or need a reliable solution that accommodates physical limitations, the full-mouth toothbrush stands as a wise choice.

content:
Scuderie Italia, at 1525 Garnet Ave., is revving up lunchtime in Pacific Beach with the launch of its new lunch menu, now available from noon to 4 p.m. Mondays through Fridays. The Italian ristorante offers a midday pit stop for guests to fuel up on Italian favorites like Panuozzos, pasta, Peroni, and more. Scuderie's lunch menu will include four Panuozzo and salad combos, each priced at $15.
The combos feature an arugula salad with shaved Parmigiano, cherry tomatoes, and balsamic dressing, paired with a choice of an authentic Italian pizza sandwich, such as the Salsiccia e Friarielli (above), made with sausage, broccoli, and provola cheese; the vegetarian-friendly Norma, crafted with eggplant, tomato, and provola cheese; the Polpette e Scamorza, made with meatballs, provola cheese, and basil; and the Caprese, with buffalo mozzarella, prosciutto, basil, tomatoes, and balsamic dressing.
Another standout is The Italian Job, featuring USDA prime ground beef, provola cheese, caramelized onion, spicy mayo, and arugula, served on Puccia bread and paired with a Peroni beer for $18.
Pasta lovers looking to set the pace can choose from a pack of flavorful frontrunners including Pasta al Forno of the Day, a rotating baked pasta special, served with a choice of one glass of beer, wine or soda, priced at $19; and the pasta, drink, and salad combination, featuring a customizable 'A Modo Mio' pasta with a choice of pasta shape and sauce, along with a fresh salad and a choice of one glass of beer, wine, or soda for $24.
Insalata Scuderie, a vibrant arugula salad with shaved Parmigiano, cherry tomatoes, balsamic, and spicy aioli, is also available with chicken for $17 or salmon for $19.

title: Gather and Grow Speech Therapy ‘a place of joy and connection'
author: Dave
description: Home and offi
content:
Home and office are the same for speech-language pathologist and communication coach Susanne Creighton.
Creighton lives in North Pacific Beach near Kate Sessions Elementary. She said working from her home office in her business named Gather and Grow Speech Therapy gives her clients 'a place where they're willing to connect and be in a space with like-minded individuals.' She added that ultimately creates 'a place of joy and connection with each other.'
Creighton noted people drop off their kids at her home, or adults drive over. 'I'm lucky to have different spaces in my home where we can work outside, or move inside,' she said pointing out, 'Often with kids, treatment is play- and activity-based.'
Possessing a master's degree in communication science and disorders from SDSU, Creighton notes she treats people at 'all ages and stages,' but her clientele tends to be composed more of children or young adults.
And there are a myriad of speech conditions out there to be treated. 'If young adults have problems with accent modification and speech fluency or articulation, or older adults have 'weak' voice or a neurogenetic disorder – we work on that,' said Creighton who was employed for 20 years in public schools before going into private practice. She also helps people pick up English as a second or third language.
What's the key to working with someone with speech difficulties? 'There is no one model,' replied Creighton adding, 'Everything has to very much be tailored to the individual. You have to play to their strengths and their interests. The idea is always to empower someone.'
Creighton added it is also essential to address speech problems as soon as possible. 'Early intervention is big, critical, especially if the kid is going to be on a path to something like autism (a neurological and developmental disorder affecting how people interact with others, communicate, learn, and behave),' she said.
Creighton noted it's important to 'celebrate the wins along the way,' in helping people overcome their speech difficulties. But she added it's most important to her for her clients to get to where they feel like 'they've got the skills and feel good about their speaking ability.'
As one example, Creighton recently treated a 74-year-old woman for a weak voice. She said her client told her, 'It's (voice) killing me in social situations.'
The speech difficulties Creighton helps people overcome aren't always overt. She said, 'I tell them, 'If you want to achieve relaxation and feel more at ease when you're speaking, and have less anxiety, I can help you with that.'
The speech pathologist talked about one dream she'd like to become a reality. 'One of my visions is to create this day camp, which would be more nurturing for kids providing them with a play-based environment where they could play board games or go nature hiking.'
The company's website is presently under construction. For more information, email [email protected] .

title: Anne Ledford Evans, hotel owner and tourism leader, dies at 92
description: Anne Ledford Evans died peacefully at home, surrounded by her family, on Feb 12. Anne contributed mightily to the world around her, whether that community was her family, her circle of friends, a…
content:
Anne Ledford Evans died peacefully at home, surrounded by her family, on Feb 12 . Anne contributed mightily to the world around her, whether that community was her family, her circle of friends, a charitable or business organization, the San Diego region, the s tate of California, or the nation. She was a model of leadership and volunteerism, a pioneering businesswoman, and a respected tourism and civic leader.
As someone with a deep love of San Diego and a desire to improve the region for the benefit of all who call it home, Anne held numerous leadership positions with organizations in a wide variety of areas, from tourism and economic development to education, philanthropy, and public service. Her famous sense of humor and warm demeanor made her a memorable presence equally at home around the family dinner table, in the board room, or at the podium of a charity event.
A second-generation San Diegan, Anne was born at Mercy Hospital to Dr. Roy Merl Ledford and the former Herma Lucille Johns. She grew up in North Park and Point Loma with her parents and siblings, Roy Merl Ledford, Jr., and Lucille Clarice Ledford.
Anne's independence, magnetic personality, and leadership skills were evident at an early age. At 16, she graduated from Point Loma High School and attended Pomona College, where she served as junior class president before graduating in 1953. She then moved to San Francisco to work for Macy's as the assistant manager for women's handbags, umbrellas, and walking sticks.
She met her future husband, William D. 'Bill' Evans, while in college. After Bill completed his service in the United States Marine Corps and United States Navy, they reconnected and were married in 1954.
In those early years, the Mission Bay that people know today – the picturesque landscape defined by waving palm trees, water sports, and white sand beaches – was a vision few people could have imagined in the 1950s. Before becoming the nation's largest 'aquatic playground,' it was then a smelly and squalid marsh. When the City of San Diego offered several parcels up for bid and expected multiple offers, there was only one bidder. Seeing the potential and willing to take on the risk, Anne and Bill were awarded the first long-term lease on Mission Bay for the land that would eventually become the Bahia Resort Hotel. Starting with just 52 rooms, the Bahia is the longest-standing lessee of the City of San Diego.
Anne and Bill later created the Catamaran Resort Hotel and Spa in 1959 and developed numerous other commercial properties in Southern California.
During most of those years, Anne was primarily a homemaker, raising five children and providing volunteer services to numerous charitable organizations and political activities. As a noteworthy and sought-after event organizer, she chaired the Charity Ball benefiting Children's Hospital and numerous political fundraisers, most notably for Pete Wilson, beginning with his time as m ayor of San Diego and spanning over his entire career. During that time, she was active in Republican politics, especially in support of g overnor and later President Ronald Reagan, serving as c o- c hair for the 1984 Reagan-Bush Committee for San Diego County and serving as a delegate to the 1984 Republican National Convention.
Over nearly 30 years, Anne and Bill raised their children, grew their business, and shared a love of community. As the love of Anne's life, Bill's sudden passing in 1984 was a devastating loss.
While many encouraged her to leave Evans Hotels behind, Anne was determined to carry on and honor her late husband's vision of the important role tourism could play in San Diego's economic development. She was also always acutely aware of the opportunities provided to the company's dedicated workforce.
Long before it was popular, she believed her primary responsibility as a business owner was to care for her team members. As she was fond of saying, 'I don't just run a business; I am responsible for 1,200 families.'
She worked tirelessly to market San Diego and Mission Bay because growing occupancy meant more hours for employees; she provided medical benefits before it was common, including the earliest domestic partner benefits; and she encouraged and celebrated the diversity of the workforce. The company welcomed and promoted women, people of color, and LGBT individuals from its earliest years, resulting in today's team, where half their managers are diverse.
Under her leadership, the company embarked on a multi-year plan to redevelop the family's hotel properties and expand its hospitality products. This began with the construction of a reproduction Mississippi-style sternwheeler in 1985, which was christened the William D. Evans in honor of her late husband.
In 1995, the Evans family acquired a property on the Torrey Pines Golf Courses in La Jolla that became The Lodge at Torrey Pines. Following an extensive redevelopment in 2002, the resort achieved a AAA Five-Diamond ranking in its opening year and has maintained it for the last 22 years.
In addition to building and running her business, Anne was an active civic volunteer. She went on to become one of the first women to serve on a variety of distinguished boards, often in leadership. She joined the San Diego Chamber of Commerce and eventually became only the third woman chair in its 100- plus year history. She also served as c hair of the San Diego Convention and Visitors Bureau (now the San Diego Tourism Authority) and was on the e xecutive c ommittee of the San Diego Regional Economic Development Corporation. She was a founding director of the California State Tourism Commission (now Visit California) and served on the California Chamber of Commerce board.
Always a supporter of the benefits of education, she served as a t rustee of her alma mater, Pomona College, on the Founders Circle of the Preuss School, as a c ommissioner for the UC San Diego Foundation, and on the advisory board of its Rady School of Management. She supported other important San Diego institutions as a t rustee of the Scripps Clinic and Research Foundation, member of the Director's Cabinet of Scripps Institution of Oceanography, and d irector of the Hubbs-SeaWorld Research Institute.
In addition, she was always willing to serve the public when asked, leading her to serve as San Diego's c hief of p rotocol under Mayor Maureen O'Connor, who was herself the first woman to hold that position. Anne was later especially honored by her appointment by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to serve as a d irector of the Los Angeles Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, which she went on to chair.
In all of those roles, she was a fierce advocate for the tourism industry and its important role in the economic development of the region and state. She consistently reminded anyone and everyone about the importance of the tourism industry to the regional and s tate economy as well as touting the size and importance of San Diego in matters of statewide concern. Anne was fond of saying that 'tourism is the industry of peace.'
Her business acumen was recognized by being asked to serve on numerous corporate boards as well, including San Diego Trust and Savings Bank, Price Enterprises, and the Automobile Club of Southern California, where she was honored as d irector e meritus upon her retirement from board service. She received the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Corporate Directors Forum for this service.
Throughout her career, Anne has been recognized for her leadership and community contributions. Locally, she was named the Hotelperson of the Year by the San Diego Hotel-Motel Association, a 'Courageous Leader' by the San Diego Regional Chamber of Commerce and was honored with the San Diego Pioneering Woman Award from the Catfish Club. Her lifetime of dedication to the region has been recognizes with the Neil Morgan Memorial Award for Lifetime Achievement from the San Diego Regional Chamber of Commerce, the Herb Klein Civic Leadership Award from the San Diego Regional Economic Development Corporation, the Lifetime Achievement Award in the Women Who Mean Business Awards from the San Diego Business Journal and the F. Norman Clark Entrepreneur of the Year Award from the California Travel Industry Association.
She has been inducted into the Visitor Industry Hall of Fame by the San Diego Convention and Visitors Bureau (now the San Diego Tourism Authority), San Diego Business Hall of Fame by Junior Achievement of San Diego, and California Tourism Hall of Fame. She was inducted into the California Women's Museum Hall of Fame in 2024 and called out as a San Diego i con by the San Diego Business Journal.
Anne's family-run business is rooted in the belief that her hotels are both 'of the community' and 'for the community.' This was never evidenced more than during the Covid pandemic when all Evans Hotels remained open to provide discounted hotel accommodations to frontline health workers in San Diego's vital healthcare sector.
Anne's free time was spent enjoying musical theatre, tending to her rose garden, and caring for her dogs. She loved taking in the least adoptable dogs and giving them the best life possible, usually several at a time.
Anne is predeceased by her parents, siblings, husband, and many dear friends. She is survived by her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren as well as many friends, current and former employees, and community members whose lives she touched.
A celebration of life will be held at a date to be determined in the spring at the Bahia Resort Hotel. In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to Rady Children's Hospital San Diego or Baja Animal Sanctuary.

title: UC San Diego clinical trial: Family-based treatment best for obese children
author: Dave
description: A new UC San Diego clinical trial finds self-guided family-based treatment for obese children is easier, more affordable, and as effective as traditional, clinician-led approaches. FBT is a clinically proven approach to treating children with obesity where a healthcare professional works with families to help their children lose weight by…
content:
A new UC San Diego clinical trial finds self-guided family-based treatment for obese children is easier, more affordable, and as effective as traditional, clinician-led approaches.
FBT is a clinically proven approach to treating children with obesity where a healthcare professional works with families to help their children lose weight by promoting physical activity, encouraging healthy eating habits, and teaching age-appropriate behavioral skills.
UC San Diego's Center for Healthy Eating and Activity Research has found that self-guided FBT is also more flexible than more traditional models with scheduling and costs significantly less, as well as requiring fewer contact hours with a provider.
'Traditional FBT is an effective treatment method but can be time-intensive, can only be offered at specific times, and is expensive, which makes families facing difficult financial circumstances less likely to seek treatment,' said senior study author Kerri Boutelle, Ph.D., director of CHEAR and professor in the Departments of Pediatrics and Psychiatry at UC San Diego School of Medicine and the UC San Diego Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science. 'By providing the same core skills as traditional FBT in a more flexible and condensed format, we can increase access to treatment for families who may not be able to participate in traditional group-based programs.' Kerri Boutelle, Ph.D., director of CHEAR and professor in the Departments of Pediatrics and Psychiatry at UC San Diego School of Medicine.
Boutelle pointed out childhood obesity is 'incredibly complex' with numerous dietary, physical, genetic, and environmental factors contributing to the condition. 'Each body is different regarding all the factors influencing how much they eat, whether they can resist bad habits, all of those things,' she said adding treatment therefore has to be individually customized.
But unlike adult obesity, which is often managed individually, helping children lose weight effectively has proven to be a family-based effort. Boutelle noted more traditional EBT treatments are done in small groups of parents with their 8- to 15-year-old children, allowing participants to 'support each other.'
But there's a catch to that method. 'That treatment is 26 hours over six months, and requires a lot of time and space as well as skilled clinical interventions,' Boutelle said. 'The self-help FBT treatment model we've developed has the same information, but takes only five hours of treatment in six months, without interventions, during 20-minute sessions every other week.'
Added Boutelle: 'Previous studies suggest outcomes are improved with more contact hours. But we're finding that the most important thing is working with parents, which can be done without a trained clinician. While some families may benefit from the standard approach, providing more flexible and accessible alternatives like self-guided FBT can help us make a wider impact on the epidemic of childhood obesity.'
Studies show about one in five U.S. children have obesity, which is associated with numerous negative health outcomes in children. Those include an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and asthma. Obesity in children is also associated with mental health concerns such as depression, anxiety, low self-esteem, and social isolation.
There is another benefit to self-help FBT for treating childhood obesity. 'The treatment can be provided without someone being specially trained,' Boutelle said. 'And it can be provided in a medical office where they (physicians) can see patients every other week. We hope that this information can be disseminated to the public through healthcare providers, health educators, and nurse practitioners. There is no reason to make people come in for treatment that much. It can be done just as effectively, more individually, and in a lot less time.'
To learn more about pediatric obesity treatment studies and other CHEAR research visit https://chear.ucsd.edu/.
CHILDHOOD OBESITY
There are multiple contributing factors to the condition including:
Diet: Consuming high-calorie, nutrient-poor foods (e.g., sugary drinks, processed foods, fast food).
Eating large portions.
Infrequent consumption of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
Physical Activity: Lack of regular physical activity.
Spending excessive time watching TV, playing video games, or using electronic devices.
Genetics: Certain genes may increase a child's susceptibility to weight gain.
Environment: Easy access to unhealthy foods, limited opportunities for physical activity, and social norms that promote sedentary lifestyles.

title: SDFC falls to Portland in second game of tournament
description: San Diego FC dropped its second match of the Coachella Valley Invitational after a 3-0 defeat to the Portland Timbers on Wednesday afternoon. SDFC forward Chucky Lozano was not in the starting lineup after having played 64 minutes in the previous game versus NYCFC, but he did come in the…
content:
San Diego FC dropped its second match of the Coachella Valley Invitational after a 3-0 defeat to the Portland Timbers on Wednesday afternoon. SDFC forward Chucky Lozano was not in the starting lineup after having played 64 minutes in the previous game versus NYCFC, but he did come in the 61st minute with the team trailing 1-0 on a 16th-minute goal by striker Felipe Mora.
Just like the match on Saturday, San Diego FC managed to create some scoring chances in the first half including one in the 43rd minute on a left-footed shot from just outside the box by midfielder Onni Valakari. Forward Emmanuel Boateng had a chance to tie the game in the 47th minute, but his angled shot from 8 yards away went just wide.
Lozano being subbed in was a shot in the arm to the offense with the Mexican striker almost finding the back of the net in the 62nd minute and then again in the 73rd minute with a shot that hit the post.
Portland ended up putting the game away thanks to two late breakaway goals from forward Gage Guerra with the first coming in the 81st minute and the other in the 84th minute off a pass by teammate Tommy McNamara.
The most controversial play of the match came in the 88th minute when SDFC defender Franco Negri was taken down inside the box by midfielder Malcolm Johnston with no whistle being blown. Negri grabbed his leg as he fell to the ground and was able to make his way to the sideline writhing in pain. Negri's teammates came to his defense after some pushing and shoving instigated by Portland had ensued with the referee nowhere in sight with no yellow cards or warnings of any kind being issued.
San Diego FC wraps up the tournament on Saturday against the New York Red Bulls.
GRADES
Goalkeeping: C+
Nothing could be done on those final two scores from Guerra, which turned into one vs. one breakaway opportunities for Portland.
Defending: C-
Even though they gave up one more goal than they did versus NYCFC, the team was pretty solid for about 80 minutes and looked better catching Portland on the offside trap several times.
Midfield: B-
The team was more cohesive and efficient with crisp passing and ball retention during large parts of the match.
Attacking: B
Despite being shut out this time, there were more quality chances to score than in the game against NYCFC. The final touch failed them this time, plus the post was not their friend.
Refereeing: F
It's funny how a pretty respectable performance can go out the window on one play, but that is exactly the case here with a blown no-call that was not only a clear penalty but a potential red card. What followed were the actions of someone clearly in over his head and not knowing how to get a match back under control once the players had to come to the defense of their teammate as the opponent saw there would be zero consequences.
