title: Building Blocks of Dependability: Essential Components for Reliable Industrial Wireless Communications
description: Wireless communication has become indispensable for optimizing operations, enhancing productivity, and ensuring safety in industrial environments. From remote monitoring and control to asset tracking…
content:
Wireless communication has become indispensable for optimizing operations, enhancing productivity, and ensuring safety in industrial environments. From remote monitoring and control to asset tracking and predictive maintenance, industrial wireless communication systems play a crucial role in facilitating real-time data exchange and decision-making.
However, achieving reliable wireless communication in industrial settings requires careful planning and deployment of essential components. This article will explore the key components that form the foundation of reliable industrial wireless communications.
1. Robust Wireless Infrastructure At the core of reliable industrial wireless communications is a robust wireless infrastructure comprising access points, routers, and antennas. Access points serve as the central hubs for connecting wireless devices to the network, while routers facilitate data transmission between devices and the central control system.
It's essential to choose industrial-grade access points and routers designed to withstand harsh environmental conditions and operate reliably in industrial settings. Additionally, selecting the right antennas for optimal signal coverage and range is crucial for ensuring consistent wireless connectivity throughout the facility.
2. Industrial-Grade Wireless Devices Industrial wireless devices, such as sensors, actuators, and controllers, form the endpoints of the wireless communication network. These devices gather data from sensors, control actuators, and interface with industrial equipment to enable various automation and monitoring tasks.
When selecting wireless devices for industrial applications, it's essential to choose industrial-grade models specifically designed for rugged environments. These devices should be resistant to temperature extremes, moisture, dust, and electromagnetic interference to ensure reliable performance in challenging conditions.
3. Redundant Networking Infrastructure To enhance reliability and fault tolerance, industrial wireless communication systems often incorporate redundant networking infrastructure. Redundancy can take various forms, including redundant access points, routers, and communication paths.
Redundant components ensure continuity of communication in the event of equipment failure, signal interference, or network congestion. By implementing redundant networking infrastructure, industrial facilities can minimize downtime, maintain productivity, and ensure uninterrupted communication for critical applications.
4. Advanced Security Measures Security is a paramount concern in industrial wireless communications, as unauthorized access or malicious interference can pose significant risks to operations and safety. Implementing advanced security measures such as encryption, authentication, and access control is essential for protecting wireless communication networks from cyber threats.
Industrial wireless communication systems should adhere to industry standards and best practices for network security, including encryption protocols such as WPA2-Enterprise and authentication mechanisms such as 802.1X.
5. Quality of Service (QoS) Mechanisms In industrial environments where real-time communication is critical, Quality of Service (QoS) mechanisms play a vital role in prioritizing traffic and ensuring timely delivery of data packets. QoS mechanisms prioritize high-priority traffic, such as control signals and alarm notifications, over low-priority traffic, such as non-time-sensitive data transmissions.
By implementing QoS mechanisms, industrial wireless communication systems can guarantee the performance and reliability of mission-critical applications, even in congested or bandwidth-limited environments.
6. Interference Mitigation Techniques Industrial environments are often characterized by high levels of electromagnetic interference (EMI) from machinery, equipment, and nearby wireless devices. Interference can degrade signal quality and reliability, leading to communication errors and packet loss.
Implementing interference mitigation techniques such as frequency hopping, channel bonding, and adaptive modulation can help minimize the impact of EMI on wireless communication systems.
Additionally, deploying industrial wireless devices with robust error correction mechanisms can help compensate for signal degradation and ensure reliable communication in noisy environments.
7. Comprehensive Monitoring and Management Tools Effective monitoring and management are essential for maintaining the performance and reliability of industrial wireless communication systems. Comprehensive monitoring tools enable administrators to track network performance, identify potential issues, and troubleshoot problems in real-time.
Management tools provide centralized control and configuration of wireless devices, allowing administrators to optimize network settings, update firmware, and implement security policies efficiently. By leveraging monitoring and management tools, industrial facilities can proactively identify and address issues before they impact operations and ensure the ongoing reliability of wireless communication systems.
Building Reliable Industrial Wireless Networks Reliable industrial wireless communications require careful consideration and deployment of essential components, including robust wireless infrastructure, industrial-grade devices, redundant networking infrastructure, advanced security measures, Quality of Service mechanisms, interference mitigation techniques, and comprehensive monitoring and management tools.
By integrating these components into their wireless communication systems, industrial facilities can achieve high levels of reliability, performance, and security, enabling them to optimize operations, enhance productivity, and maintain a competitive edge in today's dynamic industrial landscape.

title: The Impact of Drought on Plumbing and Water Usage in the East Bay Area
description: The East Bay Area faces persistent drought conditions. The drought's grip on the region also challenges the area's plumbing infrastructure. As water scarcity intensifies, residents and businesses must…
content:
The East Bay Area faces persistent drought conditions. The drought's grip on the region also challenges the area's plumbing infrastructure. As water scarcity intensifies, residents and businesses must adapt their daily water usage habits. The cascading effects of this drought strain local resources and underscore the pressing need for sustainable solutions to mitigate its impact on the community.
Understanding the Drought Situation in the East Bay Area The severe drought conditions in the East Bay are made worse by various factors, including climate change and historical water management practices. Decreased precipitation levels and rising temperatures have diminished water supplies in reservoirs and groundwater aquifers, challenging the sustainability of water resources. Outdated water management practices, such as inefficient irrigation methods and reliance on imported water sources, strain local water systems. Recognizing the factors contributing to the drought is crucial for mitigating its effects on plumbing infrastructure and promoting sustainable water usage practices within the community.
Effects of Drought on Plumbing Systems A prolonged drought strains plumbing systems within homes and buildings across the East Bay Area. Decreased water availability often reduces water pressure, affecting everyday tasks like showering and dishwashing. Water scarcity can increase pipe corrosion, leading to leaks and potential structural damage. With drought, tree roots become thirsty and seek water by invading pipes. In response, residents must heighten their awareness and adopt water conservation measures to preserve the integrity of plumbing infrastructure and the region's precious water resources.
Water Conservation Measures for Homeowners Homeowners can conserve water by taking these proactive measures:
Install low-flow fixtures such as aerators and showerheads to reduce water usage during daily activities. Regularly check for and promptly repair leaks in faucets, toilets, and irrigation systems to avoid wasting water. Use efficient irrigation techniques, such as drip irrigation or watering during cooler parts of the day, to minimize evaporation. Replace older appliances with water-efficient models, such as dishwashers and washing machines, with Energy Star ratings. Incorporate native and drought-tolerant plants in landscaping to reduce the need for excessive watering. Collect rainwater in barrels or tanks for outdoor uses, such as watering gardens or washing vehicles. Practice mindful water usage habits, such as turning off the tap while brushing teeth or scrubbing dishes, to conserve water during daily routines. By adopting these practices, you can help conserve water, minimize your impact on the water supply, and reduce damage to the plumbing infrastructure.
Impact of Drought on Water Usage Habits The impact of drought on water usage habits in the East Bay Area has prompted significant shifts in behavior among residents and businesses. Individuals have adopted more mindful and conservative practices, such as taking shorter showers, limiting outdoor water usage, and refraining from unnecessary water-intensive activities. This heightened awareness of water conservation has permeated various aspects of daily life, leading to increased vigilance in monitoring and reducing water consumption.
Role of Plumbing Professionals in Drought Mitigation Plumbing professionals play a crucial role in helping homeowners and businesses adapt to the challenges posed by drought conditions. Through their expertise, they facilitate the implementation of water-efficient solutions tailored to each property's specific needs. This includes installing and optimizing water-efficient fixtures to minimize consumption, promptly detecting and repairing leaks to prevent waste, and conducting comprehensive evaluations of plumbing systems to identify areas for improvement. Plumbing professionals contribute significantly to drought mitigation efforts by offering specialized services and guidance.
Government Initiatives and Regulations Government initiatives and regulations address the pressing drought issues within the East Bay Area. Implemented measures aim to encourage water conservation and sustainable usage practices among residents and businesses. This includes offering water rebates to incentivize the adoption of water-efficient appliances and fixtures and imposing restrictions on outdoor water usage to curtail excessive irrigation. Government agencies provide incentives for property owners to invest in upgrades that enhance water efficiency, such as rainwater harvesting systems or drought-resistant landscaping. Through these proactive measures, authorities strive to mitigate the impact of drought while fostering a culture of environmental responsibility within the community.
Community Engagement and Education Community engagement and education are fundamental in the collective effort toward effective drought mitigation strategies. By fostering awareness and understanding among residents, these initiatives empower individuals to take proactive steps in conserving water resources. Workshops and outreach programs provide valuable platforms for sharing practical tips and best practices for water conservation and facilitate open dialogue and collaboration within the community. Online resources offer accessible information and tools to support ongoing education efforts, enabling individuals to stay informed and engaged in sustainable water usage practices.
Future Outlook and Long-Term Solutions As the East Bay Area grapples with persistent drought conditions, the future outlook underscores the imperative for implementing long-term solutions to ensure water sustainability and resilience. The region must prioritize investments in innovative technologies and infrastructure upgrades to mitigate the impact of drought on water supply and usage. This includes expanding water recycling initiatives, modernizing aging plumbing systems, and adopting comprehensive sustainable water management practices. By proactively addressing the root causes of water scarcity and embracing forward-thinking approaches, the East Bay Area can chart a path toward a more resilient and sustainable future.
Final Thoughts The impact of drought on plumbing and water usage in the East Bay Area underscores the critical need for concerted action and collaboration. Through water conservation measures, the expertise of plumbing professionals, and community engagement efforts, residents and businesses can adapt to the challenges of water scarcity. By prioritizing sustainable practices, investing in modern infrastructure, and fostering a culture of environmental stewardship, the region can navigate the complexities of drought while safeguarding its precious water resources for future generations. Together, these collective efforts exemplify the resilience and commitment of the East Bay Area community in mitigating the impact of drought on plumbing and water usage to bring about a more sustainable and secure future.

title: Mission Bay girls lacrosse ends impressive season
description: The Mission Bay girls lacrosse team closed out a remarkable season on May 10 that saw them finish on top of the league standings (9-1).
content:
The Mission Bay girls lacrosse team closed out a remarkable season on May 10 that saw them finish on top of the league standings (9-1). After winning the regular-season opener versus Del Lago Academy on Feb. 21, the Bucs dropped the next three matches to Point Loma, El Capitan, and University City before turning things around by going on a six-game win streak.
'We saw how much growing we needed to do pretty early in the season with a ton of new players,' said head coach Hayley Burke. 'I was proud of the team this year.'
With only three returning seniors, Mission Bay went from finishing with only a couple of wins in 2023 to an 11-5 overall record this season while only having three seniors on the squad before falling to Castle Park in the playoff quarterfinals.
Among the team's standout performers was goalie Sydney Kidd, who, despite being injured the majority of the season, stayed involved and returned in time for the final matches. Midfielder Iris Brogan and teammate Richie Lynn Nguyen stepped up big when they were called upon to impact offense and defense.
'The girls ultimately bought in and impacted how the season ended,' Burke added. 'I feel like having a tough season last year, our learned lesson was setting small goals and just taking it day by day. I'm sad to lose the seniors, but I'm pretty excited to have a ton of returners next year to pick up where we left off.'
Mission Bay outscored its opponents 164 to 116 during the regular season, which included back-to-back shutouts over Lincoln on March 18 and Hilltop on March 23 by a combined scoreline of 35-0 along with a forfeit victory over Preuss UCSD on April 29.
'Once we learned we had a chance of making the playoffs, we set a bigger goal of going for league champion and making it as far as we could,' said Burke.

The La Mesa-Spring Valley School District (LMSV) recently received significant affirmation of its efforts to engage its families thanks to a ‘Community Schools' grant worth just over $17 million. The five-year grant was awarded by California's State Department of Education (CDE) and is part of an ambitious initiative to turn thousands of state schools into ‘Community Schools'. The funds will help LMSV provide wrap-around services for students and families that increase support beyond school instruction. title: Cabrillo Under the Stars sells out and raises funds for CNMF
author: Dave
description: Cabrillo Under the Stars, the annual fundraiser benefiting Cabrillo National Monument held Saturday, May 18 inside and outside the monument, was a sellout and a huge success.
content:
Cabrillo Under the Stars, the annual fundraiser benefiting Cabrillo National Monument held Saturday, May 18 inside and outside the monument, was a sellout and a huge success.
Guests at the 21-plus event got to experience first-hand San Diego's only national park at night during this once-a-year event while supporting one of the area's natural and historic treasures.
'This year's event featured Gilbert Castellanos and some of San Diego's finest jazz musicians from the Young Lion's Jazz Conservatory, which were one of the highlights of the evening,' said Emily M. Moore, Cabrillo National Monument Foundation's executive director. 'It is metaphoric having the Young Lions play this event since part of Cabrillo National Monument Foundation's goal is to help connect future generations to the park. That is truly the purpose of this event, to increase awareness and raise funding so we can continue to support the programs and projects that preserve Cabrillo National Monument for future generations.'
Added Moore: 'I feel like we succeeded in bringing in new members from Point Loma, the greater San Diego community, and even from as far away as Minnesota and Washington, D.C., who had previously not been engaged with Cabrillo National Monument, as well as many of our existing donors, some of whom have been supporting the foundation for 10, 15, 20, even 30 years. Marrying these groups of people in a larger effort to support the foundation … Yes, our event was a great success.'
Perched on the tip of Point Loma, soiree guests delighted in a variety of tasty fare and tastings from local brewers and vintners while enjoying lively music under the stars. Attendees also interacted with park rangers, sponsors, and donors about ways they can help make an impact to continue park discovery, youth education, and volunteer support programs at Cabrillo National Monument.
Noting Cabrillo National Monument Foundation is the official nonprofit partner of Cabrillo National Monument. The group's mission is to inspire people to support programs that preserve the rich cultural and natural treasures and enhance the visitor experience at Cabrillo National Monument.
For more information about the funding Cabrillo National Monument Foundation provides to the park and becoming a foundation member, visit cnmf.org.

title: Bali Hai serves its three millionth mai-tai … and counting
author: Dave
description: The milestone cocktail was served at the Polynesian eatery at 22
content:
The milestone cocktail was served at the Polynesian eatery at 2230 Shelter Island Drive, known for its seafood, bay views, and ultra-potent mai tais, on Monday, May 20.
With a bar full of expectant regulars looking on, a guest identified as Sean, walked in and ordered the rum-based cocktail while sitting next to Bali Hai's two millionth mai-tai cocktail winners from 16 years prior, Amy Wyte and Ted Harris. Those two were also contending to become the three millionth mai tai drinkers at Bali Hai, which has operated since 1954.
'We rang in his order and boom, Sean was sipping on the three millionth mai tai,' noted Bali Hai's ownership. Sean's prize was a new Tiki mug, a $1,000 Bali Hai gift card, and exclusive membership in the restaurant's unofficial mai-tai hall of fame.
There is an interesting tale concerning how Bali Hai created – and earned – its well-deserved reputation for being the mai tai capital of San Diego. Restaurant general manager Tommy Baumann related how Bali Hai's 'ticker,' which keeps a running tally of how many mai tai's have been sold, originated.
Pointing out he is part of his family's third generation owning and operating Bali Hai and Tom Ham's Lighthouse, Baumann said his grandfather, a public accountant, was the one who got them into the restaurant business.
'He was very much a numbers person into sales trends, etc.,' said Baumann. 'In the early 2000s, my older brother, another numbers person interested in menu items and drinks sold, was running Bali Hai. It was my older brother who went back to the early '60s (tabulating mai tais sold).'
'Given that we took over the Bali Hai in 1954, my brother figured we were well into more than a million mai tais sold,' continued Baumann. 'My brother installed an analog ticker, like a stock ticker, over the bar to count them (mai tais) – and it's still there today. It reads, ‘World Famous Mai Tais' and gives the year to date on how many have been sold.'
Sean, winner of the three millionth mai tai, Tommy Baumann, owner and GM of Bali Hai, Ted Harris and Amy Wyte, the couple who won the two millionth Mai Tai 16 years ago. Baumann added, that as Bali Hai approached its two millionth mai tai sold in the spring of 2008, there was a definite 'buzz' among clientele in the bar, small then accommodating only about a dozen guests, in anticipating the serving of mai tai No. 2 million. On a Sunday, Wyte and Harris ate some appetizers and shared Bali Hai's two millionth mai tai served. Both have remained regulars who are 'like family,' said Baumann.
Characterizing a mai tai as 'a phenomenal drink bridging generations,' Baumann pointed out, 'We have had grandmothers bringing in their grandchildren to get a mai tai for their 21st birthdays. It's become a part of the fabric of Bali Hai. It's a world-renowned drink.'
Baumann added that it also didn't hurt that mai tais fit in '100%' with Bali Hai's tropical Polynesian theme.
Given that Bali Hai's ticker indicates patrons consume approximately 70,000 mai tais annually, Baumann calculated an ETA on when the restaurant's four millionth trademark cocktail will be served. 'Hopefully, we're having this conversation in about 12 years,' he concluded adding, 'I would be ecstatic (just) to have been in business that long (82 years).'
BALI HAI MAI TAI
BALI HAI MAI TAI ½ oz Sweet and Sour Mix (or ¼ oz Lemon Juice and ¼ oz Simple Syrup). ¼ oz Orgeat. ¼ oz Triple Sec. 2½ oz Cruzan Light Rum. 2½ oz Coruba Dark Jamaican Rum.
Shake with ice.
MAI TAI'S ORIGIN
MAI TAI'S ORIGIN The history of the mai tai, a tropical rum-based cocktail, is disputed, but Victor Jules Bergeron, also known as Trader Vic, is generally credited with its creation. In 1944, Bergeron, a bartender at his Tiki-themed restaurant in Oakland, served the drink to two friends from Tahiti. After tasting it, one of his friends exclaimed 'Mai tai-roa aé,' translating as 'out of this world – the best!' Bergeron then named and created the drink. He introduced the mai tai to Hawaii and added juices to create the Royal Hawaiian mai tai, which became the islands' unofficial drink.

title: When Is the Best Time for Seawall Repair?
description: Seawalls are crucial structures that protect coastal properties, infrastructure, and ecosystems from the erosive forces of waves and tides. Over time, seawalls can deteriorate due to constant exposure…
content:
Seawalls are crucial structures that protect coastal properties, infrastructure, and ecosystems from the erosive forces of waves and tides. Over time, seawalls can deteriorate due to constant exposure to saltwater, weather conditions, and natural wear and tear.
Regular maintenance and timely repairs are essential to ensure the integrity and effectiveness of seawalls in safeguarding coastal areas. But when is the best time for seawall repair? This article will explore the factors to consider and the optimal timing for seawall repair to maximize effectiveness and minimize costs.
Understanding the Importance of Seawall Repair Before delving into the best timing for seawall repair, it's essential to understand why maintaining these structures is crucial. Seawalls play a critical role in protecting coastal properties, infrastructure, and ecosystems from erosion, flooding, and storm surges.
When damaged or compromised, seawalls can fail to provide adequate protection, leading to property damage, shoreline erosion, and environmental degradation. Timely repairs help maintain the structural integrity of seawalls, prolong their lifespan, and ensure their effectiveness in mitigating coastal hazards.
Factors Influencing the Timing of Seawall Repair Several factors influence the timing of seawall repair, including:
1. Severity of Damage The extent and severity of damage to the seawall will impact the urgency of repairs. Minor cracks or erosion may not require immediate attention, while significant structural damage or breaches in the seawall may necessitate immediate repairs to prevent further deterioration and protect coastal assets.
2. Seasonal Weather Patterns Seasonal weather patterns, such as hurricanes, tropical storms, or periods of heavy rainfall, can exacerbate erosion and accelerate seawall damage. Planning repairs during periods of calm weather or low tides can facilitate safe and efficient repair work while minimizing risks to workers and equipment.
3. Tidal Patterns Tidal fluctuations can affect access to the seawall and the feasibility of repair work. Timing repairs to coincide with low tides or slack water periods allows for easier access to the seawall and reduces the risk of working in hazardous conditions caused by strong currents or wave action.
4. Permitting Requirements Seawall repair projects like in Bayset may require permits from regulatory agencies, such as local governments or environmental authorities. Understanding and complying with permitting requirements can influence the timing of repair work and ensure that necessary approvals are obtained before commencement.
Best Times for Seawall Repair While the timing of seawall repair may vary depending on specific circumstances, several optimal times for undertaking repair work include:
1. Off-Season or Low-Tide Periods Planning seawall repairs during the off-season or low-tide periods can minimize disruptions to coastal activities and reduce the risk of damage from wave action or tidal surges. Off-peak periods also allow contractors to schedule repairs more efficiently and may result in cost savings for property owners.
2. Early Detection of Damage Early detection of seawall damage allows property owners to address issues promptly before they escalate into more significant problems. Regular inspections and maintenance can help identify minor cracks, erosion, or structural weaknesses early on, enabling timely repairs to prevent further deterioration.
3. Post-Storm Assessments Following severe weather events, such as hurricanes or tropical storms, conducting post-storm assessments of seawall conditions is crucial. Identifying and addressing storm-related damage promptly can help prevent additional erosion, stabilize the shoreline, and protect coastal properties from future storm surges.
4. Scheduled Maintenance Implementing a proactive maintenance schedule for seawalls can help prevent damage and prolong their lifespan. Scheduled maintenance activities, such as cleaning, regrading, and reinforcing vulnerable sections, should be conducted regularly to ensure the structural integrity of the seawall and identify any repair needs early on.
Strategizing Seawall Repair for Optimal Efficiency and Effectiveness The best time for seawall repair depends on various factors, including the severity of damage, seasonal weather patterns, tidal fluctuations, and permitting requirements. Planning repairs during off-peak periods, low-tide windows, or the off-season can facilitate safe and efficient repair work while minimizing disruptions to coastal activities.
Early detection of damage through regular inspections and proactive maintenance is essential for addressing issues promptly and preventing further deterioration. By prioritizing timely repairs and proactive maintenance, property owners can ensure the effectiveness and longevity of seawalls in protecting coastal areas from erosion and storm damage.

title: Pointers receive No. 1 seed in CIF Div. II playoffs
description: After a successful march through a grueling Western League schedule, Point Loma's Pointer baseball team is the No. 1 seed in CIF Div. II playoffs, a seeding that avoids a "play-in" game in the double-elimination march to a championship.
content:
After a successful march through a grueling Western League schedule, Point Loma's Pointer baseball team is the No. 1 seed in CIF Div. II playoffs, a seeding that avoids a 'play-in' game in the double-elimination march to a championship.
That No. 1 seeding also makes it likely the Pointers will play all games leading to the finals on their home field unless their opponent is a league champion. They are 10-2-3 on David Wells Field, In fact, the Pointers began their quest earlier this week when they hosted the winner of the play-in game between No. 8 Mt. Carmel and No. 9 Scripps Ranch. If they win that game they will play again on May 17 at home with the first pitch at 3:30 p.m.
During the 10-day period of the playoffs, the Pointers could play as many as six games, which places a premium on the depth of each team in the division. During the season, most teams used the same two starting pitchers when playing only on Wednesdays and Fridays. But the playoff schedule will place a strain on the pitching depth of each team.
For the Pointers, those two starters have been senior Will Sanford and junior Matthew Garrison, both of whom have been outstanding.
For Oregon-bound Sanford, his numbers are 52.1 innings pitched, a 1.20 ERA, an opponents' batting average of .111, with 28 walks and 98 strikeouts.
Garrison's numbers include 55.1 innings pitched, a 1.14 ERA, an opponents' batting average of .156, 22 walks, and 67 strikeouts.
But others such as seniors Liam Cannavino, Kai Dickinson, Brayden Taylor, and juniors Druw Frost, Marvel Underwood, and Luis Lara will be taking the mound and be counted on to keep the Pointers in games.
The Pointers finished the regular season with a 14-8-4 record (.610 win percentage), a significant improvement over last season's 14-17-1 (.453) and last-place league finish.
Offensively, the Pointers are hitting .240 as a team and have averaged 4.2 runs per game but have struggled at times getting runners on base or bringing them home. They did win three home league games, however, by 1-0 scores, evidence of great pitching and defense.
Mentally, the team has possibly never been better, a testament to the positivity, leadership, preparation, and example set by new head coach Rigo Ledezma, who is constantly teaching, supporting, and giving signals to his players. The players, in turn, have responded with attention, hustle, and support of each other.
St. Augustine finished atop the challenging Western League with a record of 7-3, however, two of those losses were to the Pointers, who knocked the Saints from atop local rankings. The only team the Pointers didn't defeat was Patrick Henry when, after the teams fought to a scoreless tie at home after nine innings, the game was called for darkness. Four Pointer games (and two league games) ended this way with scores of 0-0, 1-1, 2-2, and 8-8, all in extra innings.
If the Pointers had won the two tied league games they would have shared first place with the Saints.
The final regular season game was literally a blast for the Pointers when they hosted Christian last Friday for the 'Senior Day' celebration. The Patriots had beaten them 6-1 in El Cajon last Wednesday but the Pointers weren't about to let them spoil the rematch.
First, it was senior shortstop Eli Montgomery who launched a home run, a ball that cleared the high fence in left field. Later it was fellow senior Griffin Ice who blasted a ball in nearly the same area. But to his surprise, Ice came up later and hit another high and deep home run. Each player totaled three RBIs in the game.
The Pointers scored five runs in the second inning to open up a big lead that became a 9-0 whipping.
Other RBIs went to Dickinson and junior second baseman Adrian Gomez. Garrison threw five innings of one-hit ball with Frost and Taylor closing the game.
Parents, siblings, and relatives came onto the field following the game as players lingered for more photos and celebrating.
Now, it's on to the postseason.
EXTRA INNINGS
Parents of underclassmen organized a wonderful 'Senior Day' celebration for the team's nine graduating players and their families. Mothers received flowers and each player walked to home plate with family members for a photo. Memories written by the seniors were read along with future plans as underclassmen cheered them on from the dugout.
The annual banquet for all players (70) and families in the program is scheduled for June 3 on the spacious open area at Shelter Island's Bali Hai restaurant. Each team, including freshmen and junior varsity, will be honored.
Three Pointer seniors have younger brothers in the program. Matthew Cleator (brother Ryan),
Ice (brother Owen) and Dickinson (brother Koa).

title: Savoring Every Sip: How to Ensure Your Wine Delivery Arrives Safely
description: Ordering wine online offers unparalleled convenience, allowing you to access a vast selection of wines from the comfort of your home. However, ensuring that your wine delivery arrives safely is…
content:
Ordering wine online offers unparalleled convenience, allowing you to access a vast selection of wines from the comfort of your home. However, ensuring that your wine delivery arrives safely is crucial to preserving the quality and enjoyment of your purchase.
From choosing the right delivery service to taking precautions during transit, there are several steps you can take to ensure a smooth and secure delivery. Here's how to ensure your wine delivery arrives safely:
1. Choose a Reliable Delivery Service When ordering wine online, it's essential to choose a reliable and reputable delivery service with experience in handling fragile and perishable items. Look for delivery services that specialize in wine shipping or have a proven track record of safely delivering wines. Research customer reviews and ratings to gauge the reliability and satisfaction levels of different delivery providers.
2. Check Shipping Policies and Options Before placing your wine order, review the shipping policies and options offered by the online retailer or winery. Look for information on shipping rates, delivery times, and packaging practices.
Some retailers offer expedited shipping options or temperature-controlled shipping for an additional fee, which may be worth considering, especially during extreme weather conditions.
Opt for Temperature-Controlled Shipping Temperature fluctuations during transit can affect the quality and taste of your wines, particularly if they are exposed to high temperatures for an extended period. To ensure that your wine delivery arrives in optimal condition, opt for temperature-controlled shipping when available.
Temperature-controlled shipping helps to protect wines from heat damage during transit, ensuring that they arrive safely and ready to be enjoyed.
4. Provide Accurate Delivery Information To avoid delivery delays or issues, provide accurate delivery information when placing your order. Double-check the shipping address, contact information, and delivery instructions to ensure that your wines are delivered to the correct location and can be received by someone of legal drinking age. Clear and accurate delivery information helps to facilitate smooth and efficient delivery logistics.
5. Schedule Delivery for a Convenient Time When scheduling your wine delivery, choose a delivery time that is convenient for you or someone who can receive the package on your behalf. Avoid scheduling deliveries during times when no one will be available to accept the package, as this increases the risk of theft or damage. Many delivery services offer flexible delivery options, including evening or weekend delivery slots, to accommodate your schedule.
6. Track Your Shipment Take advantage of shipment tracking services offered by the delivery provider or online retailer to monitor the progress of your wine delivery in real-time. Tracking allows you to stay informed about the status of your shipment, including estimated delivery times and any updates or delays along the way. By tracking your shipment, you can anticipate its arrival and make necessary arrangements to receive it promptly.
7. Inspect the Package Upon Arrival When your wine delivery arrives, take the time to inspect the package for any signs of damage or tampering before accepting it. Look for visible damage to the outer packaging, such as dents, tears, or punctures, which may indicate mishandling during transit. If the package appears damaged or compromised, refuse delivery and contact the delivery provider or retailer immediately to report the issue.
8. Handle with Care Once you've accepted the wine delivery, handle the packages with care to avoid damaging the contents. Avoid dropping or shaking the packages, and store them in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight or heat sources until you're ready to unpack them. Handle bottles gently when removing them from the packaging to prevent breakage or spillage.
9. Store Wines Properly After unpacking your wine delivery, store the bottles properly to maintain their quality and freshness. Store wines in a cool, dark, and humidity-controlled environment, such as a wine cellar, wine fridge, or closet away from temperature fluctuations and light exposure. Keep bottles lying horizontally to keep the corks moist and prevent oxidation.
10. Enjoy Responsibly Once your wine delivery has arrived safely and been properly stored, it's time to sit back, relax, and enjoy your favorite wines responsibly. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion, hosting a dinner party, or simply unwinding after a long day, savor each sip and appreciate the convenience of having your favorite wines delivered directly to your doorstep.
Safeguarding Your Wine Delivery Experience Ensuring that your wine delivery arrives safely requires careful planning, attention to detail, and cooperation with reliable delivery providers. By choosing a reputable delivery service, inspecting the package upon arrival, handling with care, storing wines properly, and enjoying it responsibly, you can enjoy the convenience of wine delivery while preserving the quality and enjoyment of your wines.

title: Memorial Day schedule for City of San Diego offices and services
description: On Monday, May 27, City of San Diego administrative offices and other services will be closed for the Memorial Day holiday. The following is a guide to which services are impacted by the holiday…
content:
On Monday, May 27, City of San Diego administrative offices and other services will be closed for the Memorial Day holiday. The following is a guide to which services are impacted by the holiday closures and those still operating on a normal schedule. Regular operations will resume on Tuesday, May 28.
WHAT'S CLOSED (IMPACTED BY HOLIDAY CLOSURES):
All City of San Diego administrative offices.
Miramar Landfill, Greenery, Recycling Center, Mattress Collection Site and Container Sales (trash, recycling and organic waste bins).
Curbside trash, recyclables and organic waste (food scraps and yard trimmings) will not be collected for customers served by the City's Environmental Services Department (ESD) on Monday, May 27. Monday's normally scheduled collection will occur on Tuesday, May 28; Tuesday's collection will take place on Wednesday and so on. Residents not serviced by ESD should check with their waste hauler for holiday service schedules.
All City libraries.
City swimming pools and recreation centers.
Public buildings in Balboa Park, including the Municipal Gym, Morley Field and Balboa Park Activity Center. Check with individual museums and other park attractions for their holiday schedules.
Tecolote Canyon Nature Center.
Parks and Recreation Department Open Space, Permit Center and Maintenance Assessment District offices.
Development Services Department in-person services. Online services will still be available, including applying for permits, scheduling inspections, making payments and requesting code enforcement investigations. Check online permit processing timelines for intake, review and permit issuance.
Personnel Department's Testing and Fingerprinting offices will be closed on May 27.
Your Safe Place – A Family Justice Center. Individuals needing help related to domestic violence should call the Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-888-385-4657. Anyone experiencing immediate danger or a medical emergency should dial 9-1-1. Additional information can be found on the San Diego Police Department's domestic violence webpage.
WHAT'S OPEN (NORMAL OPERATING SCHEDULE):
All City reservoirs except Barrett will be open. PARKING IMPACTS
Parking meters, time restrictions for parking on streets, yellow zones and posted street sweeping routes under the City of San Diego's jurisdiction will not be enforced. All other parking violations will be enforced. Parking rules on Port of San Diego property and in different cities may vary. Please read posted signage.

title: The Role of Evidence in Car Accident Claims: How to Build a Strong Case
author: Grhics Tech

content:
Car accidents can be traumatic and chaotic, leaving victims to navigate the complexities of recovery and compensation. Building a strong case to secure the compensation you deserve hinges on gathering and presenting robust proof. Personal injury attorneys play a crucial role in this process, utilizing their expertise to compile and leverage evidence effectively.
Types of Evidence Needed in Car Accident Claims
1. Police Reports
1. Police Reports Police reports are foundational pieces of evidence that a dedicated car accident attorney uses in road mishap claims. They provide an objective account of the incident, including:
Police reports are foundational pieces of evidence that a dedicated car accident attorney uses in road mishap claims. They provide an objective account of the incident, including: Details of the Crash: Date, time, location, and conditions.
Date, time, location, and conditions. Involved Parties: Names, contact information, and insurance details.
Names, contact information, and insurance details. Initial Findings: Preliminary determination of fault, citations issued, and witness statements. 2. Medical Records
2. Medical Records Medical records document the injuries sustained in the mishap and the treatment received. These records are crucial for proving the extent and impact of injuries. Here, they are:
Medical records document the injuries sustained in the mishap and the treatment received. These records are crucial for proving the extent and impact of injuries. Here, they are: Initial Medical Evaluation: Diagnoses and treatment immediately following the accident.
Diagnoses and treatment immediately following the accident. Ongoing Treatment: Records of follow-up appointments, surgeries, physical therapy, and prescriptions.
Records of follow-up appointments, surgeries, physical therapy, and prescriptions. Expert Testimonies: Statements from medical professionals regarding the severity and long-term impact of injuries. 3. Witness Statements
3. Witness Statements Witness statements provide additional perspectives on the accident. They can include:
Witness statements provide additional perspectives on the accident. They can include: Eyewitnesses: Individuals who saw the crash occur.
Individuals who saw the crash occur. First Responders: Police officers, paramedics, and firefighters at the scene.
Police officers, paramedics, and firefighters at the scene. Experts: Accident reconstruction specialists and other experts who can offer technical insights. 4. Photographic and Video Evidence
4. Photographic and Video Evidence Visual evidence can be compelling in illustrating the circumstances of the accident and the extent of the damage. This might be:
Visual evidence can be compelling in illustrating the circumstances of the accident and the extent of the damage. This might be: Photos of the Scene: Images capturing the vehicles, road conditions, traffic signals, and skid marks.
Images capturing the vehicles, road conditions, traffic signals, and skid marks. Videos: Dashcam footage, security camera recordings, or bystander videos. 5. Documentation of Expenses and Losses
5. Documentation of Expenses and Losses Accurate records of all expenses related to the accident are essential for substantiating claims. These documents include the following:
Medical Bills: Invoices for hospital stays, treatments, and medications.
Invoices for hospital stays, treatments, and medications. Repair Bills: Costs for vehicle repairs or replacement.
Costs for vehicle repairs or replacement. Lost Wages: Documentation of time missed from work and the corresponding loss of income. Types of Evidence
Types of Evidence Description
Description Police Reports
Official record of the accident details and initial fault assessment
Medical Records
Documentation of injuries and treatment
Witness Statements
Accounts from those who saw the mishap or were involved in its aftermath
Photographic/Video Evidence
Visual proof of the accident scene and damages
Documentation of Expenses
Records of all financial costs related to the crash
How Personal Injury Attorneys Gather Evidence and Utilize It
How Personal Injury Attorneys Gather Evidence and Utilize It Personal injury attorneys are adept at collecting and organizing evidence to build a compelling case. They often conduct thorough investigations, which involve accident reconstruction by working with experts to recreate the crash scene and determine fault. Additionally, they interview witnesses to obtain detailed statements and gather additional evidence, such as traffic camera footage, 911 call recordings, and other pertinent information.
Lawyers also ensure that all official records are obtained and properly reviewed. This includes requesting police reports to ensure their accuracy and completeness and accessing medical records by collaborating with healthcare providers to gather comprehensive medical documentation.
Experts can provide critical insights and testimony that bolster a case. Attorneys often work with medical experts to clarify the severity and long-term effects of injuries, accident reconstruction specialists to provide a clear and scientific explanation of how the collision occurred, and financial experts to quantify economic losses and future expenses.
Building a Strong Case: Evidence Utilization
Building a Strong Case: Evidence Utilization Once facts are gathered, personal injury attorneys use them strategically to strengthen the client's claim. They demonstrate liability by using proof to establish the at-fault party's negligence. This involves proving the duty of care by showing that the defendant had a legal obligation to act reasonably. They then demonstrate the breach of this duty by detailing how the defendant's actions failed to meet this standard. Next, they establish causation by linking the breach directly to the injuries sustained and documenting the actual losses incurred due to the accident.
In negotiations with insurance companies, attorneys use evidence to negotiate effectively. They present comprehensive facts in a clear and organized manner, counter lowball offers by using strong proof to justify higher compensation demands, and mediate disputes by facilitating discussions between the victim and the insurer to reach a fair settlement.
If a fair settlement cannot be reached, attorneys prepare for trial by organizing all evidence to ensure it is admissible and compelling. They prepare witnesses by coaching them to provide clear and consistent testimony and craft persuasive arguments to develop a narrative that effectively conveys the victim's story and the extent of their losses.

title: Point-in-Time Count results show increase in homelessness
description: The Regional Task Force on Homelessness released the topline data collected from more than 1,700 volunteers spread across San Diego County in January for this year's Point-in-Time Count. The…
content:
The Regional Task Force on Homelessness released the topline data collected from more than 1,700 volunteers spread across San Diego County in January for this year's Point-in-Time Count. The information shows the minimum number of people experiencing homelessness across the region.
Overall, the 2024 Point-in-Time Count found no less than 10,605 people experiencing homelessness across our region. This includes 6,110 unsheltered San Diegans and 4,495 individuals in shelters and transitional housing. This is a 3% increase from the 2023 Point-in-Time Count. In 2023, homelessness across the region was up about 20 percent from the prior year. The 2024 count shows homelessness is a regional issue, with roughly 200 additional people experiencing homelessness in each region of San Diego County.
'While a 3% increase is encouraging, we counted more people in unsheltered conditions across the region. We're seeing a significant increase in people living in their cars. This year's numbers suggest we have a continuing need for more sheltering options and support for the efforts many cities are now taking to combat this crisis,' RTFH CEO Tamera Kohler said. 'We must focus on populations like seniors, veterans, and people living in cars, where proven housing strategies can make a difference in the months and years ahead.'
The 2024 Point-in-Time Count showed an increase in the number of people experiencing unsheltered homelessness, including a 44% increase in individuals and families living in their cars, and a decrease in shelter or other temporary housing options. With the loss of federal emergency funding, including hotel/motel vouchers, and a shift toward safe sleeping and safe parking sites in several communities, RTFH is not surprised by these data points.
It's critical to point out that the Department of Housing and Urban Development defines safe sleeping and safe parking sites as unsheltered homelessness and thus includes them in the unsheltered section of the Point-in-Time Count. In the City of San Diego, for example, 472 individuals were in the safe sleeping sites, and 285 individuals were in the safe parking sites.
RTFH Board Chair Ray Ellis said: 'San Diegans should feel cautious optimism about this data. While we are still seeing too many experiencing homelessness for the first time, our region is making the right kind of investments in critical system infrastructure and programs that make a difference.'
Beyond the topline numbers, vital data collected by Point-in-Time Count volunteers provides deeper insights into what homelessness looks like across our region. Populations that leveled off or decreased from 2023 include seniors (a less than 1% increase) and those found on CalTrans sites (a 10% decrease). 81 percent of individuals counted said they began experiencing homelessness in San Diego County.
The oldest person found experiencing unsheltered homelessness was an 85-year-old Hispanic woman.
'I hope this is the high water mark,' CoC Advisory Board Chair Pastor Rolland Slade said. 'Our board is proud of the work that communities, non-profits, religious groups, and others are embracing. Vista opening up a navigation center, the County increasing funding for RTFH's diversion practice, and Imperial Beach hiring a full-time outreach worker – these actions add up and are crucial to slowing down what has been an accelerated crisis. There's a lot more work to do but this is good progress.'
This year's count also shows the reporting of Hispanic ethnicity along with race, properly conveying the impact of homelessness on San Diego County's Hispanic population.
Data from the Point-in-Time Count is only a part of what RTFH provides to the public to better inform the community about what homelessness looks like in the region. Monthly reports created by the organization, for example, show the region has not seen a month since March, 2022 where more individuals exited homelessness than experienced homelessness for the first time, a 25-month streak. Additionally, from October 2022 to September 2023, our region's homeless response system interacted with more than 46,000 individuals, up from 41,000 the previous year.
'Our biggest challenge remains the sky-high cost of housing across our region,' Kohler said. 'The long-term need for abundant housing for people of all income levels remains apparent. There are still too few units and too much need. Yet I'm heartened by this report. There are interventions for many of the populations we've seen an increase in that can make a real difference.
'Communities across the county, from Vista to National City, San Diego to La Mesa, are leaning into game-changer solutions. If we can keep people housed, quickly end homelessness for those sleeping in their cars, and continue to target vulnerable populations, San Diego has a fighting chance to see real change moving forward.'

Mark your calendars because the East Village Block Party is coming back bigger and better than before! Rescheduled for Saturday, July 13th from 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., the free community celebration promises a fun-filled day celebrating all things East Village and of course, the San Diego Padres! J Street from 7th to 10th a venues will be filled with a wide array of exciting activations and competitions including a walk-through car show, local sports teams including San Diego FC and San Diego Legion , fitness activations, a gaming area, photo opportunities, local vendors and engaging musical entertainment. While dancing through the crowded streets, attendees can shop from a variety of local vendors including clothing and accessories by Wotown Vintage , Apollo + Luna for colorful handcrafted jewelry pieces, Down 2 Ferment for a selection of flavorful hot sauces, and other one-of-a-kind shops. Don't miss out on an unforgettable day supporting the Padres and the neighborhood.

The 2nd Annual Taste of East Village is returning Wednesday, August 28th and Thursday, August 29th from 4 to 8 p.m. Foodies will savor tasty bites and sips from more than 30 of East Village's top culinary gems showcasing the rich culinary tapestry of the neighborhood. Ticketholders will receive a Taste Passport at check-in to use as a guide for mapping out all participating restaurants in the neighborhood and to keep track of their favorite appetizers, entrees, desserts, and beverages.
